steps.instructions: Confirm use of a known-good hospital-grade outlet, inspect the power cord and plug, and look for damage, overheating, discoloration, fluid contamination, or signs of impact.

steps.title: Confirm the Failure Is Not Cleared by an Approved Power Reset
steps.instructions: With the warmer removed from patient use, perform an approved shutdown and restart, then observe whether Sys Fail 11 clears, reappears immediately, or returns intermittently.

steps.title: Inspect Accessible External Control-System Indicators and Condition
steps.instructions: Without opening the device, inspect for blank or frozen display behavior, unresponsive controls, unexpected heater indications, loose external panels, visible damage, moisture, or contamination.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Error Is Persistent
steps.instructions: If the error remains after external power, restart, and visual-condition checks, classify the problem as a persistent internal communication failure involving the Heat Control Processor and Main Application Processor.

steps.title: Escalate for Controlled Bench Evaluation
steps.instructions: Remove the warmer from service and route it for authorized bench evaluation of the ribbon cable between the Power PCA and Control PCA, the Control PCA, and the Power PCA supply path according to service documentation.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: Return the warmer to clinical use only after the identified corrective action is completed and required operational and safety verification confirms reliable heater-control operation.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 11 [XX 00 00 00], indicating loss of communication between the Heat Control Processor and Main Application Processor. Warmer removed from patient use due to unresolved heat-control reliability concern.
CCR.Cause: Confirmed recurring Sys Fail 11 after testing with a known-good outlet and completing an approved restart. No external damage, power-cord defect, or contamination identified. Fault is consistent with an internal processor communication, ribbon-cable, Control PCA, or Power PCA supply-path failure requiring bench evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Removed Panda Warmer from service, applied Out of Service labeling, and routed unit for authorized internal inspection and repair. Device will not be returned to clinical use until the error is corrected and required operational and safety verification is completed.

title: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer Infant Warmer - Error: Sys Fail 02 Heater Power Feedback Mismatch
description: Troubleshooting Sys Fail 02 when heater power feedback does not match commanded output, creating unreliable warming operation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the warmer from patient use. If an infant is being supported, notify clinical staff and transfer the infant to a known-working warming device before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm Sys Fail 02 is displayed and document whether it occurs at startup, when heater output is commanded, during warm-up, or intermittently during operation.

steps.title: Inspect External Condition and Basic Setup
steps.instructions: Inspect the heater assembly, power cord, plug, exterior surfaces, heat engine area, and power source for visible damage, contamination, obstructions, overheating evidence, or unsafe conditions.

steps.title: Confirm the Error Is Not Cleared by a Safe Power Restart
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use and no unsafe physical condition present, perform a normal power restart and determine whether Sys Fail 02 returns.

steps.title: Run the Heat Engine Health Check in Service Mode
steps.instructions: Following approved Clinical Engineering service procedures, run the Heat Engine Health Check and document whether the test passes, fails, or causes Sys Fail 02 to recur.

steps.title: Check Accessible Connections Between the Control PCA and Power PCA
steps.instructions: With the warmer appropriately powered down, inspect accessible Control PCA-to-Power PCA connections for looseness, damage, overheating evidence, harness strain, or contamination. Reseat only according to approved service practices and retest.

steps.title: Check Connections Between the Power PCA and the Heat Engine
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible Power PCA-to-heat engine connections for looseness, damage, discoloration, contamination, or overheating evidence, then repeat the Heat Engine Health Check if a safely addressable issue is corrected.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Issue Has Been Resolved
steps.instructions: Return the warmer to clinical service only after the Heat Engine Health Check passes, Sys Fail 02 does not return, and required return-to-service verification confirms normal heater operation.

CCR.Complaint: Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 02 during operation. Reported heater power did not match commanded heater power, making warming performance unreliable.
CCR.Cause: Heat Engine Health Check failed and Sys Fail 02 persisted after verifying the power source and inspecting accessible connections between the Control PCA, Power PCA, and heat engine. Findings indicate likely Power PCA failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed warmer from clinical service, labeled unit Out of Service, documented failed heater power verification, and routed unit for bench repair and Power PCA evaluation/replacement.

title: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer Infant Warmer - Error: Sys Fail 05 ADC Configuration Error or ADC Failure
description: Troubleshooting Sys Fail 05 when an ADC configuration or reference-channel failure prevents confidence in accurate sensing and reliable warmer control operation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the Panda Warmer from patient use if Sys Fail 05 occurs while supporting an infant or during preparation for care. Notify clinical staff and transfer the infant to a known-working warming device before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: With the warmer removed from patient use, power the unit on and confirm whether Sys Fail 05 is displayed. Document whether the error occurs during startup, self-test, warming operation, or intermittently, along with any abnormal control or heater behavior.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Basic External Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm connection to a known-good hospital-grade outlet. Inspect the power cord, plug, strain relief, and visible power-entry area for damage, looseness, overheating, or contamination.

steps.title: Inspect the Unit for Visible Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the control panel, display, warmer head, column, connectors, and accessible external surfaces for fluid intrusion, impact damage, burn marks, unusual odor, loose connectors, or overheating. Stop testing if unsafe conditions are identified.

steps.title: Confirm That External Accessories Are Not Contributing
steps.instructions: Inspect and disconnect removable external accessories not required to observe the startup fault, following facility procedure. Check accessory connectors and cables for bent pins, contamination, damage, or improper connection, then observe whether Sys Fail 05 remains.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Error Persists After Basic Checks
steps.instructions: After confirming safe power, visible condition, and external accessory status, power the warmer on again while it remains out of patient use. If Sys Fail 05 returns or remains active, stop operational troubleshooting and route the unit for bench evaluation.

steps.title: Escalate for Bench Evaluation or Repair
steps.instructions: Persistent Sys Fail 05 indicates likely internal ADC/reference-channel or Control PCA failure. Qualified service personnel should follow approved procedures to reset NVRAM defaults and replace the Control PCA if the error persists, followed by required verification and safety testing.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 05 during startup and could not be considered reliable for patient warming.
CCR.Cause: Verified stable outlet power and inspected external condition and removable accessory connections. Sys Fail 05 remained reproducible, indicating likely internal ADC/reference-channel or Control PCA failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed warmer from service and labeled Out of Service. Routed unit for qualified bench evaluation, including manufacturer-directed NVRAM default reset and Control PCA replacement if the error persists. Return to service pending successful repair verification and safety testing.

title: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer Infant Warmer - Error: Sys Fail 08 [XX XX 00 00] Shorted or Incorrectly Detected Touch-Panel Button
description: Troubleshooting Sys Fail 08 [XX XX 00 00] when a shorted or incorrectly detected touch-panel button prevents reliable warmer control operation and may require Touch Panel or Control PCA repair.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Panda Warmer is supporting an infant or prepared for immediate clinical use, notify clinical staff and transfer the patient to a known-working warming device before troubleshooting. Do not rely on a warmer with an unresolved touch-panel or control-interface system failure.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: With the warmer removed from patient use, power the unit on and confirm Sys Fail 08 [XX XX 00 00]. Document whether it occurs during startup, Service Mode entry, after a button is touched, or intermittently, and note any stuck or unresponsive controls.

steps.title: Rule Out Incorrect Service Mode Entry
steps.instructions: If the error occurred while attempting to enter Service Mode, confirm that both required Service Mode buttons are depressed during power-on according to the manufacturer procedure. If correct entry clears the error, document the condition and verify normal operation.

steps.title: Inspect the Touch Panel Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect for stuck buttons, damaged overlay material, residue, liquid intrusion, cleaning-product buildup, contamination, or objects pressing against the control panel. Correct or clean only according to approved guidance.

steps.title: Use the Button-Function Diagnostic Test
steps.instructions: If Service Mode can be entered properly, use the approved button-function diagnostic test to determine whether one or more buttons are continuously detected as active without intentional pressing.

steps.title: Check the Touch-Panel Connection
steps.instructions: With the warmer removed from service and following approved electrical safety precautions, inspect the touch-panel connection to the Control PCA for looseness, partial seating, visible damage, contamination, or evidence of liquid exposure. Reseat only when permitted, then repower and retest.

steps.title: Isolate the Touch Panel From the Control Path
steps.instructions: Qualified service personnel should follow the approved service procedure to disconnect the touch-panel connector from the Control PCA and repower the unit. If Sys Fail 08 clears, the Touch Panel is the likely failed component. If it remains, the Control PCA is the likely failed component.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved and Verify Function
steps.instructions: After correction or authorized component replacement, confirm Sys Fail 08 no longer appears during normal startup, touch-panel buttons respond correctly, no inputs remain falsely detected, and required operational and safety checks are completed before returning the warmer to service.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 08 [XX XX 00 00] during startup. Touch-panel button input appeared continuously detected, preventing confidence in normal control-panel operation.
CCR.Cause: Verified correct Service Mode button entry. External obstruction and contamination were not identified. Button-function diagnostics identified a continuously detected touch-panel input. Sys Fail 08 cleared when the touch-panel connector was disconnected from the Control PCA, indicating a failed Touch Panel.
CCR.Resolution: Removed warmer from clinical service, labeled unit Out of Service, and routed for Touch Panel replacement and post-repair operational verification before return to patient use.

title: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer Infant Warmer - Error: Sys Fail 01 [FF XX XX XX] Flash Memory or File System Error
description: Troubleshooting Sys Fail 01 [FF XX XX XX] when a flash memory or file system error prevents reliable warmer startup, control, or safe clinical operation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the Panda Warmer is occupied or needed for immediate patient care, notify clinical staff and transfer the infant to a known-working warming device according to clinical procedure. Do not rely on an infant warmer displaying an unresolved Sys Fail 01 [FF XX XX XX] error for temperature support or monitoring.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: With the unit removed from patient use, power the warmer on and confirm the exact displayed error: Sys Fail 01 [FF XX XX XX]. Document when the error appears, whether startup completes, whether the error is constant or intermittent, and whether display, controls, heater operation, or alarms appear abnormal.

steps.title: Check the Power Source and Basic External Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm that the warmer is connected to an approved, functioning outlet and that the power cord is fully inserted and free of visible damage. When permitted by facility procedure, test the outlet or use a known-working outlet. Inspect for liquid intrusion, contamination, burnt odor, abnormal heat, visible damage, impact, or transport damage.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Power Restart
steps.instructions: After confirming the warmer is not supporting a patient, power the unit off normally, disconnect it from AC power briefly, reconnect it to a verified outlet, and power it back on. Observe whether Sys Fail 01 [FF XX XX XX] returns during startup. If the error clears, complete functional verification according to facility procedure before return to service.

steps.title: Confirm That the Problem Is Not Accessory-Related
steps.instructions: Check for attached external accessories or optional connections. Disconnect only nonessential external accessories as allowed by facility procedure, then restart the warmer again. Do not perform internal disassembly during external troubleshooting.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Error Is Persistent
steps.instructions: If Sys Fail 01 [FF XX XX XX] repeatedly returns after verified power, external inspection, controlled restart, and removal of nonessential external connections, treat the condition as a persistent internal system failure. Document the exact displayed values, timing, and troubleshooting findings.

steps.title: Escalate for Qualified Bench Evaluation
steps.instructions: Remove the warmer from service and route it for qualified repair evaluation. Manufacturer-directed repair action may include reloading applicable software, reprogramming the main application flash, or replacing the Control PCA if the error persists after approved restoration procedures. Return the unit to clinical use only after successful verification.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 01 [FF XX XX XX] during startup and did not complete normal readiness for clinical use.
CCR.Cause: Verified stable external power, intact power cord, no visible contamination or damage, and no accessory-related cause. Error returned after controlled restart, indicating likely internal flash memory, file system, software, or Control PCA failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed Panda Warmer from service, labeled unit Out of Service, and routed for qualified bench evaluation for approved software reload or main application flash reprogramming, with Control PCA replacement if the error persists.

title: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer Infant Warmer - Error: Sys Fail 03 Memory Error Occurred
description: Troubleshooting Sys Fail 03 when a memory error prevents reliable warmer startup, control operation, settings retention, or safe infant warming use.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the Panda Warmer from patient use if Sys Fail 03 is displayed during setup or while supporting an infant. Transfer the patient to a known-working warming device according to clinical procedure before troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: With the unit removed from patient use, confirm that the display shows Sys Fail 03. Document when the error occurs and whether startup failure, unavailable controls, repeated system-failure messages, settings retention issues, alarms, or interrupted heater operation are present.

steps.title: Check Power Source and External Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify the warmer is connected to a known-good, properly grounded outlet. Inspect the power cord, plug, strain relief, and receptacle for damage, looseness, contamination, or overheating. Power-cycle the unit once using the approved startup procedure while it remains off patient use.

steps.title: Inspect the Warmer for External Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect for impact damage, fluid intrusion, heavy contamination, loose external panels, unusual odor, or evidence of overheating. Determine whether the unit was recently cleaned, moved, dropped, exposed to fluid, or affected by a power interruption.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Error Clears or Returns
steps.instructions: Restart the warmer after external checks are complete. Confirm whether Sys Fail 03 clears and normal startup completes, or whether the error returns, recurs intermittently, or prevents normal operation. If it clears, complete required operational, electrical safety, and performance verification before return to service.

steps.title: Isolate the Condition as Device-Related
steps.instructions: If stable power and acceptable external condition have been verified but Sys Fail 03 remains present, treat the issue as an internal memory or control-system failure requiring qualified bench evaluation.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: Return the warmer to service only after the error clears and the unit successfully passes required operational verification, electrical safety checks, and performance testing according to facility procedure.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 03 during startup. Unit could not be confirmed reliable for infant warming and was removed from clinical use.
CCR.Cause: Verified known-good outlet and inspected external power components and warmer condition with no external issue identified. Sys Fail 03 returned after restart, indicating likely internal memory, NVRAM retention, application flash, or Control PCA-related failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed warmer from service and labeled Out of Service for qualified bench evaluation and repair. Unit not returned to clinical use pending correction of the memory fault and successful post-repair operational and safety verification.

title: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer Infant Warmer - Error: Sys Fail 04 Memory Redundancy Error
description: Troubleshooting Sys Fail 04 Memory Redundancy Error, indicating mismatched redundantly stored variables that may prevent reliable warmer control, alarm operation, or safe clinical use.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the Panda Warmer from patient use when Sys Fail 04 is displayed. If an infant is under the warmer, notify clinical staff and transfer warming support to a known-working device before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm that the display reports Sys Fail 04 and document whether it occurs at power-up, during self-test, after operation, or intermittently after power cycling. Note any startup, control, heating, or alarm abnormalities.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Basic External Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, and device inlet for damage, looseness, contamination, or overheating. Connect the warmer to a known-good grounded hospital-grade outlet and observe startup behavior.

steps.title: Inspect for External Damage or Environmental Concerns
steps.instructions: Inspect for fluid intrusion, contamination, impact damage, unusual odor, overheating, or damage to the display and controls. Keep the unit out of service if unsafe external conditions are identified.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Power Restart
steps.instructions: With the unit out of patient use, power it off fully and restart it using the verified outlet. Observe whether Sys Fail 04 returns during startup or self-test.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Fault Is Persistent
steps.instructions: If Sys Fail 04 returns after external inspection, verified power, and controlled restart, classify it as a persistent internal Memory Redundancy Error involving mismatched redundantly stored variables.

steps.title: Escalate for Authorized Service Action
steps.instructions: Remove the warmer from clinical use and refer it for authorized bench evaluation or manufacturer-directed service. The identified corrective action is reprogramming the main application flash; if the problem persists, Control PCA replacement is indicated.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: After authorized corrective action, complete required operational verification, alarm checks, and applicable electrical safety testing. Return the warmer to service only after reliable operation is confirmed and documented.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 04 Memory Redundancy Error during startup. Unit could not be confirmed reliable for patient warming and was removed from clinical use.
CCR.Cause: Verified stable outlet power and inspected external condition with no correctable external issue found. Sys Fail 04 returned after controlled restart, consistent with a persistent internal memory redundancy failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed unit from service and labeled Out of Service. Sent for authorized bench evaluation and approved reprogramming of the main application flash; Control PCA replacement or vendor repair required if the error remains.

title: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer Infant Warmer - Error: Sys Fail 10 Self-Calibration Failure
description: Troubleshooting Sys Fail 10 [XX XX XX XX] when self-calibration fails, preventing reliable infant warmer operation and requiring removal from clinical use.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the Panda Warmer from patient use if Sys Fail 10 occurs while the warmer is occupied, prepared for use, or needed for patient care. Transfer the infant to a known-working warming device according to clinical procedure before performing troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: With the warmer removed from patient use, confirm that the display shows Sys Fail 10 [XX XX XX XX]. Document the displayed hexadecimal values exactly as shown and determine when the error occurs.

steps.title: Check the Power Source and External Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, strain relief, and power-entry area for visible damage, looseness, contamination, overheating, or liquid intrusion. Connect the warmer to a verified hospital-grade outlet for evaluation only after removal from patient use.

steps.title: Inspect the Unit for External Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Check for fluid intrusion, impact damage, cracked housing, loose assemblies, burnt odor, unusual heat, abnormal sounds, or control-panel damage. Do not open the unit during initial troubleshooting.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Power Restart
steps.instructions: With the unit out of service and disconnected from patient care, power the warmer off, wait briefly, and power it back on using a verified outlet. Observe whether Sys Fail 10 [XX XX XX XX] returns during startup.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Failure Requires Repair Evaluation
steps.instructions: If external conditions are ruled out and Sys Fail 10 returns, classify the issue as a device-related failure requiring qualified repair or bench evaluation. Manufacturer corrective information identifies Control PCA replacement as the indicated repair action.

steps.title: Confirm Safe Disposition
steps.instructions: Do not return the warmer to patient use based solely on one successful restart. Complete required functional inspection, alarm verification, and safety testing before return to service, or remove the unit from service and escalate for repair if the error remains or recurs.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare Panda Warmer displayed Sys Fail 10 [XX XX XX XX] during startup, indicating self-calibration failure. Unit was not considered safe for patient use.
CCR.Cause: Verified hospital-grade power source and inspected external condition with no correctable external issue identified. Sys Fail 10 returned after controlled restart, indicating likely internal Control PCA failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed Panda Warmer from service, labeled unit Out of Service, documented the displayed fault values, and routed the device for qualified bench repair and Control PCA evaluation/replacement as indicated.

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Acquisition Module Not Communicating
description: Troubleshooting MAC VU360 Acquisition Module communication issues caused by cable, connector, module, or functional checkout failures.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not connected to an active patient before troubleshooting the Acquisition Module. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed safely without interrupting patient care or ECG monitoring.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Communication Problem
steps.instructions: Ask staff what they observed. Confirm whether the device shows an Acquisition Module error, will not acquire ECG data, produces no waveform, intermittently loses connection, or fails during acquisition. Expected outcome: The complaint is clearly defined before parts are suspected.

steps.title: Verify the Correct Acquisition Module Is Connected
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 Acquisition Module is present and connected to the ECG device. The Acquisition Module is the patient ECG front end that acquires, digitizes, and transmits ECG signals to the main device. Expected outcome: The required ECG front-end module is physically present and connected.

steps.title: Check the Acquisition Module Cable Seating
steps.instructions: Reseat the Acquisition Module cable at both ends: the Acquisition Module and the ECG device connector. Ensure the connection is fully seated and secure. Expected outcome: If the issue was caused by a loose or partially seated cable, communication restores and ECG acquisition works. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Acquisition Module Cable
steps.instructions: Check the cable for cuts, crushing, sharp bends, stretched strain relief, exposed conductors, or signs of repeated pulling. Expected outcome: Cable damage is identified before suspecting the Acquisition Module or internal electronics.

steps.title: Inspect the Module and Device Connectors
steps.instructions: Examine the Acquisition Module connector and device-side connector for bent pins, damaged contacts, debris, liquid contamination, corrosion, or loose fit. Expected outcome: External connector problems are ruled out or corrected. If contamination or physical damage is found, remove the device from service.

steps.title: Power Cycle the ECG Device Safely
steps.instructions: With no patient connected, restart the MAC VU360 and allow it to fully boot. Recheck whether the Acquisition Module is recognized. Expected outcome: A temporary communication lockup clears and the module communicates normally. If resolved, verify operation before returning to use.

steps.title: Check for Intermittent Communication
steps.instructions: Gently move the Acquisition Module cable near the strain reliefs while observing the device status and waveform behavior. Do not force or sharply bend the cable. Expected outcome: If communication drops out when the cable is moved, suspect cable or connector damage and remove the unit from service.

steps.title: Test with Simulated ECG Data
steps.instructions: Connect a patient simulator and perform a functional ECG checkout. Verify the MAC VU360 can acquire a 12-lead ECG from simulated ECG signals. Expected outcome: A stable simulated ECG confirms the Acquisition Module signal path is functioning.

steps.title: Verify Full ECG Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm the acquired 12-lead ECG can be analyzed, stored, and transmitted according to the site’s normal workflow. Expected outcome: The device is not only acquiring ECG data but also completing the expected clinical ECG process.

steps.title: Run Acquisition LED Diagnostics
steps.instructions: From the service diagnostics area, run Acquisition LED diagnostics and confirm the Acquisition Module electrode-placement LEDs illuminate in sequence as expected. Expected outcome: LED function confirms part of the Acquisition Module communication and control path is responding.

steps.title: Run Acquisition Pushbutton Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Run Acquisition pushbutton diagnostics and test the ECG, Stop, Rhythm, and barcode scan buttons if present. Expected outcome: Button responses confirm the Acquisition Module input functions are communicating correctly.

steps.title: Run Related Functional Checkout Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Complete any related functional checkout diagnostics available for the MAC VU360 that support ECG acquisition, module communication, and accessory operation. Expected outcome: The device passes functional checkout before being returned to service.

steps.title: Document Any Repeatable Failure Pattern
steps.instructions: Note whether the issue occurs during boot, during acquisition, when the cable is moved, after transport, or only intermittently. Expected outcome: Repair escalation has enough detail to isolate cable, connector, module, or device-side failure.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC VU360 would not communicate with the Acquisition Module and could not reliably acquire a 12-lead ECG.
CCR.Cause: Found the Acquisition Module cable connection loose at the device-side connector; simulated ECG acquisition failed until the cable was reseated.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and inspected the Acquisition Module cable, verified no connector damage, ran simulated 12-lead ECG functional checkout, and confirmed acquisition, analysis, storage, and transmission passed.

helpfulDetails: Whether the Acquisition Module was detected at startup
Whether the failure was constant or intermittent
Acquisition Module cable reseated at both ends
Bent pins, debris, corrosion, or contamination found
Whether ECG analysis, storage, and transmission passed
Any barcode scan button behavior if equipped
Final device status: returned to service or removed from service

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Acquisition Module LEDs Not Working
description: Troubleshooting Acquisition Module electrode-placement LEDs that do not illuminate, cycle, or indicate electrode status correctly.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not actively connected to a patient before troubleshooting the Acquisition Module LEDs. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed only when it is safe and does not interrupt patient care. If the device is needed for an active ECG, have staff use another ECG machine before continuing.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported LED Problem
steps.instructions: Ask staff what they observed. Identify whether: No Acquisition Module LEDs illuminate; Only one LED does not work; Several LEDs do not work; LEDs illuminate but do not match electrode status; LEDs worked intermittently; The Acquisition Module itself is not being recognized. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is understood before parts are suspected.

steps.title: Check That the Acquisition Module Is Connected
steps.instructions: Inspect the Acquisition Module connection to the MAC VU360. Make sure the module cable is fully seated and not loose, strained, pinched, or damaged. Expected outcome: A poor module connection is ruled out as the reason the LEDs are not functioning. If reseating the connection restores LED function, document the loose connection and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Acquisition Module Externally
steps.instructions: Check the Acquisition Module for cracks, fluid intrusion, impact damage, missing labels, damaged LED windows, or signs of contamination. Expected outcome: Visible external damage is identified before diagnostics are run. If there is fluid damage, burning smell, unusual heat, or physical damage, remove the device from service and escalate for bench evaluation.

steps.title: Check the Module Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Inspect the cable and connector pins or contact areas for bent pins, debris, corrosion, looseness, or damaged strain relief. Expected outcome: The module communication and power path appears physically intact. If connector damage is found, do not continue using the module clinically until evaluated or repaired.

steps.title: Power Cycle the MAC VU360
steps.instructions: Turn the device off, wait briefly, and power it back on. Observe whether the Acquisition Module initializes normally and whether the LEDs respond. Expected outcome: A temporary software or communication issue is cleared. If the LEDs begin working normally after restart, verify operation and return the device to service if no other issues are present.

steps.title: Run Acquisition LED Diagnostics
steps.instructions: From the Service > Diagnostics screen, run Acquisition LED Diagnostics. Start the test and observe the Acquisition Module LEDs as the test cycles them on one by one. Expected outcome: All Acquisition Module LEDs illuminate in the expected sequence during the diagnostic test. If all LEDs cycle correctly, the LED hardware is likely functional. Continue checking electrode setup, leadwires, or staff-reported use conditions if the original complaint involved electrode status indication.

steps.title: Identify Which LEDs Fail During Diagnostics
steps.instructions: If the diagnostic does not pass, note the exact behavior. Record whether: No LEDs illuminate; Only one LED fails; LEDs are dim; LEDs flicker; LEDs do not cycle in order; The test does not start; The Acquisition Module is not detected. Expected outcome: The failure is documented clearly enough to support repair evaluation.

steps.title: Check for Leadwire or Electrode Misinterpretation
steps.instructions: If the LEDs illuminate during diagnostics but staff report incorrect electrode indications, check the patient cable, leadwires, electrodes, and electrode placement. Poor skin prep, dry electrodes, damaged leadwires, or bad lead connectors can make LED behavior appear incorrect even when the LEDs themselves work. Expected outcome: LED function is separated from electrode impedance or lead connection problems. If replacing electrodes or leadwires resolves the reported issue, document the accessory fault and stop.

steps.title: Do Not Replace Parts Until External Causes Are Ruled Out
steps.instructions: Before replacing the Acquisition Module or related parts, confirm that the module connection, cable, connector, leadwires, electrodes, and diagnostic results have been checked. Expected outcome: The repair path is based on verified failure, not assumption.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GE MAC VU360 Acquisition Module electrode-placement LEDs were not lighting during ECG setup.
CCR.Cause: Acquisition LED Diagnostics showed that the Acquisition Module LEDs did not cycle correctly, and external module cable and connector checks did not resolve the issue.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the MAC VU360 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for bench evaluation of the Acquisition Module and connection path.

helpfulDetails: Whether the issue affected all LEDs or only specific LEDs
Whether the Acquisition Module was recognized by the device
Whether Acquisition LED Diagnostics passed or failed
Whether LEDs cycled one by one during diagnostics
Any visible damage, fluid exposure, unusual heat, or smell
Whether leadwires or electrodes were swapped

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Acquisition Module Buttons Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting MAC VU360 Acquisition Module ECG, Stop, Rhythm, or barcode scan buttons that do not respond correctly.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the MAC VU360 is connected to a patient or being used for an active ECG. If the Acquisition Module buttons are not responding during patient use, have staff complete care using another available ECG machine before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is not dependent on a device with unreliable acquisition, rhythm, stop, or barcode controls. If this resolves the immediate clinical need, stop troubleshooting until the unit is safe to evaluate.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Button Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff which button failed and what the device did when pressed. Identify whether the issue involves: ECG button not starting acquisition; Rhythm button not starting rhythm printout or recording; Stop button not stopping a report or printout; Barcode scan button not initiating barcode scan function; Multiple Acquisition Module buttons not responding; Intermittent button response. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined before testing.

steps.title: Check Whether the Main Unit Still Responds
steps.instructions: Use the MAC VU360 touchscreen or main controls to confirm whether the ECG machine itself is operating normally. Expected outcome: If the main unit responds but Acquisition Module buttons do not, the issue is more likely isolated to the Acquisition Module, its cable path, or button assembly. If the entire ECG machine is locked up, frozen, or nonresponsive, address the system lockup or power issue first.

steps.title: Inspect the Acquisition Module Cable Connection
steps.instructions: Check that the Acquisition Module cable is fully seated and not loose, pulled, pinched, or strained. Look for bent pins, damaged connectors, broken strain relief, or signs that the cable has been stretched during use. Expected outcome: A secure cable connection supports button communication between the Acquisition Module and the MAC VU360. If reseating the cable restores button response, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Physical Buttons
steps.instructions: Examine the ECG, Stop, Rhythm, and barcode scan buttons for sticking, cracking, missing button covers, depressed buttons, or inconsistent tactile feel. Expected outcome: Buttons should move normally and feel consistent when pressed. If a button is physically damaged or stuck, remove the device from service and escalate for repair.

steps.title: Check for Fluid Intrusion or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the Acquisition Module for fluid residue, cleaning chemical buildup, dried gel, corrosion, or debris around the buttons and seams. Do not continue using a module with suspected fluid intrusion. Expected outcome: The module should be clean, dry, and free of contamination that could interfere with button operation. If fluid intrusion, corrosion, unusual smell, or sticky residue is found, remove the device from service and escalate.

steps.title: Confirm the Barcode Scanner Function Separately
steps.instructions: If only the barcode scan button is reported as not working, confirm whether the barcode reader itself is connected and functional. Try a known-good barcode and verify that the barcode reader is not the actual cause of the complaint. Expected outcome: The issue is separated between the Acquisition Module scan button and the barcode reader function. If the barcode reader is the problem, troubleshoot the barcode reader path before suspecting the Acquisition Module buttons.

steps.title: Run Acquisition Pushbutton Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Access the MAC VU360 diagnostic menu and run Acquisition Pushbutton Diagnostics. Test the ECG, Stop, Rhythm, and barcode scan button functions as prompted. Expected outcome: Each button press should register correctly during diagnostics. If all buttons pass diagnostics, attempt normal operation again and confirm with staff. If a button fails diagnostics after cable and physical checks, remove the device from service and escalate.

steps.title: Check for Intermittent Operation
steps.instructions: If diagnostics pass but the complaint was intermittent, gently reposition the Acquisition Module and cable while repeating button checks. Do not force or excessively flex the cable. Expected outcome: Button operation should remain consistent during normal handling. If button response drops out when the cable or module is moved, suspect a cable, connector, or module fault and remove the unit from service.

steps.title: Verify Final Function Before Returning to Use
steps.instructions: Confirm that the ECG, Stop, Rhythm, and barcode scan button functions respond normally. Expected outcome: The Acquisition Module buttons operate consistently, and the unit is safe to return to service. If button response cannot be verified, do not return the ECG machine to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the MAC VU360 Acquisition Module ECG button would not start an ECG acquisition.
CCR.Cause: Acquisition Module cable was secure, no fluid intrusion was found, but the ECG button failed Acquisition Pushbutton Diagnostics.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the MAC VU360 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and escalated for Acquisition Module repair or replacement.

helpfulDetails: Which button failed: ECG, Stop, Rhythm, or barcode scan
Whether one button or multiple buttons were affected
Whether the main MAC VU360 controls still responded
Evidence of fluid, residue, gel, corrosion, smell, heat, or damage
Barcode reader behavior, if barcode scan button was involved
Whether the failure was constant or intermittent

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Acquisition Module Barcode Scanner Not Scanning
description: Troubleshooting an Acquisition Module barcode scanner that will not scan patient barcodes or fails barcode diagnostics.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not being used for an active patient ECG. Do not troubleshoot the Acquisition Module barcode scanner while staff are actively acquiring a patient ECG. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed only when it is safe and does not delay patient care.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Barcode Scanner Problem
steps.instructions: Ask staff what happens when they attempt to scan a patient barcode. Determine whether: Nothing happens when the barcode scan button is pressed; The scanner activates but does not read the barcode; The barcode reads incorrectly; The scanner works intermittently; The Acquisition Module barcode diagnostic fails. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified before parts or configuration are suspected.

steps.title: Verify the Barcode Scanner Option Is Present
steps.instructions: Confirm the Acquisition Module is equipped with the optional barcode reader. Some Acquisition Modules may not have the scanner option installed. Expected outcome: The issue is not mistaken for a failure when the option is not physically present. If the barcode reader option is not installed, stop troubleshooting and document that the device is operating as configured.

steps.title: Verify Barcode Scanning Is Enabled
steps.instructions: Check the device configuration to confirm the barcode scanner option is enabled. If the option is disabled, staff may press the barcode scan button and see no useful response. Expected outcome: The device is configured to allow Acquisition Module barcode scanning. If enabling or correcting the configuration restores scanning, return the unit to service after verifying proper operation.

steps.title: Confirm Staff Are Using the Correct Barcode Scan Button
steps.instructions: Verify staff are pressing the barcode scan button on the Acquisition Module when attempting to start a patient barcode scan. Expected outcome: The scanner is being activated correctly. If staff were using the wrong control or workflow, provide guidance and stop once scanning is verified.

steps.title: Check Barcode Type and Barcode Quality
steps.instructions: Test with a known-good patient barcode or approved test barcode. Inspect the barcode for smearing, wrinkles, poor print contrast, damage, incorrect format, or glare from label covering. Expected outcome: The scanner reads a clean, compatible barcode. If the known-good barcode scans correctly, the issue is likely barcode quality, label format, or registration workflow rather than hardware failure.

steps.title: Inspect the Acquisition Module Scanner Window
steps.instructions: Check the barcode scanner window on the Acquisition Module for dirt, adhesive residue, cracks, scratches, or obstruction. Clean only according to approved facility and manufacturer cleaning practices. Expected outcome: The scanner window is clear and unobstructed. If cleaning the window restores barcode scanning, verify repeated successful scans before returning the device to service.

steps.title: Inspect the Acquisition Module and Cable Connections
steps.instructions: Check that the Acquisition Module cable is fully seated and not strained, pinched, cracked, or damaged. Inspect the connector for bent pins, looseness, contamination, or signs of impact. Expected outcome: The Acquisition Module has a reliable physical connection to the MAC VU360. If reseating the connection restores function, perform several test scans and document the corrected connection.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage to the Acquisition Module
steps.instructions: Inspect the module housing, scanner area, buttons, cable strain relief, and connector end. Look for evidence of drops, fluid intrusion, cracked plastic, damaged lens area, or an unresponsive scan button. Expected outcome: No obvious physical damage is present. If damage is found, remove the module from service and escalate for repair or replacement.

steps.title: Run Acquisition Barcode Reader Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Run the Acquisition Barcode Reader Diagnostics listed as part of functional checkout. Follow the diagnostic prompt and scan a compatible barcode when instructed. Expected outcome: The barcode scan completes successfully and the diagnostic passes. If the diagnostic passes, verify normal patient barcode workflow with staff before returning the unit to service.

steps.title: Compare With a Known-Good Setup if Available
steps.instructions: If another compatible MAC VU360 Acquisition Module is available, compare behavior using the same barcode and same main unit. Determine whether the issue follows the Acquisition Module or remains with the MAC VU360 system configuration/workflow. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the barcode, configuration, Acquisition Module, or system side before escalation.

steps.title: Do Not Assume Scanner Hardware Failure Too Early
steps.instructions: Before suspecting the scanner or module, confirm: Scanner option is installed; Scanner option is enabled; Correct scan button is being used; Barcode is compatible and readable; Scanner window is clean; Acquisition Module cable and connector are intact; Acquisition Barcode Reader Diagnostics have been performed. Expected outcome: Common external and configuration causes have been ruled out first.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the GE MAC VU360 Acquisition Module barcode scanner would not scan patient wristband barcodes when the barcode scan button was pressed.
CCR.Cause: Acquisition barcode troubleshooting found the scanner option enabled, barcode quality acceptable, but the Acquisition Barcode Reader Diagnostic failed after cable and scanner window checks.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the affected Acquisition Module from service, labeled it Out of Service, and escalated for module/scanner repair evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Whether the barcode scanner option was installed
Whether barcode scanning was enabled in configuration
Whether staff used the Acquisition Module barcode scan button
Whether a known-good barcode was used
Any visible cracks, fluid damage, or impact damage
Whether Acquisition Barcode Reader Diagnostics passed or failed
Whether the issue followed the Acquisition Module

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Bad Electrode Connection LED
description: Troubleshooting red Acquisition Module electrode LEDs caused by high impedance, poor skin prep, bad electrodes, leadwires, or connector issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the ECG is being attempted on an active patient. If the ECG is urgent and the MAC VU360 cannot obtain a clean tracing, have clinical staff use another available ECG machine. Expected outcome: Patient care is not delayed while troubleshooting electrode or cable problems.

steps.title: Confirm the LED Condition
steps.instructions: Look at the electrode LEDs on the Acquisition Module. A red electrode LED indicates a bad electrode connection due to high impedance. A green electrode LED indicates a good low-impedance connection. Expected outcome: The affected electrode position is identified before parts are replaced.

steps.title: Check Whether All Other Leads Are Green
steps.instructions: Determine whether only one electrode LED is red or whether multiple electrodes are affected. If only one LED is red, focus on that electrode, leadwire, and connector path. If multiple LEDs are red, suspect patient prep, electrode condition, common cable handling, or connection technique before suspecting the Acquisition Module. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is narrowed to either a single lead path or a broader setup issue.

steps.title: Verify Skin Preparation
steps.instructions: Check whether the electrode site was properly cleaned and prepped. Poor skin prep can create high impedance and cause a red electrode LED. Re-prep the site using the facility-approved process, especially if the patient has lotion, sweat, hair, dry skin, or poor electrode contact. Expected outcome: The LED should change from red to green once electrode contact improves. If the LED turns green, the issue was likely skin prep related. Stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Electrode Freshness and Condition
steps.instructions: Remove and inspect the electrode associated with the red LED. Check for dry gel, expired electrodes, poor adhesion, damaged packaging, or electrodes left open to air. Replace the electrode with a fresh, known-good electrode. Expected outcome: A good electrode should lower impedance and change the LED to green. If the LED turns green, replace the bad electrode supply as needed and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify Electrode Placement
steps.instructions: Confirm that the electrode is placed in the correct anatomical location and has full contact with the skin. An electrode placed over heavy hair, loose skin, clothing, dressing material, or bony areas may not make reliable contact. Expected outcome: Proper placement should produce a stable green LED and better ECG quality. If repositioning resolves the red LED, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Leadwire
steps.instructions: Check the leadwire connected to the electrode with the red LED. Look for cracked insulation, loose snap or clip connection, bent connector pins, contamination, strain damage, or intermittent connection when the cable is gently moved. Expected outcome: The leadwire should remain physically secure and should not cause the LED to flicker between red and green.

steps.title: Swap the Electrode and Leadwire Position
steps.instructions: Move the suspected electrode and leadwire to another position, or swap with a known-good leadwire position if available. Observe whether the red LED follows the electrode or leadwire, or stays with the same Acquisition Module input. Expected outcome: If the red LED follows the electrode, replace the electrode. If the red LED follows the leadwire, replace the leadwire or patient cable set. If the red LED stays with the same module input after known-good electrode and leadwire swaps, continue troubleshooting the module connection path.

steps.title: Check the Lead Connector at the Acquisition Module
steps.instructions: Inspect the lead connector where it attaches to the Acquisition Module. Make sure the connector is fully seated, clean, undamaged, and not loose. Do not force the connector or probe internal contacts. Expected outcome: A secure connector should allow the Acquisition Module to detect a good low-impedance connection.

steps.title: Test With a Known-Good Leadwire or Patient Cable Set
steps.instructions: If available, connect a known-good leadwire or cable set and repeat the electrode connection check. Expected outcome: If the red LED clears with a known-good cable set, the original cable or leadwire should be removed from service. If the red LED remains on the same module input with known-good electrodes and cables, suspect a module input or internal connection issue.

steps.title: Confirm ECG Quality Before Returning to Use
steps.instructions: When all electrode LEDs are green, confirm that the ECG waveform is stable and suitable for diagnostic acquisition. Expected outcome: All LEDs are green and ECG quality is acceptable for diagnostic use. If the device passes this check, return it to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported a red electrode LED on the GE MAC VU360 Acquisition Module and difficulty obtaining a clean ECG tracing.
CCR.Cause: Found high impedance at the affected electrode position caused by a dry electrode and intermittent leadwire connection.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the electrode, swapped in a known-good leadwire, verified all Acquisition Module electrode LEDs turned green, and confirmed acceptable ECG waveform quality.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or multiple LEDs were affected
Electrode lot or expiration issue, if found
Whether the issue followed the electrode, followed the leadwire, or stayed with the module input
Connector condition at the Acquisition Module

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Keyboard Keys Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting MAC VU360 keyboard keys that are partially or completely unresponsive before escalating to keyboard, cable, or printer PWA repair.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not actively being used on a patient. If the EKG is needed for patient care, move staff to another available electrocardiograph before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed without delaying patient testing or interrupting an active ECG acquisition.

steps.title: Confirm the Keyboard Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask the user which keys are not responding. Determine whether: Only certain keys fail; Entire sections of the keyboard fail; None of the keys respond; The issue happens all the time or intermittently. Expected outcome: The failure is separated into a partial keyboard failure or complete keyboard failure.

steps.title: Check for External Obstruction or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the keyboard surface for stuck keys, liquid residue, debris, adhesive labels, cleaning residue, or physical damage. Wipe the keyboard surface using approved cleaning methods only. Expected outcome: Keys are not being held down, blocked, or affected by obvious contamination. If cleaning or removing an obstruction restores normal key response, return the device to service after functional verification and stop.

steps.title: Check Device Power State and Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is powered on normally and the display is responsive. Verify whether the touchscreen or other controls respond, if available. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to keyboard input and not a full system lockup. If the entire device is frozen, follow the appropriate system lockup or power troubleshooting process instead.

steps.title: Restart the Device if Safe to Do So
steps.instructions: If no patient data entry or active acquisition is in progress, power cycle the MAC VU360. After restart, test several keys again. Expected outcome: Temporary software or input recognition issues clear after restart. If the keyboard responds normally after restart, document the finding, verify operation, and stop.

steps.title: Run Keyboard Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Access and run Keyboard Diagnostics according to site procedure and available service access. Test the reported keys and several known-good keys. Expected outcome: The diagnostic confirms whether the keyboard input is being detected correctly. If the keyboard passes diagnostics and the issue cannot be duplicated, document the test results and return the unit to service if clinically acceptable.

steps.title: If Only Some Keys Fail
steps.instructions: If Keyboard Diagnostics shows that only some keys do not respond, treat the keyboard assembly as faulty. The manual’s keyboard failure guidance identifies partial key failure as a keyboard fault. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to the keyboard assembly rather than the full input path. Remove the unit from service and replace or escalate for keyboard replacement per service process.

steps.title: If None of the Keys Work
steps.instructions: If no keys respond during Keyboard Diagnostics, inspect the keyboard membrane first. Look for: Cuts; Cracks; Worn or illegible labels; Liquid damage; Separation or lifting of the membrane; Signs of impact or abuse. Expected outcome: Obvious keyboard membrane damage is identified before deeper repair escalation. If the keyboard membrane is damaged, remove the unit from service and replace or escalate for keyboard replacement.

steps.title: Inspect the Keyboard Connection Path
steps.instructions: If none of the keys work and the keyboard membrane appears intact, the issue may involve the keyboard-to-printer PWA cable or printer PWA. Do not continue repeated clinical testing on a device with no keyboard response. Expected outcome: External and visible keyboard causes have been ruled out before repair-level action.

steps.title: Escalate Cable or Printer PWA Repair
steps.instructions: If the keyboard looks good but no keys work, remove the device from service for bench evaluation. The next likely repair path is the keyboard-to-printer PWA cable. If replacing the cable does not resolve the issue, the printer PWA may be the cause. Expected outcome: The device is routed for proper repair instead of continued field troubleshooting.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that several MAC VU360 keyboard keys would not respond during patient information entry.
CCR.Cause: Keyboard Diagnostics confirmed partial key failure, and no external obstruction or contamination was found.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the MAC VU360 from service and escalated for keyboard replacement.

helpfulDetails: Whether some keys failed or all keys failed
Specific keys or keyboard sections affected
Evidence of cuts, cracks, liquid damage, or worn labels
Whether touchscreen or other controls responded
Whether the issue was intermittent or constant
Whether the unit was removed from service

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Touchscreen Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting an unresponsive, inaccurate, intermittent, or partially working touchscreen using safe external checks before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not actively being used on a patient. If the touchscreen issue occurs during an active ECG, have clinical staff complete or repeat the ECG on another available device if needed. Expected outcome: Patient testing is not delayed or affected by an unreliable user interface.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Touchscreen Symptom
steps.instructions: Ask staff what the touchscreen is doing. Identify whether the issue is: Fully unresponsive; Responding intermittently; Registering touches in the wrong location; Only failing on one screen or menu; Delayed or freezing after startup; Working with some functions but not others. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is understood before assuming a touchscreen hardware issue.

steps.title: Check for Obvious Surface Issues
steps.instructions: Inspect the touchscreen surface for moisture, gel, adhesive residue, cleaning chemical buildup, cracks, or impact damage. Clean the screen using the facility-approved method for the device. Expected outcome: The touchscreen responds normally after contamination or residue is removed. If this resolves the issue, return the device to service and document the cleaning correction.

steps.title: Check for Gloves, Stylus, or Use-Related Factors
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the issue occurs with bare hands, gloved hands, or only with a specific user. If a stylus or nonstandard object is being used, test normal fingertip operation. Expected outcome: User technique or accessory-related touch issues are ruled out.

steps.title: Verify the Issue Is Not Application-Specific
steps.instructions: Navigate through multiple screens if possible. Check whether the touchscreen fails everywhere or only in one menu, workflow, or patient entry screen. Expected outcome: A global touchscreen problem is separated from a possible software screen or workflow issue.

steps.title: Reboot the MAC VU360
steps.instructions: Power the unit down using the normal shutdown method when possible. Restart the device and allow it to fully boot before retesting the touchscreen. Expected outcome: Temporary software lockup or frozen touch response clears after reboot. If the touchscreen works normally after restart, monitor briefly and document that the issue was cleared by reboot.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage Around the Display Assembly
steps.instructions: Inspect the bezel, screen edges, hinge/display area, and housing for signs of impact, liquid intrusion, looseness, or separation. Do not disassemble the display in the clinical area. Expected outcome: External signs of damage are identified before deeper service evaluation.

steps.title: Run Touchscreen Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Access and run the MAC VU360 Touchscreen Diagnostics. The service manual includes Touchscreen Diagnostics to verify whether the touch sensor is functioning properly, and touchscreen diagnostics are also part of the functional checkout procedure. Expected outcome: The diagnostic confirms whether the touch sensor is passing or failing. If Touchscreen Diagnostics passes, retest normal operation and check whether the issue is intermittent or workflow-specific. If Touchscreen Diagnostics fails, remove the device from service and proceed to repair escalation.

steps.title: Perform Functional Checkout as Needed
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen was cleaned, rebooted, or repaired, complete the appropriate functional checkout steps before returning the unit to use. Expected outcome: Touchscreen function is verified as safe and reliable for clinical operation.

steps.title: Escalate for Touchscreen-Related FRU Evaluation
steps.instructions: If external checks do not resolve the issue and Touchscreen Diagnostics fails, inspect or replace touchscreen-related FRUs according to the GE Healthcare service procedure. Expected outcome: The device is moved from troubleshooting to controlled repair or bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC VU360 touchscreen was not responding during patient entry.
CCR.Cause: Touchscreen surface was clean and undamaged, reboot did not correct the issue, and Touchscreen Diagnostics failed.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the MAC VU360 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for bench evaluation of touchscreen-related FRUs.

helpfulDetails: Whether the screen was fully unresponsive or intermittent
Whether the issue occurred on all screens or one menu only
Any cracks, impact damage, moisture, or residue

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - USB Port Not Detecting Flash Drive
description: Troubleshooting USB flash drive detection issues caused by media format, disabled USB storage settings, disabled ports, or failed USB hardware paths.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not being used for an active patient ECG acquisition. Do not troubleshoot USB storage, export, or port issues during an active test. Expected outcome: Patient testing is not interrupted and ECG data is not lost during troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported USB Issue
steps.instructions: Ask the user exactly what failed. Determine whether the issue involves: Flash drive not detected; ECG export failure; USB storage option unavailable; Only one USB port failing; All USB ports failing; Intermittent flash drive detection; Flash drive recognized on a PC but not on the MAC VU360. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly separated from a general export, network, or workflow issue.

steps.title: Try a Known-Good USB Flash Drive
steps.instructions: Use a known-good USB flash drive that has been verified on another computer. Prefer a simple FAT32-formatted USB flash drive. Avoid encrypted drives, security-locked drives, USB hubs, USB adapters, or very large-capacity drives during initial testing. Expected outcome: The device detects the known-good flash drive. If the known-good FAT32 drive is detected, the original flash drive is likely incompatible, improperly formatted, damaged, or security-restricted. Document the finding and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the USB Flash Drive and Port Area
steps.instructions: Check the flash drive connector for damage, looseness, or debris. Inspect the MAC VU360 USB ports for bent contacts, obstruction, cracked plastic, looseness, liquid contamination, or signs of physical damage. Expected outcome: No obvious physical damage is found. If a USB port is physically damaged or loose, remove the device from service and escalate for repair.

steps.title: Check Whether One Port or All Ports Fail
steps.instructions: Test the same known-good FAT32 USB flash drive in each of the three USB ports. Record whether the flash drive is detected in: USB port 1; USB port 2; USB port 3. Expected outcome: The flash drive is detected in all three USB ports. If only one port fails, suspect a localized port, cable, connector, or board path issue. If all three ports fail, continue checking system settings before assuming hardware failure.

steps.title: Verify External USB Storage Is Enabled
steps.instructions: Access the device settings and check: Settings > Hardware > USB setting. Verify that Enable External USB Storage is enabled. This setting matters because the MAC VU360 can block access to USB flash drives if external USB storage is disabled. Expected outcome: External USB storage is enabled. If the setting is disabled, enable it if authorized by site policy, retest the flash drive, document the correction, and stop if resolved.

steps.title: Verify at Least One USB Port Is Enabled
steps.instructions: In the same USB settings area, confirm that at least one USB port is enabled. If individual USB ports are disabled, flash drive access may be blocked even when the flash drive and physical port are functional. Expected outcome: The required USB ports are enabled. If the needed ports were disabled, enable them if authorized, retest all ports with the known-good flash drive, document the correction, and stop if resolved.

steps.title: Confirm Site Policy Before Changing USB Settings
steps.instructions: If USB storage or specific USB ports are disabled, confirm whether this was intentional due to cybersecurity, data security, or department policy. Do not override security restrictions without authorization. Expected outcome: USB access is either restored with approval or confirmed intentionally disabled. If USB use is blocked by policy, document that the device is functioning as configured and stop.

steps.title: Run USB Port Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Run the MAC VU360 USB Port Diagnostics function. Test all three USB ports using the known-good flash drive. Expected outcome: Diagnostics confirm flash drive detection in all three USB ports. If diagnostics pass and the flash drive is detected in all ports, the USB ports are working. If diagnostics fail on one port only, isolate the issue to that port path. If diagnostics fail on all ports after settings are verified, suspect a deeper USB controller, internal cable, or board-level issue.

steps.title: Retest the User’s Original Workflow
steps.instructions: After settings and diagnostics are verified, repeat the original task, such as exporting ECG data or saving to USB. Expected outcome: The MAC VU360 detects the flash drive and completes the intended USB workflow. If the known-good drive works but the user’s original flash drive does not, replace or reformat the original flash drive according to facility policy.

steps.title: Check for Intermittent Detection
steps.instructions: Gently verify that the flash drive remains detected without wiggling or stressing the connector. Do not force the drive or repeatedly flex the port. Expected outcome: USB detection remains stable. If detection is intermittent, remove the device from service and escalate for repair due to possible port or connector damage.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GE MAC VU360 would not detect a USB flash drive for ECG export.
CCR.Cause: Found external USB storage disabled under Settings > Hardware > USB setting, which blocked access to USB flash drives.
CCR.Resolution: Enabled authorized USB storage setting, verified at least one USB port was enabled, tested a known-good FAT32 flash drive in all three USB ports, and confirmed USB detection restored.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or user message shown during USB detection or export attempt
Accessories swapped, including known-good FAT32 USB flash drive and original flash drive tested
Power behavior during USB testing, including whether the issue occurred on AC power or battery
Environmental factors such as liquid contamination, physical port damage, debris, or cybersecurity restrictions
Indicator lights, USB storage setting status, individual USB port setting status, and USB Port Diagnostics result
Final device status, including whether all three USB ports failed or only one, whether intermittent detection was noted, and whether the device was returned to service or labeled Out of Service

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Event Log Will Not Export to USB
description: Troubleshooting MAC VU360 event log export failures, USB detection issues, USB settings, and flash drive format problems.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not being used for an active patient ECG acquisition. Do not troubleshoot USB export functions while clinical staff are actively acquiring or reviewing a patient ECG. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed only when the device is safe to access and clinical workflow is not interrupted.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Export Failure
steps.instructions: Ask the user what message appears during the event log export attempt. Common messages may include: No USB device detected; Save to USB failed; Export option unavailable; USB drive inserted but not recognized; Event log export starts but does not complete. Expected outcome: The failure mode is identified before changing settings or replacing accessories.

steps.title: Verify That External USB Storage Is Supported and Enabled
steps.instructions: Confirm the event log export workflow is intended to use External USB Storage. Verify that at least one USB port is enabled in the device settings or configuration, if accessible to Clinical Engineering. Expected outcome: The export path is available and the MAC VU360 is allowed to communicate with a USB storage device.

steps.title: Check USB Drive Seating
steps.instructions: Remove and firmly reinsert the USB flash drive into the MAC VU360 USB port. Avoid using excessive force. Inspect for loose fit, bent connector, damaged USB housing, or debris in the port. Expected outcome: The USB drive seats fully and the device has another opportunity to detect it. If the event log exports successfully after reseating the drive, document the result and stop.

steps.title: Try Another USB Port if Available
steps.instructions: If the MAC VU360 has more than one enabled USB port, move the USB flash drive to another enabled port. This helps separate a port-specific issue from a USB drive or settings issue. Expected outcome: The USB drive is recognized in another enabled USB port. If the export works from another port, document the original port behavior and evaluate whether that port requires further service review.

steps.title: Use a FAT32 USB Flash Drive
steps.instructions: Confirm the USB flash drive is formatted as FAT32, since the MAC VU360 supports the FAT32 file system for USB flash drive use. Avoid using USB drives formatted as NTFS, exFAT, encrypted, locked, or partitioned in an unusual way. Expected outcome: The USB drive uses a supported file system and is more likely to be recognized by the device.

steps.title: Confirm the USB Drive Is Write-Enabled
steps.instructions: Use a USB flash drive that is not write-protected, encrypted, full, damaged, or restricted by security software. If available, test the USB drive on a workstation by copying a small non-patient test file to it. Expected outcome: The drive can accept new files before it is used for event log export.

steps.title: Respond to “No USB Device Detected”
steps.instructions: If the message No USB device detected appears: Reseat the USB drive; Try another enabled USB port; Try a different FAT32 USB flash drive; Verify USB port settings are enabled; Inspect the USB port for visible damage or looseness. Expected outcome: The device detects a properly formatted and supported USB flash drive. If a different USB drive or port resolves the issue, document the failed accessory or port and stop.

steps.title: Respond to “Save to USB Failed”
steps.instructions: If the message Save to USB failed appears: Try a different FAT32 USB flash drive; Confirm the drive is write-enabled; Confirm the drive has available space; Avoid using encrypted or security-managed flash drives; Retry the export after reinserting the drive. Expected outcome: The event log saves successfully to a compatible USB drive. If a replacement drive resolves the issue, remove the failed USB drive from use and document the accessory issue.

steps.title: Check for Repeated Failure Across Known-Good Drives
steps.instructions: If multiple FAT32, write-enabled USB flash drives fail on all enabled ports, suspect a device configuration, software, or hardware issue rather than the USB accessory. Do not continue repeated export attempts if the port feels loose, damaged, overheated, or physically unstable. Expected outcome: External causes have been reasonably ruled out before escalation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GE MAC VU360 event log would not export to a USB flash drive and displayed a USB export failure message.
CCR.Cause: Found the original USB drive was not recognized by the MAC VU360; event log export requires External USB Storage, an enabled USB port, and a compatible FAT32 USB flash drive.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the USB drive, verified USB port availability, replaced it with a FAT32 write-enabled USB flash drive, and confirmed the event log exported successfully.

helpfulDetails: Error message displayed: No USB device detected or Save to USB failed
Whether another USB port was tested
Whether USB ports were enabled in settings
USB drive format confirmed as FAT32
Whether the USB drive was write-enabled
Whether another USB drive was tested
Any visible USB port damage or looseness

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Barcode Reader Not Working
description: Troubleshooting MAC VU360 barcode reader failures, missed scans, failed barcode diagnostics, or barcode text not entering correctly.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not actively being used to acquire an ECG on a patient. Do not troubleshoot scanner function during active ECG acquisition or while patient demographics are being entered for a live patient. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed without risking incorrect patient identification or workflow interruption.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Barcode Reader Problem
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff what is happening when they try to scan. Identify whether the issue is: Barcode reader has no light or response; Barcode scans but no text appears; Wrong patient information populates; Scanner only works intermittently; Barcode Reader Diagnostics shows Failure; Scanner works on some barcodes but not others. Expected outcome: The failure mode is clearly understood before parts are swapped.

steps.title: Check the Barcode Reader Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the barcode reader cable and connector. Confirm the barcode reader is fully seated and connected to the correct port or connection path used by the MAC VU360. Look for loose USB connections, damaged cable strain relief, bent connector pins, cracked housing, or signs of liquid damage. Expected outcome: The reader is physically connected and no obvious external damage is present. If reconnecting the reader restores scanning, verify with a test barcode, document the loose connection, and stop.

steps.title: Check for Power or Scanner Response
steps.instructions: Aim the barcode reader at a barcode and confirm whether the scanner illuminates, beeps, vibrates, or otherwise responds. Expected outcome: The scanner shows normal response when triggered. If there is no response at all, suspect a disconnected reader, failed reader, damaged cable, or port/connection issue.

steps.title: Verify Barcode Quality
steps.instructions: Inspect the barcode being scanned. Check for smearing, wrinkles, poor print contrast, torn labels, curved surfaces, glare, or labels covered by tape or plastic. Expected outcome: The barcode is clean, flat, readable, and appropriate for scanning. If the barcode is damaged or poor quality, test with a better label or reprinted barcode before assuming a device issue.

steps.title: Try a Known-Good Barcode
steps.instructions: Scan a known-good barcode that has worked previously or a clean test barcode provided by the department. Expected outcome: The barcode reader scans the known-good barcode and enters readable text.
