If the known-good barcode scans correctly, the issue is likely barcode quality, label formatting, or workflow-specific rather than barcode reader failure.

steps.title: Check Scanner Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the barcode reader has not been changed, replaced with the wrong model, reprogrammed, or reset to an incompatible configuration. Some barcode scanners can be configured by scanning setup barcodes, which may change output format, suffix, prefix, barcode type, or USB keyboard behavior. Expected outcome: The scanner configuration supports the barcode type and input behavior expected by the MAC VU360. If configuration is suspected, compare with a known-good scanner or escalate for proper configuration verification.

steps.title: Run Barcode Reader Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Access the MAC VU360 Barcode Reader Diagnostics test. During the test, scan the barcode shown on the screen. Expected outcome: The scanned information displays as text and the diagnostic result shows Success. If the scan does not complete successfully, the diagnostic test displays Failure.

steps.title: Interpret the Diagnostic Result
steps.instructions: If Barcode Reader Diagnostics shows Success, the reader is communicating with the MAC VU360. Recheck barcode quality, barcode type, workflow setup, and whether the issue only occurs with specific patient labels. Expected outcome: A successful diagnostic points away from a basic reader communication failure. If Barcode Reader Diagnostics shows Failure, continue with reader and connection path checks.

steps.title: Swap with a Known-Good Barcode Reader if Available
steps.instructions: Connect a known-good compatible barcode reader and rerun Barcode Reader Diagnostics. Expected outcome: The known-good reader scans the displayed barcode and the test shows Success. If the known-good reader works, remove the failed barcode reader from use and replace it. If the known-good reader also fails, suspect the MAC VU360 USB/reader connection path, configuration, or internal interface issue.

steps.title: Inspect the USB / Reader Connection Path
steps.instructions: Check for loose external connections, damaged port housing, debris in the connector, or intermittent movement when the cable is touched. Do not perform internal board-level troubleshooting during field checks. Expected outcome: Any external port or cable issue is identified without unnecessary disassembly. If the port or internal connection path appears faulty, remove the device from service and escalate for repair evaluation.

steps.title: Confirm Final Function Before Returning to Use
steps.instructions: After any reconnection, scanner swap, or configuration correction, run Barcode Reader Diagnostics again. Then scan a known-good barcode in the normal workflow if appropriate. Expected outcome: Barcode information displays correctly and the diagnostic result shows Success. If the barcode reader works normally, return the MAC VU360 to service and document the resolution.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC VU360 barcode reader would not scan patient ID labels.
CCR.Cause: Barcode Reader Diagnostics failed, and the original scanner did not display scanned text when scanning the on-screen diagnostic barcode.
CCR.Resolution: Verified barcode quality and connection, tested with a known-good barcode, swapped in a known-good barcode reader, confirmed Barcode Reader Diagnostics showed Success, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Barcode Reader Diagnostics result: Success or Failure
Whether scanned text displayed during diagnostics
Barcode quality or label damage observed
Scanner response, light, beep, or no response
Whether issue occurred with all barcodes or only specific labels

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - LAN Communication Failure
description: Troubleshooting MAC VU360 LAN communication, Ethernet, IP configuration, and network diagnostic failures using external checks before escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not being used for an active patient ECG acquisition. If the unit is needed for patient care, move staff to another working ECG machine before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed without delaying patient testing or interrupting active ECG acquisition.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported LAN Failure
steps.instructions: Ask staff what failed and when it occurred. Determine whether the issue involves: LAN communication failure, DICOM or MUSE transmission failure, Ethernet connection unavailable, LAN diagnostics failure, Adapter not available, LAN interface disabled, LAN interface not found, Failed IP configuration retrieval, Unable to retrieve network configuration, Invalid IP configuration, Failed IP address retrieval, Failed to add IP rule. Expected outcome: The failure type is identified before changing settings or involving IT.

steps.title: Check Whether the Device Works Locally
steps.instructions: Verify the MAC VU360 can power on, acquire ECG data, display waveforms, and save or print locally if configured. Expected outcome: If local ECG functions work but network transmission fails, the issue is more likely LAN, configuration, or network-path related. If the unit cannot function locally, troubleshoot the base device issue first.

steps.title: Inspect the Ethernet Cable
steps.instructions: Confirm the Ethernet cable is fully seated in the MAC VU360 LAN port and the wall jack. Look for bent clips, damaged cable jackets, sharp kinks, loose connectors, or signs that the cable has been pulled. Expected outcome: A properly connected and undamaged cable is confirmed. If reseating or replacing the cable restores LAN communication, document the cable issue and stop.

steps.title: Swap with a Known-Good Ethernet Cable
steps.instructions: Replace the Ethernet cable with a known-good hospital-approved cable. Expected outcome: This rules out a failed or intermittent cable before deeper troubleshooting. If communication returns, leave the working cable in place, remove the failed cable from service, and stop.

steps.title: Verify the Wall Jack and Network Port
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is connected to the correct network wall jack for ECG/MUSE/DICOM communication. If available, compare with another working MAC VU360 location or test the same cable on a known-good active jack. Expected outcome: The physical network path is verified before assuming device failure. If the wall jack appears inactive or assigned incorrectly, escalate to IT/network support.

steps.title: Inspect the MAC VU360 LAN Port
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the LAN port on the MAC VU360 for obvious external damage, looseness, debris, bent contacts, or poor connector retention. Do not disassemble the device to inspect internal boards. Expected outcome: The external LAN port is physically intact and able to hold the cable securely. If the LAN port is damaged or loose, remove the device from service and send it for repair evaluation.

steps.title: Check LAN Link Indicators if Visible
steps.instructions: Look for link or activity indicators at the Ethernet port if visible on the device, dock, adapter, or connected network equipment. Expected outcome: Link activity supports that the physical network connection is active. If no link indication is present with a known-good cable and known-good jack, suspect a network path issue or device LAN hardware fault.

steps.title: Verify LAN Settings on the MAC VU360
steps.instructions: Review the configured LAN settings using the appropriate device menu and facility-approved configuration. Confirm whether the unit should use DHCP or a static IP address. Verify that network values match the site standard, including: IP address, Subnet mask, Gateway, DNS settings, Network profile or interface setting, LAN enabled status. Expected outcome: The device LAN configuration matches the hospital’s expected network setup. If settings are incorrect, correct them only if authorized or coordinate with IT.

steps.title: Run LAN Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Run the MAC VU360 LAN diagnostics and review the Hardware, Software, and IP Configuration check results. Expected outcome: LAN diagnostics help separate physical adapter/interface issues from IP configuration problems. If diagnostics show adapter not available, LAN interface disabled, or LAN interface not found, focus on LAN enablement, cable path, port condition, and possible device hardware failure. If diagnostics show failed IP configuration retrieval, invalid IP configuration, failed IP address retrieval, unable to retrieve network configuration, or failed to add IP rule, focus on network settings and IT support.

steps.title: Perform the LAN Ping Test
steps.instructions: Use the LAN ping test with a valid IPv4 address or fully qualified domain name approved by IT. Test a known network destination such as a gateway, server, or approved host. Expected outcome: A successful ping confirms basic LAN communication beyond the device. If ping fails by hostname but works by IP address, suspect DNS configuration. If ping fails by IP address, suspect device IP settings, VLAN/network assignment, wall jack issue, or LAN hardware path failure.

steps.title: Confirm MUSE, DICOM, or Destination Server Settings
steps.instructions: If basic LAN connectivity works but ECG transmission still fails, verify the destination settings. Check that the server address, port, destination name, and workflow settings match the current hospital configuration. Expected outcome: LAN connectivity is separated from application-level transmission problems. If the LAN ping test passes but transmission fails, involve the ECG system administrator, MUSE administrator, or IT application support.

steps.title: Test from a Known-Good Network Location
steps.instructions: If practical, connect the MAC VU360 to a known-good ECG network location used by another working MAC VU360. Expected outcome: This helps determine whether the issue follows the machine or stays with the wall jack/network location. If the issue follows the MAC VU360, suspect device configuration or device hardware. If the issue stays with the room or jack, escalate to IT/network support.

steps.title: Avoid Unapproved Network Changes
steps.instructions: Do not randomly assign IP addresses, change VLAN-related settings, alter server destinations, or reset network profiles without facility approval. Expected outcome: The troubleshooting does not create duplicate IP conflicts, failed routing, or patient data transmission issues.

steps.title: Confirm Resolution with a Controlled Test
steps.instructions: After correcting cable, jack, LAN setting, or IP configuration issues, repeat LAN diagnostics and the LAN ping test. If applicable, send a test ECG or confirm a successful transmission with the appropriate clinical or ECG system contact. Expected outcome: Network communication is verified before returning the MAC VU360 to service. If the issue is resolved, document the corrective action and stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GE MAC VU360 would not transmit ECGs over LAN and showed a LAN communication failure.
CCR.Cause: LAN diagnostics showed an IP configuration failure, and the device network settings did not match the assigned hospital network configuration.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected LAN configuration with IT, verified Ethernet connection, passed LAN diagnostics, confirmed successful ping test, and returned the MAC VU360 to service.

helpfulDetails: Network port or jack location used
Hardware, Software, and IP Configuration diagnostic status
Ping passed or failed by IP address
Ping passed or failed by hostname
IP address, subnet, gateway, and DNS verified with IT
MUSE, DICOM, or server destination tested
Whether issue followed the machine or stayed with the room

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Wireless Communication Failure
description: Troubleshooting MAC VU360 WLAN connection, SSID, wireless signal, credential, security, or transfer failures using external and configuration checks first.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the ECG is not actively being used for patient acquisition or urgent ECG transmission. If the unit is needed for immediate patient care, move staff to another working ECG machine or use the approved downtime workflow. Expected outcome: Patient ECG acquisition and transmission are not delayed by troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Wireless Failure
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff what failed and when it occurred. Identify whether the issue involves: No wireless connection; Cannot find the wireless network; Connects but does not transmit; DICOM, MUSE, or order download failure over Wi-Fi; Intermittent wireless dropouts; WLAN diagnostics failure; Wireless works in one area but not another. Expected outcome: The failure is defined before network settings are changed.

steps.title: Check Whether the Problem Is Wireless Only
steps.instructions: If available, test the device on a known-good wired LAN connection. Confirm whether ECG transmission, order download, or system communication works over LAN. Expected outcome: If LAN works but WLAN fails, the issue is likely wireless configuration, signal, access point, antenna/module, or WLAN security related. If LAN also fails, troubleshoot general network, server, MUSE, DICOM, or device communication settings before focusing only on WLAN.

steps.title: Confirm Wireless Is Enabled
steps.instructions: Check the MAC VU360 communication or network settings and confirm WLAN is enabled. Verify the device is not set to wired-only communication or another communication profile. Expected outcome: The device is configured to attempt wireless communication. If enabling the correct WLAN setting resolves communication, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: Verify the Correct SSID
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is trying to connect to the correct hospital wireless SSID. Compare the configured SSID with the approved clinical network information. Watch for similarly named guest, public, test, or legacy networks. Expected outcome: The ECG is pointed to the correct wireless network. If correcting the SSID resolves communication, document the change and stop.

steps.title: Check Wireless Range and Location
steps.instructions: Move the ECG to an area with known-good wireless coverage. If another MAC VU360 or similar clinical device works in the same area, compare performance. Expected outcome: Wireless failure is separated from poor signal coverage or local access point issues. If the unit works in one area but not another, escalate to network support for wireless coverage or access point review.

steps.title: Check Signal Strength
steps.instructions: Review wireless signal strength at the MAC VU360 if visible in the device settings or WLAN diagnostics. Weak or fluctuating signal can cause intermittent transmission failures even when the device appears connected. Expected outcome: The device has stable signal strength before communication testing continues.

steps.title: Verify Wireless Credentials
steps.instructions: Confirm the configured wireless credentials are correct. Depending on the facility setup, this may include: Pre-shared key; Username and password; Certificate requirement; Authentication method; Network profile assigned to the device. Expected outcome: The ECG has valid credentials for the approved clinical WLAN. If credentials were changed by IT or expired, coordinate with network support before returning the device to service.

steps.title: Check Wireless Security Requirements
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 wireless profile matches the hospital wireless security requirements. Review whether the network requires WPA/WPA2 settings, enterprise authentication, certificates, MAC address registration, or device whitelisting. Expected outcome: The ECG wireless configuration matches the current network security policy. If security settings do not match, correct only approved configuration items or escalate to the appropriate network or GE support team.

steps.title: Confirm Country or Region Wireless Settings
steps.instructions: Check that the wireless country or region setting is correct for the facility. Incorrect region settings may affect available wireless channels or allowed WLAN operation. Expected outcome: The MAC VU360 wireless region setting matches the device location and approved configuration.

steps.title: Run WLAN Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Use the MAC VU360 WLAN Diagnostics function listed in the service information. Record whether diagnostics show: Wireless adapter present; SSID detected; Signal strength; Association success or failure; Authentication failure; IP address status; Gateway or server reachability issue. Expected outcome: WLAN Diagnostics narrows the issue to signal, authentication, IP/network routing, or hardware detection.

steps.title: Check IP Address and Network Assignment
steps.instructions: Confirm the device receives the expected IP address, subnet, gateway, and DNS information if those details are visible. If the unit connects to the SSID but cannot communicate with MUSE, DICOM, or servers, the issue may be DHCP, VLAN, routing, firewall, or DNS related. Expected outcome: Wireless connection and network communication are both verified, not just SSID association.

steps.title: Compare Against a Known-Good MAC VU360
steps.instructions: If another MAC VU360 is working on WLAN, compare non-sensitive configuration items. Check SSID, communication profile, wireless mode, server destination, and general network setup. Do not copy passwords, certificates, or restricted credentials unless following approved facility and vendor procedures. Expected outcome: Device-specific configuration differences are identified.

steps.title: Inspect External Wireless Hardware Indicators
steps.instructions: Without opening the device, check for obvious external damage, missing covers, impact damage, or signs that the unit was dropped. If the wireless module is not detected in diagnostics or WLAN settings are unavailable, suspect internal wireless hardware or antenna-related failure. Expected outcome: External damage or missing WLAN detection is identified before escalation.

steps.title: Restart and Retest Safely
steps.instructions: If allowed by department workflow, restart the MAC VU360 after confirming no active patient data will be lost. Recheck WLAN connection, run WLAN Diagnostics again, and attempt a test transmission according to site policy. Expected outcome: Temporary communication faults are cleared without affecting patient care. If the wireless connection and transmission now pass, return the device to service and document the successful retest.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC VU360 would not connect to the wireless network and ECGs were not transmitting to MUSE over WLAN.
CCR.Cause: WLAN Diagnostics showed the device was in range but was configured for the wrong hospital SSID.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the WLAN profile to the approved clinical SSID, verified wireless connection, completed successful test transmission, and returned the ECG machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or wireless failure message shown to staff
Accessories swapped or network connection method tested
Power behavior, restart behavior, and whether LAN communication worked
Environmental factors such as device location, signal coverage, wireless SSID verified, and access point area
Indicator lights, WLAN Diagnostics result, authentication or credential error, and IP address/DHCP status
MUSE, DICOM, or order download behavior
Whether another MAC VU360 worked in the same area
Any access point, VLAN, firewall, or certificate escalation

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - No Battery Backup
description: Troubleshooting a MAC VU360 that will not operate on battery power or loses power when unplugged from AC.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not being used for an active patient ECG. If the device loses power when unplugged, do not attempt patient testing until battery backup is confirmed reliable. Expected outcome: Patient testing is not interrupted by sudden device shutdown.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Battery Backup Failure
steps.instructions: Ask staff what occurred and when it occurred. Determine whether the unit shuts off immediately when unplugged, runs only briefly on battery, shows a low battery warning, does not appear to charge, shows abnormal battery LED behavior, or fails battery diagnostics or checkout testing. Expected outcome: The failure mode is clearly identified before parts are replaced.

steps.title: Verify AC Power First
steps.instructions: Plug the MAC VU360 into a known-good hospital-grade outlet. Confirm the power cord is fully seated at the device and wall outlet. Check that the unit powers normally on AC. Expected outcome: The device operates normally on AC power before battery backup is evaluated. If the unit does not power on with AC, troubleshoot AC power or power supply concerns first.

steps.title: Check Battery Charge Status
steps.instructions: Leave the device connected to AC power long enough to allow charging. Observe the keyboard battery LED. Useful LED indications include: Flashing amber every two seconds: battery is charging; Flashing amber every one second: battery is critically low; Flashing amber every half-second: battery communication failure. Expected outcome: The battery LED provides a clear indication of charge, low battery, or communication status.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Seating and Battery Door
steps.instructions: Power the unit down safely. Remove AC power only after confirming it is safe to do so. Check that the battery is properly seated in its compartment. Verify the battery door is installed correctly and fully latched. Expected outcome: A loose battery, poor seating, or improperly installed battery door is ruled out. If reseating restores battery function, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: Reseat the Battery
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the battery according to facility-approved procedures. Reconnect AC power and observe whether the battery LED resumes normal charging behavior. Expected outcome: The device recognizes the battery and begins charging normally. If the LED continues to indicate communication failure, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check for Battery Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If the keyboard battery LED flashes amber every half-second, treat this as a battery communication failure. Reseat the battery again and inspect for obvious issues such as battery not fully seated, damaged battery contacts, debris in the battery area, loose or damaged battery holder, or battery door interference. Expected outcome: Any simple seating or contact issue is corrected before replacing parts.

steps.title: Run Battery Metrics
steps.instructions: Access the battery metrics available through the device service or diagnostic workflow. Review the reported battery condition, charge level, and any battery-related fault information. Expected outcome: Battery condition is verified using device-reported data rather than guesswork. If the battery metrics show poor battery condition, failed communication, or abnormal battery status, replace or escalate as appropriate.

steps.title: Perform the Quick Battery Charge and Discharge Test
steps.instructions: Run the quick battery charge and discharge functional checkout test. Confirm the battery can charge, support operation, and discharge as expected. Expected outcome: The battery passes the functional checkout and supports short battery operation. If the device fails the quick charge/discharge test, do not return it to service.

steps.title: Test Battery Operation After Charging
steps.instructions: After charging, power the device on while connected to AC. Disconnect AC power briefly in a controlled test area. Confirm the unit remains powered on without rebooting, shutting down, or displaying a critical battery condition. Expected outcome: The MAC VU360 continues operating on battery backup when AC is removed. If the device remains powered on and battery status is acceptable, return it to service after documenting the results.

steps.title: Replace the Battery if Diagnostics Fail
steps.instructions: If the battery fails metrics, fails the quick charge/discharge test, will not hold charge, or continues to show communication failure after reseating, replace the battery per facility process. After replacement, repeat the battery metrics and quick battery charge/discharge test. Expected outcome: The replacement battery is recognized, charges correctly, and supports battery operation.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Holder and External Power Path
steps.instructions: If a known-good or replacement battery still does not work, inspect the battery holder area and accessible power path for obvious damage. Look for damaged contacts, loose holder components, unusual heat, smell, or signs of liquid intrusion. Expected outcome: External and easily visible battery connection issues are identified before deeper repair escalation. Do not perform internal board-level troubleshooting during basic Clinical Engineering response unless authorized and trained.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported the GE MAC VU360 shut off immediately when unplugged from AC power and would not operate on battery backup.
CCR.Cause: Battery LED showed abnormal battery status and the unit failed the quick battery charge/discharge test after battery reseating.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the MAC VU360 from service, labeled it Out of Service, replaced the battery for evaluation, and repeated battery diagnostics before return-to-service decision.

helpfulDetails: AC adapter or power cord condition
Any unusual heat, smell, or liquid intrusion

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Audio / Speaker Not Working
description: Troubleshooting missing audio, failed audio diagnostics, muted alerts, or speaker concerns using external checks before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not actively being used for patient ECG acquisition. Do not troubleshoot audio during an active ECG, stress workflow, or patient-connected session unless clinical staff confirm it is safe. Expected outcome: Troubleshooting is performed without interrupting patient care or missing audible alerts during use.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Audio Symptom
steps.instructions: Ask the user whether all audio is missing or only certain sounds are affected. Determine whether the issue involves: No audible feedback at all; No alert tones; No keyboard or touchscreen feedback sounds; Low or distorted speaker output; Intermittent audio; Audio Diagnostics failure during functional checkout. Expected outcome: The exact audio complaint is understood before adjusting settings or removing the device from service.

steps.title: Check Volume and Sound Settings
steps.instructions: Review the MAC VU360 volume and audio settings from the device interface. Confirm audio has not been muted, lowered, or disabled through user-accessible settings. Expected outcome: Audio returns after correcting volume or mute settings. If this resolves the issue, document the setting correction and stop.

steps.title: Verify the Device Is Fully Powered and Stable
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit is properly powered by AC or has adequate battery charge. Low battery, startup instability, or abnormal system behavior may affect device functions during checkout. Expected outcome: The device is operating in a stable powered condition before audio testing.

steps.title: Restart the Device if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the audio issue appears after startup, software lag, or abnormal interface behavior, perform a normal shutdown and restart. Do not force power down during active patient use or data transfer. Expected outcome: Normal audio function returns after restart. If this resolves the issue, document the restart and confirm audio before returning the unit to service.

steps.title: Run Audio Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Run the MAC VU360 Audio Diagnostics as part of the functional checkout process. The functional checkout requires Audio Diagnostics to pass because audible feedback and alerts are part of safe device operation. Expected outcome: Audio Diagnostics passes and audible output is verified. If Audio Diagnostics passes and sound is heard clearly, return the device to service after documentation.

steps.title: Listen for Speaker Quality Issues
steps.instructions: During Audio Diagnostics, listen for abnormal behavior such as: No sound; Very low sound; Crackling; Distortion; Intermittent tone; Speaker cutting in and out. Expected outcome: Audio is clear, consistent, and loud enough for normal clinical use.

steps.title: Inspect External Speaker Openings and Housing
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the speaker area and device housing for obvious external problems. Check for fluid residue, debris, blocked speaker openings, cracked housing, or signs of impact damage. Expected outcome: No external obstruction or damage is affecting speaker output. If contamination, impact damage, or fluid intrusion is suspected, remove the unit from service and escalate for bench evaluation.

steps.title: Check for Recent Cleaning or Fluid Exposure
steps.instructions: Ask whether the unit was recently cleaned, splashed, dropped, or exposed to fluid. Fluid intrusion near speaker openings or internal audio components can cause failed audio diagnostics or distorted output. Expected outcome: Possible environmental or handling cause is identified.

steps.title: Repeat Audio Verification After Corrections
steps.instructions: After correcting settings, restarting the unit, or clearing any safe external obstruction, rerun Audio Diagnostics. Expected outcome: Audio Diagnostics passes and audible function is verified. If the diagnostic fails again, do not return the device to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC VU360 had no audible tones and failed the audio portion of functional checkout.
CCR.Cause: Volume settings were verified, the unit was restarted, and Audio Diagnostics failed with no speaker output heard.
CCR.Resolution: Device was removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for bench evaluation due to failed audible function verification.

helpfulDetails: Whether all audio was missing or only certain sounds
Whether tones were low, distorted, intermittent, or absent
Evidence of impact, fluid, debris, unusual heat, or smell

title: GE Healthcare MAC VU360 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Display Dim, Brightness, or Screen Visibility Problem
description: Troubleshooting dim, blank, flickering, or hard-to-see MAC VU360 display issues using external checks and onboard diagnostics.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC VU360 is not actively being used to acquire or review a patient ECG. If the display issue occurs during an active patient test, have clinical staff pause use of the device and move to another ECG machine if needed. Expected outcome: Patient testing is not delayed or affected by an unreliable display.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Display Symptom
steps.instructions: Ask staff what they are seeing on the screen. Determine whether the issue is: Display is dim; Display is blank; Screen brightness changes unexpectedly; Screen flickers; Image is present but hard to see; Display works but touchscreen response is normal; Display issue occurs only on battery or only on AC power. Expected outcome: The display problem is separated from touchscreen, printing, acquisition, or power issues.

steps.title: Check AC Power and Battery State
steps.instructions: Connect the MAC VU360 to a known-good AC outlet. Confirm the device powers on normally and observe whether the display improves while connected to AC power. Expected outcome: A weak battery, low-power condition, or poor outlet connection is ruled out as the cause of reduced screen visibility. If the display returns to normal on AC power, continue checking battery condition and charging behavior before replacing display parts.

steps.title: Check Display Brightness Settings
steps.instructions: Review the device brightness setting and adjust it through the available user or system settings. Increase brightness and confirm whether the screen becomes clearly visible. Expected outcome: The issue is resolved if the brightness setting was reduced or changed unintentionally. If adjusting brightness restores normal visibility, document the setting correction and return the device to service.

steps.title: Check Screen Angle and Ambient Lighting
steps.instructions: View the screen from normal working positions used by ECG staff. Check whether overhead lighting, room glare, window reflection, or viewing angle is making the screen appear dim. Expected outcome: Environmental visibility problems are ruled out before assuming a display failure. If repositioning the device or reducing glare resolves the complaint, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Exterior Display Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the screen surface for cracks, impact marks, fluid intrusion, heavy residue, cleaning chemical damage, or protective film interference. Expected outcome: Physical or contamination-related screen visibility issues are identified. If liquid damage, cracked glass, or screen damage is found, remove the device from service and escalate for repair evaluation.

steps.title: Check for Normal Boot and Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: Power the MAC VU360 off and back on using the normal shutdown and startup process. Observe whether the GE logo, startup screen, menus, and ECG application screens appear normally. Expected outcome: The device display initializes correctly during startup. If the screen remains blank but the unit appears powered, produces sounds, or shows other signs of operation, suspect a display subsystem issue.

steps.title: Differentiate Display Visibility From Touchscreen Response
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the image is visible and whether touch response works. If the display is visible but touch does not respond correctly, handle that as a touchscreen diagnostic issue rather than a brightness issue. Expected outcome: Display visibility and touchscreen response are not combined into one failure without verification.

steps.title: Run Display Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Access the MAC VU360 diagnostic function according to site-approved service access procedures. Run Display Diagnostics. Expected outcome: Display function passes the onboard diagnostic check. If Display Diagnostics fail, do not continue clinical use. Escalate for bench evaluation of the display assembly, display cable, or display-related FRUs.

steps.title: Run Brightness Diagnostics
steps.instructions: Run Brightness Diagnostics as part of the functional checkout or diagnostic process. Confirm whether the device can control and verify screen brightness properly. Expected outcome: Brightness control passes diagnostic testing. If Brightness Diagnostics fail, suspect a display brightness control, backlight, cable, or display subsystem problem.

steps.title: Check for Flicker or Intermittent Display Behavior
steps.instructions: While the device is stationary and powered on, observe whether the display flickers, dims intermittently, or changes when the lid, housing, or device position is gently moved. Do not open the device or stress cables during basic troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Intermittent display behavior is identified before return to service. If flickering or intermittent blanking is observed, remove the device from service and escalate for repair.

steps.title: Perform a Functional Checkout After Any Correction
steps.instructions: If the issue was corrected by brightness settings, power connection, cleaning, or environmental adjustment, perform a basic functional check. Confirm the display remains readable during startup, patient entry, waveform viewing, ECG acquisition workflow, and review screens. Expected outcome: The MAC VU360 display is readable through normal ECG workflow before returning to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC VU360 display was very dim and difficult to read during ECG setup.
CCR.Cause: Brightness setting was found reduced; Display Diagnostics and Brightness Diagnostics passed after adjustment.
CCR.Resolution: Adjusted screen brightness, verified display visibility on AC power and battery, completed functional checkout, and returned the ECG machine to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether issue occurred on AC power, battery, or both
Whether screen was dim, blank, flickering, or glare-related
Any cracks, fluid damage, residue, or screen contamination

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Poor ECG waveform quality, artifact, noise, or lead-off message
description: Troubleshooting noisy ECG traces, poor waveform quality, artifact, unstable baselines, and lead-off messages before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is not being troubleshot during an active diagnostic acquisition unless clinical staff are present and the patient is stable. If waveform quality is poor during a patient ECG, have staff pause the acquisition, verify the patient is safe, and repeat the ECG only after the cause is addressed. Expected outcome: No diagnostic ECG is accepted from a setup with questionable waveform quality.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Waveform Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask the user what they are seeing. Determine whether the issue involves: Lead-off message; One lead missing; Multiple leads missing; Wandering baseline; Muscle artifact; AC noise; Intermittent waveform dropout; Poor signal only on one patient; Poor signal on all patients; Artifact after moving the cart or cable. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to patient prep, electrodes, leadwires, acquisition cable, environment, or device hardware.

steps.title: Check Patient Preparation and Electrode Placement
steps.instructions: Verify that the patient’s skin was properly prepared. Confirm that electrodes are placed correctly, skin is dry, excess hair is addressed, and the electrodes are firmly attached. Poor skin contact is one of the most common causes of ECG artifact and lead-off messages. Expected outcome: Waveforms improve after proper skin prep and electrode placement. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Electrode Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the electrodes being used with the MAC 5. Confirm they are not expired, dried out, poorly stored, or from an opened package that has lost gel quality. Replace the electrodes with a fresh known-good set. Expected outcome: Lead-off messages and noisy traces clear with fresh electrodes. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify Leadwire Connection at Each Electrode
steps.instructions: Confirm each snap, clip, or tab connection is fully seated on the electrode. Gently check each connection without pulling on the patient or cable. Expected outcome: The lead-off message clears when the loose or poorly seated connection is corrected. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Patient Cable and Leadwires
steps.instructions: Look for obvious external damage to the trunk cable, leadwire set, strain reliefs, clips, snaps, and connectors. Check for cracked insulation, bent pins, pulled wires, fluid contamination, or intermittent connection when the cable is moved. Expected outcome: Damaged or intermittent cables are identified and removed from use.

steps.title: Swap With a Known-Good Leadwire Set or Patient Cable
steps.instructions: Replace the suspect leadwire set or patient cable with a known-good compatible cable. Repeat the ECG test using fresh electrodes. Expected outcome: If waveform quality improves, the original cable or leadwire set is the likely cause. Replace the accessory and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm the Acquisition Cable Is Fully Seated at the MAC 5
steps.instructions: Check the connector between the patient cable/acquisition cable and the MAC 5. Reseat the connector if safe to do so and inspect for bent pins, looseness, debris, or damage. Expected outcome: The MAC 5 detects the leads normally and the waveform stabilizes. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check for Environmental Electrical Noise
steps.instructions: Move the MAC 5 and patient cable away from obvious electrical noise sources. Check for nearby equipment such as beds, pumps, blanket warmers, power strips, monitors, chargers, or damaged outlets. Avoid running ECG cables parallel to power cords. Expected outcome: Noise decreases when the ECG setup is moved away from interference. If resolved, document the environmental cause.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Battery Operation
steps.instructions: If artifact appears while plugged into AC power, test the MAC 5 on battery power if the battery is charged and the site procedure allows. Also try a different known-good wall outlet. Expected outcome: If noise changes between AC and battery operation, investigate outlet grounding, charger/power supply concerns, or environmental electrical noise.

steps.title: Check Patient Movement and Muscle Artifact
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient was still, relaxed, warm, and not talking during acquisition. Tremors, shivering, muscle tension, and movement can create artifact that may be mistaken for equipment failure. Expected outcome: Waveform quality improves when movement and muscle artifact are reduced.

steps.title: Test With a Simulator
steps.instructions: Connect the MAC 5 to a known-good ECG simulator using compatible cables. Run a basic rhythm or 12-lead simulation and observe waveform quality and lead status. Expected outcome: Clean simulator waveforms suggest the MAC 5 is functioning and the issue is likely patient prep, electrodes, cable, or environment.

steps.title: Compare Results Across Leads
steps.instructions: Identify whether the issue follows one lead, one group of leads, or all leads. A single bad lead often points to an electrode, leadwire, or connector issue. Noise on all leads may point to patient prep, trunk cable, acquisition module, power, or environmental interference. Expected outcome: The problem pattern helps isolate the likely fault area.

steps.title: Restart the MAC 5 if the Display or Acquisition Appears Abnormal
steps.instructions: If the waveform display is frozen, delayed, or inconsistent, power the MAC 5 down and restart it when not connected to a patient. Do not restart during active patient care unless clinical staff approve. Expected outcome: Temporary software or acquisition display issues clear after restart. If resolved, document the restart and final test result.

steps.title: Verify Final ECG Quality Before Returning to Use
steps.instructions: After corrective action, perform a test ECG or simulator check. Confirm stable baseline, clear waveform, no inappropriate lead-off messages, and acceptable print/display quality. Expected outcome: The MAC 5 is returned to service only after waveform quality is verified.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported poor ECG waveform quality and intermittent lead-off messages on the GE MAC 5 during patient testing.
CCR.Cause: Troubleshooting found dried electrodes and an intermittent RA leadwire causing unstable signal and repeated lead-off alarms.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced electrodes, swapped the defective leadwire set with a known-good cable, verified clean simulator waveform, and returned the MAC 5 to service.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or lead-off behavior noted
Accessories swapped, including patient cable or leadwire set
Power behavior, including outlet tested and battery versus AC behavior checked
Environmental factors such as nearby equipment, power strips, chargers, or electrical noise sources
Indicator lights or on-screen lead status messages

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Acquisition Module, Patient Cable, Or Leadwire Connection Fault
description: Troubleshooting MAC 5 acquisition module, patient cable, leadwire, electrode, and ECG signal connection faults before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is not actively being used to acquire a patient ECG. If the fault appears during an ECG, have clinical staff stop the acquisition, remove the patient leads safely, and use another ECG machine if the tracing is clinically needed. Expected outcome: Patient care is not continued on a device with unreliable ECG acquisition.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Connection Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask the user what they observed. Determine whether the issue involves: Acquisition module not detected; Patient cable not recognized; Lead-off message; One lead missing; Multiple leads missing; Intermittent ECG waveform; Excessive artifact; No waveform from all leads; Fault appears only when the cable is moved. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to the acquisition module, patient cable, leadwire set, electrodes, or device connection port.

steps.title: Check Electrode Placement and Skin Contact
steps.instructions: Verify that electrodes are fresh, properly placed, and making good skin contact. Replace dried, loose, expired, or poorly adhered electrodes. Expected outcome: Lead-off or noisy tracing clears if the issue was caused by poor electrode contact. If resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Leadwires
steps.instructions: Visually inspect each leadwire for: Bent clips or snaps; Broken insulation; Pulled strain reliefs; Loose connector ends; Fluid contamination; Damaged or missing labels; Intermittent signal when flexed. Expected outcome: Damaged leadwires are identified and replaced. If replacing the leadwire set resolves the issue, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check the Patient Cable Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the patient cable or leadwire assembly at the acquisition module or ECG input connection. Ensure the connector is fully seated, aligned correctly, and not forced. Expected outcome: A loose or partially seated patient cable connection is corrected. If the fault clears, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Patient Cable Connector
steps.instructions: Check the patient cable connector for bent pins, debris, corrosion, cracked housing, or signs of liquid intrusion. Do not use sharp tools or force connector pins. Expected outcome: Obvious cable connector damage is found before assuming a MAC 5 device failure.

steps.title: Swap With a Known-Good Patient Cable or Leadwire Set
steps.instructions: Replace the suspect patient cable or leadwire set with a known-good compatible set. Run a test ECG or simulator check if available. Expected outcome: If the issue follows the cable or leadwire set, replace the accessory and return the MAC 5 to service after verification.

steps.title: Check the Acquisition Module Seating and Connection
steps.instructions: If the MAC 5 uses a separate acquisition module, confirm it is properly connected, seated, charged or powered as applicable, and paired or communicating according to site configuration. Expected outcome: Communication or recognition faults caused by an improperly connected acquisition module are corrected.

steps.title: Inspect the Acquisition Module Externally
steps.instructions: Look for cracks, loose ports, worn contacts, damaged cable entry points, missing labels, or fluid contamination. Do not open the module or perform internal repair during clinical floor troubleshooting. Expected outcome: External damage or contamination is identified and the module is removed from use if unsafe.

steps.title: Check for All-Leads Versus Single-Lead Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue affects one lead, a lead group, or all ECG leads. One lead usually suggests electrode, leadwire, or patient cable issue. Multiple related leads may suggest cable, trunk cable, or acquisition module connection issue. All leads missing may suggest acquisition module, patient cable, device input, or system communication issue. Expected outcome: The failure pattern helps guide whether to replace accessories or escalate.

steps.title: Use an ECG Simulator if Available
steps.instructions: Connect a compatible ECG simulator to the patient cable or leadwire set. Verify whether the MAC 5 displays a clean waveform on all leads. Expected outcome: A clean simulator signal points toward electrode or patient setup issues. Missing or noisy leads with a simulator suggest cable, leadwire, acquisition module, or device input fault.

steps.title: Check for Artifact Caused by Movement or Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm the cable is not pulled tight, routed near power cords, wrapped around equipment, or placed near sources of electrical noise. Gently move the cable while watching the waveform. Expected outcome: Intermittent signal during movement suggests a damaged cable, leadwire, connector, or acquisition module port.

steps.title: Restart the MAC 5 if the Hardware Checks Pass
steps.instructions: If all external connections and accessories appear normal, restart the MAC 5 when it is safe to do so. Do not restart during active patient acquisition or before confirming saved ECG data is protected. Expected outcome: Temporary communication or software recognition faults clear after restart. If resolved, verify acquisition before returning to service.

steps.title: Perform a Functional ECG Acquisition Check
steps.instructions: After replacing accessories, reseating connections, or restarting the unit, perform a test acquisition using a simulator or approved facility process. Confirm all leads display correctly and the device completes ECG acquisition without lead-off or module faults. Expected outcome: The MAC 5 is verified before clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the MAC 5 displayed repeated lead-off messages and would not capture a complete resting ECG.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the RA leadwire had an intermittent connection when flexed near the snap connector.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the leadwire set, verified clean ECG waveform on all leads using an ECG simulator, and returned the MAC 5 to service.

helpfulDetails: Which lead or lead group failed
Whether the issue was intermittent or constant

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Touchscreen, Keyboard, Barcode Scanner, or User Input Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting MAC 5 touchscreen, keyboard, barcode scanner, and user input response issues before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is not actively being used on a patient. If the input issue occurs during an ECG, have clinical staff stop the acquisition if safe, disconnect the patient leads as appropriate, and use another ECG machine if the test is clinically needed. Expected outcome: Patient testing is not continued on a device with unreliable user input.

steps.title: Confirm Which Input Is Not Responding
steps.instructions: Ask the user exactly what is not working. Determine whether the issue involves: Touchscreen not responding; Touchscreen responding inaccurately; Keyboard not responding; Specific keys not working; Barcode scanner not scanning; Cursor, menu, or selection not moving; User login or patient entry not accepting input; Entire device frozen. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to touchscreen, keyboard, barcode scanner, software lockup, or general system response.

steps.title: Check for a Frozen Application or Locked Screen
steps.instructions: Look for signs that the device is frozen, such as no clock update, no menu response, no patient data entry response, or no change after repeated input. If the system appears frozen, perform a normal shutdown and restart if the device is not in active patient use. Expected outcome: If the issue clears after restart, document the freeze and return the device to service after confirming normal operation.

steps.title: Check Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is connected to a known-good AC outlet or has adequate battery charge. Low power or unstable power can cause delayed response, screen issues, or unexpected lockups. Expected outcome: Device powers normally and input response is checked under stable power.

steps.title: Inspect the Touchscreen Surface
steps.instructions: Check the screen for moisture, cleaning residue, tape, labels, cracked glass, heavy smudging, or anything pressing on the screen. Clean the touchscreen using facility-approved cleaning practices and allow it to dry fully before retesting. Expected outcome: Touch input responds normally after external contamination or obstruction is removed.

steps.title: Check Whether Touch Response Is Incorrect or Completely Absent
steps.instructions: Tap several areas of the screen and confirm whether the device responds in the correct location. If touch works only in some areas or selects the wrong item, treat it as a touchscreen accuracy or calibration-related issue and remove from service if clinical workflow is affected. Expected outcome: Touchscreen behavior is identified as normal, partially responsive, inaccurate, or failed.

steps.title: Inspect Keyboard and Physical Keys
steps.instructions: Check for stuck keys, fluid residue, cracked keycaps, debris around the keyboard, or signs of impact. Press several known-good keys and confirm whether any response appears on screen. Expected outcome: Keyboard input is confirmed functional, partially functional, or nonresponsive.

steps.title: Check for an External Accessory Conflict
steps.instructions: If any external USB device, flash drive, scanner, or accessory is connected, remove it and restart the MAC 5 if safe to do so. A faulty accessory or USB device can sometimes interfere with normal input operation. Expected outcome: If input returns after removing an accessory, keep that accessory out of service and document the finding.

steps.title: Check the Barcode Scanner Connection and Scan Target
steps.instructions: Confirm the barcode scanner is properly connected or seated, depending on the site configuration. Inspect the scanner window for dirt, damage, or obstruction. Try scanning a known-good barcode from a badge, test label, or patient label approved for testing. Expected outcome: Scanner reads a known-good barcode or the problem is narrowed to scanner, cable, barcode quality, or configuration.

steps.title: Verify Barcode Format and Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm the scanner failure is not limited to one label type. If the scanner reads some barcodes but not patient labels, involve the ECG/MUSE administrator, IT, or registration team to verify barcode format, patient ID mapping, and workflow configuration. Expected outcome: A barcode format or workflow issue is separated from a scanner hardware issue.

steps.title: Check User Login or Security State
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is not waiting for a login, locked user session, required field, or prompt that prevents normal input. Ask the user what screen they were on when the issue occurred. Expected outcome: Input is not mistaken for a device failure when the system is waiting for required workflow action.

steps.title: Restart and Perform a Functional Check
steps.instructions: After external checks, restart the device and verify: Touchscreen responds; Keyboard enters text; Barcode scanner reads a known-good barcode; Patient entry screen accepts input; ECG acquisition workflow can be navigated; No repeated lockup occurs. Expected outcome: Device passes a basic user input functional check.

steps.title: Check for Recurrence
steps.instructions: Ask whether the issue happens every time, only after long use, only with one user, only on battery, or only during a specific workflow. Expected outcome: Intermittent behavior is documented clearly for repair evaluation.

steps.title: Return to Service Only If Input Is Reliable
steps.instructions: If all input devices respond normally after troubleshooting and no repeat issue is observed, return the MAC 5 to service. If the problem returns, affects patient entry, prevents ECG acquisition, or causes unreliable operation, remove the device from service. Expected outcome: The device is only returned to clinical use when input function is dependable.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the MAC 5 touchscreen and barcode scanner were not responding during patient ECG setup.
CCR.Cause: Found touchscreen surface clean and power stable, but barcode scanner failed to read a known-good test barcode after restart.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the MAC 5 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for bench evaluation of the scanner/input subsystem.

helpfulDetails: Whether AC power or battery was used
Whether touchscreen, keyboard, barcode scanner, or all inputs failed
Whether the device was frozen or still updating
Any visible screen damage, fluid residue, or stuck keys
Whether one barcode type or all barcodes failed

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Battery Runtime, Charging, Power-On, or AC Adapter Issue
description: Troubleshooting MAC 5 battery runtime, charging, power-on, AC adapter, and external power issues before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is not being used for an active patient ECG. If the unit powers off, fails to boot, or shows low battery during patient use, have clinical staff move to another available ECG machine. Expected outcome: Patient testing is not delayed or performed on an unreliable power source.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Power Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask the operator what happened and when it occurred. Determine whether the issue involves: Unit will not power on; Unit powers on only with AC connected; Unit shuts off on battery; Battery runtime is short; Battery does not charge; Charging indicator does not appear; AC adapter not recognized; Intermittent power when the cord is moved; Unit powers on but shuts down during printing. Expected outcome: The issue is separated into battery, AC adapter, charging, power button, or internal power path behavior.

steps.title: Check for Active Physical Damage or Safety Concerns
steps.instructions: Inspect the MAC 5, AC adapter, power cord, battery area, and connector points for damage. Look for: Cracked adapter housing; Bent or loose plug; Damaged cord insulation; Burn marks; Liquid intrusion; Swollen or leaking battery; Unusual heat or odor. Expected outcome: Any unsafe power accessory or device condition is identified before further use. If damage, heat, odor, or battery swelling is found, stop troubleshooting, remove the unit from service, and escalate for repair.

steps.title: Verify the Wall Outlet
steps.instructions: Plug the AC adapter into a known working hospital-grade outlet. Avoid using a power strip during troubleshooting unless approved by site policy. Expected outcome: The MAC 5 receives power from a verified outlet. If the unit powers on normally from a different outlet, document the failed outlet location and notify Facilities.

steps.title: Confirm the Correct AC Adapter Is Being Used
steps.instructions: Verify the AC adapter matches the MAC 5 and is not borrowed from another device. Check that the adapter rating and connector type match the approved accessory for the unit. Expected outcome: The device is not being powered by an incorrect, under-rated, or incompatible adapter. If the adapter is incorrect, replace it with the correct approved adapter and retest.

steps.title: Inspect the AC Adapter Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm the adapter is fully seated at the wall outlet, power brick, and MAC 5 power input. Gently check for looseness without forcing the connector. Expected outcome: Charging or AC power status appears consistently when the adapter is connected. If the power status changes when the connector is moved, suspect a damaged adapter cable, plug, or device power input and escalate.

steps.title: Test With a Known-Good AC Adapter If Available
steps.instructions: Use a known-good approved MAC 5 AC adapter. Expected outcome: The unit powers on and indicates AC power or charging normally. If the known-good adapter resolves the issue, replace the faulty adapter and return the MAC 5 to service after functional verification.

steps.title: Check Battery Seating
steps.instructions: Power the device down safely if possible. Confirm the battery is properly installed and seated according to normal operator-accessible battery handling procedures. Expected outcome: The battery is fully seated and recognized by the device. If reseating restores battery operation, charge the battery and verify normal power-on behavior before returning the unit to service.

steps.title: Allow Adequate Charging Time
steps.instructions: Connect the MAC 5 to AC power and allow the battery to charge. The MAC 5 is designed for AC mains or battery operation, and published product information lists battery operation as supporting a minimum of 180 minutes under a defined ECG acquisition and printing use pattern. Expected outcome: Battery charge status improves and the unit remains powered on after charging. If the battery does not accept charge or runtime remains very short, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Battery Age and Use History
steps.instructions: Review equipment records, battery replacement history, and staff reports. Battery concerns are more likely if: Runtime has gradually decreased; The unit is frequently left unplugged; The device shuts off during printing; The battery has not been replaced in several years; Multiple low-battery complaints are documented. Expected outcome: A weak or aged battery is identified as a likely external replaceable cause.

steps.title: Test Battery-Only Operation
steps.instructions: After charging, disconnect AC power and power on the MAC 5 using battery power. Observe whether the unit: Powers on normally; Immediately shuts off; Shows low battery; Runs briefly then powers down; Fails during printing. Expected outcome: Battery performance is confirmed under realistic use. If the unit operates normally on AC but fails on battery, suspect a depleted or failed battery.

steps.title: Test AC-Only Operation
steps.instructions: Connect the MAC 5 to AC power and power it on. Confirm the unit boots normally, remains powered, and can perform basic ECG workflow checks without relying on battery power. Expected outcome: AC operation is stable. If the unit does not power on with a known-good adapter and known-good outlet, suspect an internal power input, charging, or power supply fault.

steps.title: Check for Charging Indicator or Battery Status Message
steps.instructions: Review the device screen or power indicator for battery and charging status. Expected outcome: The device clearly indicates AC connection, battery presence, or charging state. If the battery is installed but not recognized, or charging status never appears with a known-good adapter, remove the device from service for bench evaluation.

steps.title: Perform a Functional Power Check
steps.instructions: Once the suspected issue is corrected, confirm the MAC 5 can: Power on with AC connected; Show expected charging or AC power status; Power on using battery; Remain powered during basic operation; Print or complete a test ECG workflow if site policy allows. Expected outcome: Power and battery behavior are stable before returning the unit to service. If the device passes these checks, document the result and return it to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC 5 would not stay powered on when unplugged from AC power.
CCR.Cause: Battery-only testing confirmed the unit powered off shortly after startup, while AC operation was stable with a known-good adapter.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the failed battery, verified charging status, confirmed battery operation, and returned the MAC 5 to service.

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - LAN/WLAN or network communication failure
description: Troubleshooting MAC 5 LAN, WLAN, network, order download, ECG transmission, or connectivity failures before repair escalation.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is not actively being used to acquire a patient ECG. If the communication issue occurs after acquisition, make sure the ECG is saved locally or printed if clinically needed before restarting or changing network settings. Expected outcome: Patient ECG data is protected before troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Network Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask the user what failed and when it occurred. Determine whether the issue involves: LAN connection failure; WLAN connection failure; No network icon or poor signal; Worklist not loading; ECG not transmitting; Failed send to MUSE, PACS, EMR, or archive; Incorrect patient demographics; Device connected to network but destination unavailable; One MAC 5 affected or multiple ECG carts affected. Expected outcome: The issue is separated into local device, wired network, wireless network, destination, or configuration problem.

steps.title: Check Whether the Device Has Power and Is Fully Booted
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 powers on normally and reaches the main operating screen without boot errors. If the device is frozen, slow, or showing system errors, restart only after confirming no unsaved ECG is at risk. Expected outcome: Network troubleshooting starts from a stable operating state.

steps.title: Check LAN Cable Connection if Using Wired Network
steps.instructions: Inspect the Ethernet cable at the MAC 5 and the wall jack. Reseat both ends of the cable and check for broken clips, damaged insulation, bent connectors, or loose wall plate ports. Expected outcome: The cable is firmly connected and physically intact. If reseating the cable restores communication, document the cable connection issue and stop.

steps.title: Swap the Ethernet Cable
steps.instructions: Replace the Ethernet cable with a known-good cable. This helps rule out a damaged or intermittent patch cable before assuming a device or network failure. Expected outcome: The MAC 5 communicates normally with the known-good cable. If the replacement cable resolves the issue, remove the bad cable from use and stop.

steps.title: Test the Network Wall Jack
steps.instructions: Move the MAC 5 to a known-working network jack, or ask IT to verify the original jack. If another device works on the same jack, the jack is less likely to be the cause. Expected outcome: The problem follows either the MAC 5 or the network location. If the MAC 5 works on another jack, escalate the wall jack or network drop issue to IT.

steps.title: Confirm WLAN Is Enabled if Using Wireless Network
steps.instructions: Verify the MAC 5 is configured for wireless operation and is not accidentally set to wired-only communication. Confirm the device is in range of the expected wireless network. Expected outcome: Wireless communication is enabled and the device is within usable signal range.

steps.title: Check Wireless Signal and Location
steps.instructions: Move the MAC 5 closer to a known-good access point or to an area where other MAC 5 units communicate successfully. Avoid testing in shielded rooms, basements, elevators, storage rooms, or areas with known poor wireless coverage. Expected outcome: Wireless signal improves and communication succeeds. If communication works in another area, document a probable wireless coverage or access point issue and involve IT.

steps.title: Confirm the Correct Network Is Selected
steps.instructions: Check that the MAC 5 is attempting to connect to the correct hospital SSID or approved network profile. Incorrect SSID selection, expired credentials, or guest-network connection can prevent worklist and ECG transmission even if Wi-Fi appears connected. Expected outcome: The device is connected to the correct clinical network.

steps.title: Check IP Address and Network Status
steps.instructions: Review the device network status screen, if accessible. Look for whether the MAC 5 has a valid IP address, subnet, gateway, and DNS information. Expected outcome: The MAC 5 has a valid network address appropriate for the site. If the IP address is missing, invalid, duplicated, or outside the expected range, involve IT before changing network configuration.

steps.title: Compare Against a Known-Good MAC 5
steps.instructions: Compare the failing MAC 5 with another working MAC 5 in the same department. Check only externally verifiable items such as: Same LAN or WLAN method; Same network location; Same destination workflow; Same general configuration profile; Same send behavior; Same worklist behavior. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to one device, one location, or a broader network/destination issue.

steps.title: Check Date and Time
steps.instructions: Verify the MAC 5 date and time are reasonably correct. Incorrect date, time, or timezone can interfere with authentication, worklist queries, ECG record matching, and downstream system acceptance. Expected outcome: Device time matches site expectations.

steps.title: Confirm the Destination System Is Available
steps.instructions: Ask whether other ECG carts are successfully sending to the same destination. If multiple carts cannot send, the issue may be with MUSE, the EMR interface, DICOM destination, server, VPN, firewall, or network routing. Expected outcome: The issue is not incorrectly blamed on one MAC 5 when the destination system is unavailable.

steps.title: Check Worklist Versus ECG Send Separately
steps.instructions: Test whether the MAC 5 can retrieve orders or worklist. Then test whether a completed ECG can transmit. Worklist failure with successful send may indicate one destination or interface issue. Send failure with successful worklist may indicate a different server, port, route, or receiving-system issue. Expected outcome: The failed network function is narrowed to order retrieval, transmission, or both.

steps.title: Review Error Messages
steps.instructions: Record the exact error message displayed by the MAC 5. Note whether the error refers to network unavailable, server unavailable, authentication, timeout, failed transmission, host unreachable, or invalid destination. Expected outcome: The error message supports accurate escalation to IT, Clinical Engineering, or the vendor.

steps.title: Restart the MAC 5 Safely
steps.instructions: After confirming patient data is saved or no active patient exam is in progress, restart the MAC 5. Do not repeatedly power-cycle the device if the same failure returns. Expected outcome: Temporary communication or software session issues clear after one safe restart. If restart resolves the issue, perform a test transmission if site workflow allows, document the result, and stop.

steps.title: Check for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the LAN port, wireless antenna area if externally visible, cart housing, power connector area, and accessory connections. Look for impact damage, liquid intrusion, loose connectors, cracked plastics, unusual heat, or odor. Expected outcome: No visible damage suggests continued external troubleshooting is reasonable. If damage, heat, liquid exposure, or burning odor is found, remove the device from service.

steps.title: Coordinate With IT Before Changing Network Settings
steps.instructions: Do not guess at IP addresses, wireless credentials, certificates, ports, or destination settings. Network changes should match site-approved configuration and be coordinated with IT or the ECG system administrator. Expected outcome: The device is not misconfigured during troubleshooting.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Test Transmission
steps.instructions: If allowed by site policy, send a test ECG or known test record to the approved destination. Confirm with the receiving system or clinical staff whether the record arrived. Expected outcome: Communication is verified end-to-end, not just from the device screen. If the test transmission succeeds, return the device to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the GE MAC 5 would not send completed ECGs over WLAN to the ECG management system.
CCR.Cause: Verified the MAC 5 had poor wireless signal in the treatment area but transmitted successfully when moved near a known-good access point.
CCR.Resolution: Documented probable wireless coverage issue, notified IT, confirmed successful test transmission from a known-good location, and returned the MAC 5 to service with location limitation noted.

helpfulDetails: Whether other MAC 5 units are affected

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Error: Software Upgrade Failed
description: Troubleshooting the GE Healthcare MAC 5 Software Upgrade Failed error caused by invalid, missing, unsigned, inaccessible, or failed installation software packages.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the MAC 5 from patient use before attempting software upgrade troubleshooting. Do not perform software upgrades while the device is needed for active ECG acquisition, patient testing, or clinical workflow. Provide clinical staff with another verified ECG machine if patient testing is needed. Expected: The unit is safely unavailable for patient use during troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the displayed error is Software Upgrade Failed. Look for related upgrade failure messages such as invalid software image, missing software image, unsigned or invalid digital signature, failed file copy, failed software download, or installation failure. Observe whether the failure occurs at upgrade startup, while locating the USB or shared folder, while copying files, during digital signature validation, during installation, during reboot, or intermittently during a network upgrade. Expected: The upgrade failure is reproducible or clearly tied to a specific part of the upgrade process.

steps.title: Confirm the Device Is on Stable Power
steps.instructions: Connect the MAC 5 to AC power before retrying the upgrade. Check that the power adapter is fully seated at the device and wall outlet. Avoid performing upgrades on battery power alone. Expected: The MAC 5 remains powered and stable throughout the upgrade attempt.

steps.title: Verify the Correct Software Package
steps.instructions: Confirm the software package is intended for the GE Healthcare MAC 5. Verify that the upgrade files are the correct version supplied or approved for that device. Do not use renamed, extracted, incomplete, copied-from-another-device, or unofficial files. Expected: The upgrade source contains the correct MAC 5 software package.

steps.title: Confirm the Software Image Is Digitally Signed
steps.instructions: Verify that the software image and required digital signature files are present. Do not modify the file names, file extensions, or folder structure unless the manufacturer instructions specifically require it. Expected: The device can identify the software image and validate its digital signature.

steps.title: Check the USB Flash Drive
steps.instructions: If upgrading by USB, remove and reinsert the USB flash drive. Confirm the drive is detected by the MAC 5. Check that the software package is located where the device expects it, commonly the root directory of the USB drive when required. Try a known-good USB flash drive if detection, access, or copy errors occur. Expected: The MAC 5 detects the USB drive and can read the upgrade files.

steps.title: Check USB Access Settings
steps.instructions: If the device reports USB access denial or does not allow external storage use, review the storage or system settings. Confirm external storage access is enabled if controlled by device configuration. Expected: The MAC 5 permits access to the USB flash drive.

steps.title: Check the Shared Network Folder
steps.instructions: If upgrading through a shared path, confirm the MAC 5 is connected to the network. Verify LAN or WLAN connection status. Confirm the shared network path is enabled and configured. Check that the software image and digital signature files are present in the correct shared folder location. Expected: The MAC 5 can reach the shared folder and locate the required upgrade files.

steps.title: Verify Permissions
steps.instructions: Confirm the USB drive or shared network folder allows the MAC 5 to read and copy the software upgrade files. If using a shared network path, verify credentials and access rights. If using USB, verify the files are not locked, restricted, or corrupted. Expected: The device can copy or download the required software files without permission errors.

steps.title: Retry the Upgrade From a Known-Good Source
steps.instructions: After correcting the package, location, access, or network issue, retry the software upgrade. Use only one upgrade method at a time, such as USB upgrade with a known-good USB drive or network upgrade with a verified shared folder. Do not repeatedly retry with the same questionable package or storage device. Expected: The upgrade progresses past the previous failure point.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the upgrade completes successfully, allow the MAC 5 to fully reboot. Confirm the device starts normally. Check basic ECG machine function before returning it to service, including power-on, date and time, user interface response, acquisition screen access, printer readiness if applicable, and network connection if applicable. Expected: The MAC 5 operates normally after the software upgrade.

CCR.Complaint: User reported MAC 5 displayed Software Upgrade Failed during attempted software upgrade. Upgrade did not complete and device was removed from patient use.
CCR.Cause: Software upgrade package, USB/shared-folder location, digital signature, network access, and file permissions were checked. Failure appeared related to upgrade source/configuration or persistent internal software installation issue.
CCR.Resolution: Verified AC power, checked software package location, confirmed digitally signed upgrade files, tested USB/shared-folder access, and retried upgrade. If successful, device passed startup and functional checks and was returned to service. If unsuccessful, device was labeled Out of Service and escalated to GE HealthCare Service/bench repair.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior, including the exact displayed software upgrade error message and when it appeared during the upgrade.
Accessories swapped, including USB flash drive, AC adapter, network cable, or upgrade media tested.
Power behavior, including whether the MAC 5 was connected to AC power throughout the upgrade.
Environmental factors, including LAN/WLAN availability, shared-folder access, credentials, and storage access settings.
Indicator lights, including USB detection, charging status, network connection, and any startup behavior after reboot.
Final device status, including whether the upgrade completed, whether functional checks passed, or whether the unit was labeled Out of Service.
