Comparison to a known working MAC 5
Whether ECG export, archive, or worklist was affected

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Error: Software Image Not Found in Shared Folder
description: Troubleshooting Software Image Not Found in Shared Folder on a GE Healthcare MAC 5 when the device cannot locate a valid software image in the configured network shared path.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the MAC 5 from patient use before troubleshooting software update or software loading issues. Do not attempt software update troubleshooting while the device is needed for active ECG acquisition. Move patient ECG testing to another available ECG machine if needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the displayed message is exactly: Software Image Not Found in Shared Folder. Observe whether the error appears at startup, during a software update attempt, when accessing a shared network location, after changing network settings, or after replacing or moving software files.

steps.title: Translate the Error Into the Real-World Problem
steps.instructions: This error means the MAC 5 is looking in a configured shared folder for a software image, but it does not find a valid image file there. Likely causes include an incorrect shared folder path, missing software image, wrong file copied to the folder, invalid or unsigned software image, network access issue, permission issue, credential issue, or incorrect shared path configuration.

steps.title: Confirm the Device Is on a Stable Power Source
steps.instructions: Connect the MAC 5 to AC power before continuing. Do not perform software image checks or update-related work on battery power alone.

steps.title: Confirm Basic Network Connectivity
steps.instructions: Verify whether the MAC 5 is connected by LAN or WLAN. For LAN, confirm the Ethernet cable is fully seated, check for link or activity lights if available, and try a known-good network cable and wall jack if possible. For WLAN, confirm the device is connected to the correct wireless network, check signal strength, and move closer to an access point if the issue is intermittent.

steps.title: Verify the Shared Path
steps.instructions: Confirm the shared path entered on the MAC 5 matches the intended network location exactly. Check for an incorrect server name, wrong folder name, missing subfolder, typographical error, old share path from a previous update process, or path changed by IT or Clinical Engineering.

steps.title: Confirm the Software Image Is Actually Present
steps.instructions: From a workstation with access to the same share, open the shared folder and verify that the software image file is present. Confirm the folder is not empty and that the file was not placed in a different subfolder.

steps.title: Confirm the Software Image Is Valid and Digitally Signed
steps.instructions: Verify that the file placed in the shared folder is the correct GE Healthcare MAC 5 software image and not a renamed, incomplete, extracted, or unrelated file. Make sure the software image is valid and digitally signed as required.

steps.title: Check for File Transfer or Copy Problems
steps.instructions: If the software image was recently copied to the shared folder, confirm the file copy completed successfully. Check for partial file transfer, zero-byte file, interrupted copy, compressed archive placement, wrong version, or security software quarantine.

steps.title: Confirm Shared Folder Permissions
steps.instructions: Verify the MAC 5 or the account used by the MAC 5 has permission to access the shared folder. Confirm read permission exists, credentials are current, the password has not expired, and both share permissions and NTFS permissions allow access. Check with IT or the system administrator if needed.

steps.title: Check Whether Other Devices Can Access the Same Image
steps.instructions: If multiple MAC 5 units use the same shared software image location, test whether another MAC 5 can see the image. If another MAC 5 works from the same shared folder, the issue may be isolated to this unit’s network configuration, credentials, or local software state. If no MAC 5 can see the image, the issue is likely with the shared folder, file placement, permissions, or image validity.

steps.title: Restart and Recheck After Corrections
steps.instructions: After correcting the path, file placement, network access, or permissions, restart the MAC 5 and attempt the process again. The MAC 5 should locate the software image without displaying the error. If resolved, document the correction and return the device to service only after normal operation is confirmed.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the valid digitally signed software image is placed in the correct shared path and the MAC 5 recognizes it, no further troubleshooting is needed. Confirm the device boots normally, network settings remain correct, and ECG acquisition is available before returning it to service.

CCR.Complaint: User reported MAC 5 displays Software Image Not Found in Shared Folder during software image access or update attempt. Device could not locate update image in configured shared path.
CCR.Cause: Shared folder did not contain a valid digitally signed software image, or the device could not access the correct shared path due to path, permission, credential, or network configuration issue.
CCR.Resolution: Verified AC power, network connection, shared path, folder access, and software image placement. Confirmed valid digitally signed software image was present in the correct shared folder. Restarted device and verified error cleared. Returned device to service.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or exact error behavior
Accessories swapped, including network cable, wall jack, USB media, or workstation access path if applicable
Power behavior and whether AC power was connected during troubleshooting
Environmental factors, including network location, wireless signal strength, or recent device movement
Indicator lights, including LAN link/activity lights or wireless connection status
Final device status, including whether the error cleared, whether ECG acquisition was verified, and whether the device was returned to service or removed from service

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Error: No Network Connection
description: Troubleshooting No Network Connection on the GE Healthcare MAC 5 when LAN or WLAN communication is unavailable and worklist download, ECG transmission, archive communication, MUSE communication, or EMR communication may be affected.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is not actively being used for a patient ECG. If the device cannot transmit ECGs, worklists, or patient demographics during clinical use, make sure staff save or print the ECG locally if needed. Use another ECG machine if network communication is required for immediate clinical workflow. Expected result: Patient testing is not delayed or dependent on a device with unresolved network communication failure.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the screen displays Error: No Network Connection. Ask when the message appears, such as at startup, when opening worklist, when attempting to send ECGs, when connecting to LAN, when using WLAN, or after the device was moved. Identify the associated impact, such as no worklist download, ECGs not transmitting, MUSE or archive destination unavailable, missing network icon, missing wireless signal, or local operation without network communication. Expected result: The No Network Connection error is clearly observed or reproducible.

steps.title: Check Whether the Device Is Using LAN or WLAN
steps.instructions: Determine whether this MAC 5 is expected to connect by wired LAN, wireless WLAN, or both. Verify the correct network method is enabled in the device configuration. Expected result: The MAC 5 is configured for the connection type used in that clinical area.

steps.title: Check the Wired LAN Connection
steps.instructions: If using LAN, inspect the Ethernet cable at the MAC 5 and the wall jack. Reseat both ends of the cable. Try a known-good Ethernet cable if available. Expected result: The network connection indicator returns, or the No Network Connection error clears.

steps.title: Check the Network Wall Jack
steps.instructions: Plug the MAC 5 into a known-good network jack in the same area if available. If another MAC 5 or network device works on the original jack, the jack is less likely to be the problem. Expected result: The device connects on a known-good jack.

steps.title: Check for Link Lights or Connection Indicators
steps.instructions: Inspect the Ethernet port, cable connection, dock, or adapter area if visible. Look for link or activity lights if the hardware provides them. No link indication may suggest a bad cable, inactive wall jack, disabled switch port, or device-side network issue. Expected result: Link or activity indication appears when connected to an active network jack.

steps.title: Check Wireless Signal and Location
steps.instructions: If using WLAN, confirm the MAC 5 is in an area with known wireless coverage. Move the device to a location where another MAC 5 or approved clinical wireless device normally connects. Expected result: WLAN signal appears and the No Network Connection error clears.

steps.title: Confirm WLAN Is Enabled and Correctly Configured
steps.instructions: Verify the device is set up for the correct wireless network profile. Check for obvious configuration problems such as WLAN disabled, wrong SSID, incorrect security setting, expired or changed credentials, incorrect IP configuration, or a WLAN profile that is not valid for the current location. Expected result: The WLAN configuration matches the approved hospital network settings.

steps.title: Restart the MAC 5
steps.instructions: After saving any needed ECG data, power cycle the MAC 5. Allow the device to fully restart and attempt network reconnection. Expected result: The network connection restores after reboot if the issue was temporary.

steps.title: Check Whether the Issue Affects One Device or Many
steps.instructions: Ask whether other MAC 5 units in the same department are also offline. Compare with a known-working MAC 5 using the same LAN jack, WLAN area, or workflow. Expected result: The issue is narrowed to one device, one room, one area, or a wider network problem.

steps.title: Check Destination-Specific Communication
steps.instructions: Determine whether the MAC 5 has no network connection at all or whether it is connected but cannot reach a destination such as MUSE, worklist, archive, or EMR. Separate a true No Network Connection condition from a server unavailable, destination rejected, or order/worklist problem. Expected result: The error is confirmed as a network connection failure, not only a failed send destination.

steps.title: Verify Device Configuration With Site Standards
steps.instructions: Compare the MAC 5 network settings against approved site configuration. Confirm settings such as IP address method, static IP or DHCP, gateway, subnet, DNS, WLAN profile, destination settings, and device location or department assignment. Expected result: Device settings match the hospital’s approved MAC 5 configuration.

steps.title: Check for Recent Changes
steps.instructions: Ask whether the device was recently moved, taken offsite, reconfigured, repaired, connected to a different network jack, or affected by IT or vendor network changes. Correct any change that appears related to the network failure. Expected result: Any recent change is identified and corrected if related.

steps.title: Isolate External Versus Device-Related Failure
steps.instructions: If the MAC 5 fails on multiple known-good LAN jacks or cannot connect to WLAN in a known-good coverage area, suspect a device-side issue. If another MAC 5 also fails on the same jack or in the same wireless area, escalate to IT or network support. Expected result: The problem is narrowed to network infrastructure, configuration, or device hardware/software.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If reconnecting LAN, correcting WLAN configuration, moving to a known-good network area, or restarting the device clears the error, confirm normal operation. Test the appropriate workflow, such as worklist download, ECG send, archive transmission, or network status indication. Return the device to service only after successful communication is confirmed.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare MAC 5 displays No Network Connection. User reports device cannot connect to the network and ECGs/worklist communication are unavailable.
CCR.Cause: LAN/WLAN connection issue confirmed. External network cable, wall jack, wireless coverage, and device network configuration checked. Fault resolved after reconnecting/configuring network, or persistent fault indicates likely device-side network/configuration issue requiring further evaluation.
CCR.Resolution: Verified reported error, inspected LAN/WLAN connection, reseated or replaced network cable, checked known-good network jack or wireless area, confirmed network configuration, restarted device, and tested ECG transmission/worklist communication. Device returned to service after successful network connection, or removed from service and escalated for repair/network support.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior, including the exact error displayed and when No Network Connection appears.
Accessories swapped, including Ethernet cable, adapter, dock connection, or other external network accessory.
Power behavior, including whether a restart was performed and whether the error returned after reboot.
Environmental factors, including device location, WLAN coverage, network jack used, recent move, offsite use, or department change.
Indicator lights, including Ethernet link lights, network icon status, WLAN signal status, or other connection indicators.
Final device status, including whether worklist download, ECG send, archive transmission, or network connection test passed before return to service.

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Error: Failed to Download Digital Signature
description: Troubleshooting Failed to Download Digital Signature when the GE Healthcare MAC 5 cannot find or access the required digital signature file in the configured network shared path during a software image download or update workflow.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the MAC 5 from patient use before troubleshooting software download, signature, update, configuration, or network file access issues. Do not continue software loading or update attempts while the unit is needed for active patient ECG acquisition. Move patient ECG testing to another available ECG machine if needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact message displayed is: Failed to Download Digital Signature. Determine whether the error appears during software update, startup, network configuration, shared network access, or after a software image was placed on a server or shared folder.

steps.title: Confirm Network Connection
steps.instructions: Check whether the MAC 5 is connected to the hospital network by LAN or WLAN. For LAN, confirm the Ethernet cable is fully seated, the network jack is active, link lights are present if visible, and the cable is not damaged. For WLAN, confirm wireless is enabled, signal strength is acceptable, the correct wireless profile is selected, and the device is connected to the expected network.

steps.title: Verify the Network Shared Path
steps.instructions: Confirm the network shared path entered in the MAC 5 configuration is correct. Check for a misspelled server name, wrong folder name, incorrect slash direction or path format, changed server share name, retired server path, extra spaces, or extra characters.

steps.title: Confirm the Digital Signature File Is Present
steps.instructions: Using an approved workstation or administrator access, verify that the network shared folder contains the required digital signature file. Confirm the expected digital signature file is present in the same required location as the software image or in the manufacturer-specified folder structure.

steps.title: Confirm the Software Image Is the Correct Version
steps.instructions: Verify that the software image placed in the shared folder is intended for the GE Healthcare MAC 5. Confirm the image is not an incomplete, renamed, extracted, or partially copied file set. Check that the image came from an approved GE source and that the signature file belongs to the same software image.

steps.title: Check Shared Folder Permissions
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 has permission to access the shared path. Check read permissions, network credentials, domain or local account access, firewall restrictions, server access restrictions, recent password changes, share permissions, and folder permissions.

steps.title: Test Access From Another Device
steps.instructions: From a networked computer on the same clinical or biomedical network segment, attempt to access the shared path. Confirm that the folder opens and the signed software image file set is visible.

steps.title: Retry the Download After Correcting the File Path or File Set
steps.instructions: After confirming the correct signed software image and digital signature file are present, retry the download or update process. Confirm the digital signature download completes without the error.

steps.title: Verify Final Device Function
steps.instructions: Confirm startup completes without the error. Confirm no related software download, image, network, or signature errors return. Verify the ECG acquisition screen opens normally. Check that date, time, and network status are correct. Complete a test ECG or functional check per site procedure before returning the unit to service.

CCR.Complaint: GE Healthcare MAC 5 displayed Failed to Download Digital Signature during software/network download attempt. Device could not locate the required digital signature file from the configured network shared path.
CCR.Cause: Digital signature file was missing from the network shared path, or the device could not access the correct signed software image file set due to path, permissions, or network share issue.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from patient use. Verified network connection and shared path. Confirmed signed software image and digital signature file placement. Corrected file/path access issue and retried download. Device completed download without error and passed functional check.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or exact error behavior
Accessories swapped, including Ethernet cable or network jack if applicable
Power behavior during startup, download, or software update attempt

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Error: Installation of Software Image Unsuccessful
description: Troubleshooting the GE Healthcare MAC 5 Installation of Software Image Unsuccessful error when the device fails to extract the software image to the inactive partition during a shared network software upgrade.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the MAC 5 from patient use before troubleshooting or retrying the software upgrade. Do not perform software upgrades while the device is connected to a patient or needed for active ECG acquisition. Move ECG testing to another available machine if clinical testing is required.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact displayed message is Installation of Software Image Unsuccessful. Ask when the error appeared: during software upgrade, while using a shared network location, during extraction of the software image, after download or file selection, or after a reboot or upgrade attempt.

steps.title: Translate the Error Into the Real-World Failure
steps.instructions: This error means the MAC 5 could not successfully extract the software image to the inactive software partition during the upgrade. In practical terms, the device is seeing the upgrade file but cannot complete the installation process from the current source.

steps.title: Stop Using the Shared Network Upgrade Source
steps.instructions: Do not keep retrying the same upgrade from the same shared network path. Network interruptions, permissions, file access problems, slow transfer, or incomplete reads can prevent successful extraction.

steps.title: Verify the Software Image Is Valid
steps.instructions: Confirm the software image is the correct version and intended for the GE Healthcare MAC 5. Check that the file was fully downloaded or copied and was not renamed, partially transferred, modified, or mixed with unrelated upgrade files.

steps.title: Prepare a USB Flash Drive
steps.instructions: Use a clean USB flash drive approved by site policy. Copy the valid software image directly to the USB flash drive. Avoid using a USB drive that contains unrelated files, multiple software images, questionable formatting, or old upgrade packages.

steps.title: Retry the Software Upgrade From USB
steps.instructions: Insert the USB flash drive into the MAC 5. Retry the software upgrade using the USB copy of the valid software image. Do not remove power or USB media during the upgrade process.

steps.title: Check Power Stability During the Upgrade
steps.instructions: Connect the MAC 5 to reliable AC power before retrying the upgrade. Confirm the AC adapter is connected securely and the unit is not relying only on battery power.

steps.title: Check the USB Port and Media Recognition
steps.instructions: If the device does not detect the USB drive or image file, try a different known-good USB flash drive. Inspect the USB port for obvious physical damage, looseness, contamination, or poor fit.

steps.title: Confirm the Error Does Not Return After Successful Upgrade
steps.instructions: After the upgrade completes, restart the MAC 5 and verify normal boot. Confirm there is no software image installation error on startup. Open ECG acquisition and verify basic device operation.

CCR.Complaint: User reported GE Healthcare MAC 5 displayed Installation of Software Image Unsuccessful during software upgrade from a shared network location.
CCR.Cause: Software image installation failed during extraction to the inactive partition while using a shared network source. Shared network upgrade source was ruled out by preparing a valid software image on USB media.
CCR.Resolution: Removed MAC 5 from patient use, verified reported error, copied valid software image to USB flash drive, retried upgrade from USB, confirmed successful upgrade, restarted device, and verified normal boot and basic ECG operation.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or exact error message displayed
Accessories swapped, including USB flash drive or network cable if applicable
Power behavior, including whether AC power was connected during the upgrade
Environmental factors, including network share availability or interruption
Indicator lights or USB detection behavior
Final device status, including software version and whether the device was returned to service or removed for repair

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5 Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Error: Printer Error. Door Is Open.
description: Troubleshooting the MAC 5 Printer Error. Door Is Open. message during Writer Diagnostics or printing when verifying printer door sensor function and printer door closure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Confirm the MAC 5 is not being used for an active patient ECG. If the printer issue occurs during clinical use, have staff save or repeat the ECG on another available machine if printing is needed for patient care. Expected: The device is removed from active patient use before troubleshooting. Why it matters: A printer door or printer sensor issue can prevent reliable ECG printout generation.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Error and Behavior
steps.instructions: Enter or observe the MAC 5 during Writer Diagnostics. Confirm the exact message: Printer Error. Door Is Open. Note whether the message appears only during diagnostics, during startup, during printing, or intermittently during normal use. Expected: The error is clearly observed and tied to the printer door condition. Why it matters: This confirms whether the message is a normal diagnostic response or a true printer door sensing problem.

steps.title: Open the Printer Door During Writer Diagnostics
steps.instructions: While in Writer Diagnostics, open the printer door. Watch the diagnostic screen for the message: Printer Error. Door Is Open. Expected: The message appears when the printer door is open. Why it matters: If the door is open and the message appears, the printer door sensor test passes.

steps.title: Close the Printer Door
steps.instructions: Close the printer door fully and confirm it latches correctly. Verify the error message clears. Expected: The Printer Error. Door Is Open. message clears after the door is fully closed. Why it matters: This confirms the system recognizes the door closed condition.

steps.title: Inspect the Printer Door for Simple External Causes
steps.instructions: Check for anything preventing the door from closing completely. Look for paper not seated correctly, a crooked paper roll, debris near the latch area, a damaged hinge or latch, a warped or loose printer door, or foreign material around the sensor area. Correct any obvious obstruction and close the door again. Expected: The door closes flush and the message clears. Why it matters: A mechanical closure issue can mimic a failed door sensor.

steps.title: Check Printer Paper Loading
steps.instructions: Open the printer compartment and verify the paper is installed correctly. Make sure the paper is not pinched, folded, oversized, or interfering with the printer door. Close the door firmly. Expected: The printer door closes normally without pressure or misalignment. Why it matters: Incorrect paper loading is a common external cause of printer door errors.

steps.title: Repeat the Diagnostic Door Sensor Test
steps.instructions: Open the printer door again during Writer Diagnostics. Confirm the message appears. Close the printer door again. Confirm the message clears. Expected: The error appears when open and clears when closed. Why it matters: This confirms the printer door sensor responds correctly in both states.

steps.title: Determine Whether the Condition Is Sensor-Related or Door-Closure Related
steps.instructions: If the door is open and the message appears, the sensor test passes. If the door is open and the message does not appear, the printer door sensor test fails. If the door is closed and the message remains, inspect again for poor closure, latch damage, or obstruction. Expected: The issue is narrowed to normal diagnostic behavior, mechanical door closure, or likely sensor failure.

steps.title: Stop When Resolved
steps.instructions: If the message appears when the door is open and clears when the door is closed, no repair is needed. Return the MAC 5 to service after confirming printer operation if clinically required. Expected: Printer door status is detected correctly and the ECG machine is usable.

CCR.Complaint: User reported MAC 5 displayed Printer Error. Door Is Open. during Writer Diagnostics or printer testing.
CCR.Cause: Printer door diagnostic response verified. Message appeared when printer door was opened and cleared when door was closed. Printer door sensor test passed.
CCR.Resolution: Opened printer door during Writer Diagnostics and confirmed Printer Error. Door Is Open. appeared. Closed printer door and confirmed message cleared. Checked printer door closure and paper loading. Device returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior, including whether the message appeared with the printer door open and cleared with the printer door closed
Accessories swapped, including printer paper roll or approved paper supply if replaced
Power behavior, including whether the error appeared at startup, during diagnostics, or during printing
Environmental factors, including debris, foreign material, paper storage condition, or damage around the printer compartment
Indicator lights or on-screen diagnostic messages observed during Writer Diagnostics
Final device status, including whether the MAC 5 was returned to service or removed from service for repair

title: GE Healthcare Avance Anesthesia Machine - System Checkout or Leak Test Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed checkout or leak testing caused by circuit connections, breathing-system assembly, vaporizers, absorbers, sampling components, or test setup.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform a system checkout, leak test, or extended troubleshooting while the Avance is connected to an active patient. If a leak or checkout failure occurs during clinical use: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Transfer ventilation and anesthesia delivery to another verified anesthesia machine or approved backup method. Maintain independent patient monitoring. Follow the facility’s anesthesia-equipment failure procedure. Expected: Patient care is no longer dependent on equipment with an unresolved leak or checkout failure. If the device is safely removed from patient use, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Test Failure
steps.instructions: Review the displayed checkout results and record: The specific test that failed; any displayed leak value; whether the failure involves the machine, breathing circuit, or vaporizer; whether the failure occurs consistently or intermittently; any accompanying alarm or advisory message. The Avance low-pressure leak check evaluates the gas path before the breathing system, while other checkout portions evaluate the breathing circuit and ventilation system. Expected: The failed portion of the checkout is clearly identified before components are disturbed.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that: No patient is connected. The machine is in the required checkout or standby condition. The breathing circuit is configured as instructed by the checkout prompts. The circuit outlet or patient connection is properly occluded when requested. The reservoir bag and test lung are connected only when required. Fresh-gas controls and vaporizers are positioned as directed by the screen. An incorrect setup can create a failure even when the machine is functioning normally. Expected: The checkout is repeated using the correct configuration. If the test passes, document the setup error and return the device to service after completing the full checkout.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check the inspiratory and expiratory limbs for: Loose connections; cracked tubing; damaged cuffs; open sampling ports; missing plugs or caps; incorrectly installed filters, adapters, or elbows; water traps or accessories that are not fully seated. Replace questionable disposable components with known-good compatible items. Expected: The breathing circuit is complete, securely connected, and free of visible damage. Repeat the failed test. If it passes, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Check the Patient Y-Piece and Test Occlusion
steps.instructions: Inspect the Y-piece and the device used to occlude the patient connection. Confirm that: The Y-piece is not cracked. The occlusion plug seals completely. No small monitoring port remains open. The test plug is the correct size and is undamaged. GE identifies properly sized, undamaged plugs as necessary for isolating breathing-system sections during leak testing. Expected: The patient connection remains completely sealed during the test.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Bag, Bag Hose, and Bag/Vent Connections
steps.instructions: Check: Reservoir bag for pinholes, splits, or a loose neck; bag hose for cracks or loose fittings; bag arm connection; bag/vent switch position; manual breathing-system components for incomplete seating. Substitute a known-good reservoir bag and hose when available. Expected: The manual breathing path is securely assembled and does not introduce leakage. Repeat the checkout. If the test passes, replace the failed accessory and stop.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Breathing-System Module Is Fully Seated
steps.instructions: Inspect the externally removable breathing-system assembly. Confirm that: The module is fully inserted and latched. No tubing or cable obstructs its seating. Accessible seals are present, clean, and undamaged. The inspiratory and expiratory flow-sensor areas are correctly assembled. The adjustable pressure-limiting valve and breathing-system controls move normally. Do not force the assembly or remove internal covers. Expected: The breathing system sits flush and locks securely into position.

steps.title: 8. Check the Absorber Canister Assembly
steps.instructions: Inspect the carbon-dioxide absorber assembly for: Canister not fully locked; loose disposable absorber; cracked canister; missing or damaged accessible seal; debris on the sealing surface; incorrectly assembled bypass or condenser components, if equipped; excessive moisture around the mounting area. Reseat the absorber according to normal operator-accessible procedures. Expected: The absorber is securely installed with clean, intact sealing surfaces. Repeat the leak test. If the test passes, document the seating or absorber issue.

steps.title: 9. Inspect Sampling and Gas-Monitoring Connections
steps.instructions: Check the gas-sampling path for: Loose sample line; cracked sample tubing; open sampling connection; water trap not fully inserted; damaged water-trap seal; incorrectly connected scavenging or exhaust tubing; unsupported accessories creating tension on fittings. Temporarily replace suspect sampling accessories with known-good compatible parts. Expected: All gas-monitoring connections are secure and properly sealed.

steps.title: 10. Inspect Vaporizers and Mounting Positions
steps.instructions: Ensure all installed vaporizers are: Approved for the machine; fully seated on the manifold; locked into position; turned off for checkout when instructed; free from obvious mounting damage; not tilted, loose, or overfilled. If permitted by facility procedure, remove and reseat one vaporizer at a time while the machine is out of service. Repeat the appropriate test after each change. Do not open or internally service a vaporizer. The machine checkout may identify leakage within the vaporizer or low-pressure gas path before the breathing system. Expected: Vaporizers are securely mounted and do not cause the test failure.

steps.title: 11. Check External Gas and Auxiliary Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible connections for: Auxiliary common gas outlet not fully closed or connected; open auxiliary oxygen outlet; loose pipeline hoses; cylinder yokes not correctly secured; missing cylinder washers; external accessories connected to the fresh-gas path; damaged externally visible fittings. Use a known-good pipeline source when a supply problem is suspected. Expected: External gas connections are secure and are not creating an unintended leak path.

steps.title: 12. Power-Cycle and Repeat the Full Checkout
steps.instructions: After correcting any external issue: Turn the machine off using the normal shutdown process. Wait for shutdown to complete. Restart the Avance. Allow initialization to finish. Perform the complete manufacturer-directed checkout. Do not bypass or accept a failed mandatory checkout solely because ventilation appears functional. Expected: All required checkout tests pass without recurring messages or abnormal leakage. If the checkout passes repeatedly, complete a functional verification and return the device to service according to facility policy.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GE Healthcare Avance failed the pre-use system checkout with a breathing-system leak message.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the absorber canister was not fully seated, creating leakage during the checkout.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and locked the absorber canister, inspected the circuit connections, and completed the full system checkout successfully.

helpfulDetails: Reservoir bag and bag hose tested
Sampling line and water trap condition
Test plug or occlusion method verified

title: GE Healthcare Avance Anesthesia Machine - Flow Sensor Calibration Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed flow-sensor calibration caused by improper removal, moisture, contamination, incorrect installation, damaged sensors, or breathing-system connection problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not calibrate, remove, or exchange flow sensors while the Avance is supporting an active patient. If the failure occurs during clinical use: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Confirm that ventilation, airway pressure, and volume monitoring remain clinically reliable. Transfer the patient to another verified anesthesia machine or approved ventilation method when measurement accuracy is uncertain. Troubleshoot the affected machine only after it is safely removed from patient use. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on equipment with questionable flow or volume measurement.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Record the complete displayed message and determine whether the failure involves: Inspiratory flow sensor; Expiratory flow sensor; Both flow sensors; Calibration that will not begin; Calibration that starts but does not complete; Unstable or implausible volume readings after calibration. Expected outcome: The affected sensor and failure behavior are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Machine Is in the Correct State
steps.instructions: Place the Avance in Standby and ensure that no patient is connected. Access the flow-sensor calibration through the applicable calibration menu for the installed software version. Follow the on-screen instructions exactly. GE guidance specifies that the sensors are removed from the breathing system during routine flow calibration. Expected outcome: The system accepts the calibration request and displays the required preparation steps.

steps.title: 4. Remove Both Flow Sensors as Directed
steps.instructions: Remove the inspiratory and expiratory flow sensors from their installed positions before starting calibration. Confirm that: Both sensors are fully removed. No sensor remains partially engaged. The sensor ports are not blocked. The breathing-system components are not pressing against the sensor connectors. Expected outcome: The machine recognizes the zero-flow condition required for calibration. If calibration completes successfully, reinstall the sensors correctly, perform the required checkout, and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Moisture or Condensation
steps.instructions: Examine both sensors for: Water droplets; Condensation; Residual cleaning solution; Moisture inside the sensing channels; Wet connector areas. Allow the sensors to dry completely according to facility and manufacturer-approved handling procedures. Do not use unapproved heat, compressed air, or objects inside the sensing passages. Expected outcome: Both sensors are clean and completely dry before another calibration attempt.

steps.title: 6. Inspect for Contamination or Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Visually inspect each sensor for: Dust or debris; Secretion residue; Cracked housing; Warped sensing surfaces; Damaged electrical contacts; Bent, recessed, or contaminated connection points. Do not scrape or probe the sensing elements. Expected outcome: Only clean, undamaged sensors remain in use. Remove any visibly damaged sensor from service.

steps.title: 7. Check Sensor Identification and Placement
steps.instructions: Confirm that the inspiratory and expiratory sensors are installed in their correct locations and orientations. Check that: Each sensor matches the approved type for the Avance. Directional markings are followed. The sensors are fully seated. Latches or retaining mechanisms engage normally. No tubing or breathing-system component prevents full insertion. Expected outcome: Both sensors are correctly positioned and recognized by the system.

steps.title: 8. Reseat the Breathing-System Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect and reseat the accessible breathing-system assembly around the flow sensors. Look for: Loose sensor-module connections; Misaligned seals; Improperly installed breathing-system components; Damaged or missing accessible seals; Components installed after cleaning in the wrong orientation. Expected outcome: The breathing system is completely and correctly assembled without stressing the sensors.

steps.title: 9. Repeat the Flow-Sensor Calibration
steps.instructions: Remove the sensors again when instructed and repeat the calibration. Do not move the machine, disturb the sensor ports, or create airflow near the open sensor locations while calibration is running. Expected outcome: Calibration completes without an error message. If successful: Reinstall both sensors. Complete the required machine checkout. Verify stable inspiratory and expiratory volume readings using an appropriate test lung or analyzer. Return the machine to service only after all tests pass.

steps.title: 10. Test With Known-Good Sensors
steps.instructions: When permitted by facility policy, install a compatible, known-good pair of GE-approved flow sensors and repeat calibration. GE describes these sensors as critical to accurate airway-flow and ventilation measurement. If calibration succeeds, the original sensor or sensor pair is defective or out of specification. If calibration still fails, the problem may involve the sensor interface, wiring, breathing-system electronics, or internal measurement circuitry. Expected outcome: The test distinguishes a sensor problem from a machine-side fault.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Complete Checkout
steps.instructions: After any sensor replacement, reseating, or successful calibration, complete the manufacturer-required pre-use checkout. Verify: Flow-sensor calibration passes; Leak testing passes; Inspiratory and expiratory volumes are stable; Delivered and measured tidal volumes are reasonably consistent; No flow-sensor alarms return; Mechanical and manual ventilation operate correctly. Expected outcome: The machine passes all required functional and safety checks before clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia staff reported that the GE Avance displayed a flow-sensor calibration failure and would not provide reliable volume measurements.
CCR.Cause: The expiratory flow sensor contained visible condensation and failed calibration until it was dried and correctly reseated.
CCR.Resolution: Dried and reinstalled both flow sensors, completed flow calibration and machine checkout, verified stable volumes with a test lung, and returned the Avance to service.

helpfulDetails: Inspiratory, expiratory, or both sensors affected

title: GE Healthcare Avance Anesthesia Machine - O2 Sensor Calibration or FiO2 Measurement Error
description: Troubleshooting failed oxygen-sensor calibration, inaccurate inspired-oxygen readings, unstable FiO2 values, or oxygen-monitoring errors caused by setup, gas supply, sampling, or sensor issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not calibrate or troubleshoot the oxygen-monitoring system while the Avance is supporting an active patient. If the displayed FiO2 is missing, unstable, or inconsistent with the selected gas mixture: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Use an approved independent oxygen analyzer. Transfer the patient to another verified anesthesia machine when reliable oxygen monitoring cannot be confirmed. Follow the facility’s anesthesia-machine failure procedure. Expected: Patient care no longer depends on equipment with questionable oxygen measurement. If the patient is safely supported elsewhere, continue troubleshooting in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Review the reported message and determine whether the problem involves: O2 sensor calibration failure; Calibration required; FiO2 reading higher or lower than expected; FiO2 value drifting or fluctuating; Missing oxygen reading; Reading that does not respond to changes in oxygen concentration. Record the complete displayed message and the conditions present when it occurred. Expected: The failure is clearly identified before components or settings are changed.

steps.title: Allow the System to Complete Startup
steps.instructions: Power the Avance on using a verified electrical outlet and allow it to complete its normal startup sequence. Do not attempt calibration while the system is still initializing or displaying unresolved startup alarms. Expected: The machine completes startup without unrelated power, gas-supply, or system-check errors. If a broader startup or system failure is present, troubleshoot that condition before evaluating the oxygen sensor.

steps.title: Verify the Medical-Gas Supplies
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The oxygen pipeline hose is securely connected. The wall outlet is supplying oxygen. The pipeline-pressure indication is within the facility’s acceptable range. Backup oxygen-cylinder pressure is adequate. Air and nitrous-oxide hoses are connected to the correct indexed outlets. No gas-supply alarms are active. Use an approved independent method to verify the gas source when the pipeline supply is questionable. Expected: The Avance has stable and correctly connected medical-gas supplies. If correcting the supply resolves the FiO2 error, complete an operational check and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Breathing System
steps.instructions: Check the accessible breathing-system components for: Loose inspiratory or expiratory connections; Incorrectly installed breathing circuit; Open sampling ports; Disconnected reservoir bag; Improperly seated absorber canister; Damaged hoses or fittings; Excessive leakage; Incorrect auxiliary gas outlet configuration. A significant leak or incorrect circuit configuration can prevent a stable oxygen concentration from reaching the measurement system. Expected: The breathing system is correctly assembled and free of obvious external leaks. If correcting the circuit resolves the reading, complete the required system test and stop.

steps.title: Check the Gas-Sampling Path
steps.instructions: Inspect the external sampling components, when equipped, including: Sample line connections; Water trap installation; Water trap fill level; Kinked or occluded tubing; Moisture or contamination; Loose connections at the patient circuit and gas module; Exhaust or scavenging tubing that may be restricted. Replace suspect disposable sampling components with compatible, known-good items. Expected: Gas can travel through the sampling path without leakage, moisture blockage, or restriction. If the FiO2 reading becomes stable after replacing a sampling component, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Accessible O2 Sensor Components
steps.instructions: With the machine removed from clinical use, inspect the externally accessible oxygen-sensor location and connections. Check for: Loose or partially seated sensor; Damaged connector or cable; Moisture around the sensor; Contamination; Cracked housing; Bent or damaged contacts; Incorrect or incompatible replacement sensor; Sensor installation that does not match the device configuration. Do not open sealed sensor assemblies or perform internal board-level work. Expected: The oxygen sensor and its accessible connections are clean, dry, compatible, and securely installed. If reseating an approved accessible connection resolves the problem, repeat the operational check and stop.

steps.title: Confirm Calibration Conditions
steps.instructions: Place the machine in the required nonclinical operating condition and ensure the sensor is exposed to the correct calibration gas environment. Before starting calibration: Remove the machine from patient use. Confirm stable gas supplies. Allow the oxygen reading to stabilize. Ensure the breathing and sampling systems are correctly configured. Prevent residual high-oxygen mixtures or anesthetic gas from affecting the calibration environment. Follow the facility-approved procedure and the applicable GE Healthcare instructions for the installed software and sensor configuration. Expected: Calibration is attempted only after the measurement environment is stable and known. The Avance uses oxygen monitoring as part of its gas-measurement system, so inaccurate calibration conditions can produce an incorrect displayed value.

steps.title: Perform the Approved O2 Sensor Calibration
steps.instructions: Run the user-accessible oxygen-sensor calibration from the normal calibration or checkout menu. Observe whether the calibration: Completes successfully; Times out; Produces an unstable-value message; Reports a sensor failure; Returns immediately to calibration required. Do not repeatedly recalibrate a sensor that continues to fail under verified conditions. Expected: Calibration completes and the displayed oxygen value stabilizes at an appropriate reading for the test gas. If calibration succeeds, continue to functional verification.

steps.title: Compare the Reading With an Independent Analyzer
steps.instructions: Connect a calibrated external oxygen analyzer using an approved test setup. Test the Avance with controlled oxygen concentrations appropriate for the facility’s verification procedure. Compare the machine’s displayed FiO2 with the independent analyzer after both readings stabilize. Expected: The Avance reading tracks changes in oxygen concentration and remains within the manufacturer’s applicable tolerance. If the machine reading is inaccurate while the independent analyzer remains stable, suspect a deteriorated sensor, gas-module problem, connection fault, or internal measurement failure.

steps.title: Substitute Approved External Components
steps.instructions: When permitted by facility policy, substitute one external component at a time: Known-good compatible oxygen sensor; Known-good sample line; Known-good water trap; Known-good gas-analysis module, if externally interchangeable; Known-good breathing circuit. Repeat calibration or verification after each substitution. Expected: The defective external component is isolated without unnecessary internal disassembly. If a known-good oxygen sensor calibrates and measures correctly, replace the original sensor and document the result.

steps.title: Complete Final Operational Verification
steps.instructions: After calibration or component replacement: Run the required system checkout. Confirm the oxygen reading is present and stable. Change the delivered oxygen concentration and verify that the displayed FiO2 responds appropriately. Confirm oxygen alarms activate as expected using the facility-approved test method. Verify there are no active gas-monitoring or calibration messages. Compare the displayed value with an independent calibrated oxygen analyzer. Expected: The Avance passes checkout and provides stable, credible oxygen measurement before being returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia staff reported that the GE Healthcare Avance displayed an O2 sensor calibration failure and an unstable FiO2 reading.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found moisture in the gas-sampling water trap and a restricted sample line, preventing stable oxygen measurement during calibration.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the water trap and sample line, completed O2 sensor calibration, verified the reading against a calibrated external oxygen analyzer, and returned the machine to service.

helpfulDetails: O2 sensor age or replacement date
Sample line and water trap condition
FiO2 response at different oxygen concentrations
Unusual heat, sound, odor, or moisture

title: GE Healthcare Avance Anesthesia Machine - Gas Module Not Recognized or Gas Measurement Unavailable
description: Troubleshooting unavailable respiratory-gas measurements caused by module seating, sampling components, moisture, blockage, configuration, power, or communication problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not remove, exchange, or troubleshoot the gas module while the Avance is actively supporting a patient unless directed by the anesthesia provider under an approved backup-monitoring plan. If inspired or expired O2, CO2, N2O, or anesthetic-agent measurements are unavailable during a procedure: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Establish approved independent gas and patient monitoring. Move the patient to another verified anesthesia machine when clinically appropriate. Do not rely on estimated gas concentrations. Expected: Patient care continues with verified ventilation and respiratory-gas monitoring. The Avance airway module measures gases delivered to and exhaled by the patient, making loss of these measurements clinically significant. If patient safety and alternate monitoring are established, continue troubleshooting off patient.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Condition
steps.instructions: Record the complete displayed message and determine what information is unavailable: Entire gas module not recognized. No CO2 waveform or value. Inspired or expired O2 unavailable. Anesthetic-agent identification unavailable. N2O measurement unavailable. Sampling or water-trap alarm. Values appear briefly and then disappear. Check whether ventilation pressure, flow, and volume measurements remain available. Expected: The failure is narrowed to module recognition, a specific gas measurement, or the sampling pathway.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Gas Module Installation
steps.instructions: Verify that the compact airway or respiratory gas module is: Installed in the correct module slot. Fully inserted. Straight and securely seated. Free from visible damage. Not partially released from the module rack. Remove and reseat the module only when the machine is not being used on a patient and according to facility procedures. Expected: The module seats completely and is detected by the Avance. If recognition returns and gas measurements stabilize, complete an operational verification and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Module and Slot Contacts
steps.instructions: Remove the module and inspect the exterior connector area and module slot for: Moisture. Dust or residue. Bent or damaged contacts. Cracked housing. Foreign material. Signs of liquid intrusion. Do not insert tools, sprays, or cleaning fluids into the module slot. Clean only accessible external surfaces using approved methods. Expected: The module and slot are dry, clean, and visibly undamaged. If contamination, liquid intrusion, or damaged contacts are present, remove the device or module from service and escalate for repair.

steps.title: 5. Check the Water Trap
steps.instructions: Inspect the gas-module water trap for: Full or excessive collected fluid. Cracks. Loose installation. Incorrect water-trap type. Contaminated filter membrane. Damaged seals. Evidence of fluid passing beyond the trap. Empty or replace the water trap according to facility policy and the applicable manufacturer instructions. Expected: A compatible, dry water trap is securely installed and the sampling pathway is protected from moisture. If measurements return after correcting the water trap, allow readings to stabilize and stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Sampling Line
steps.instructions: Trace the complete sample line from the patient circuit to the gas module. Check for: Disconnection. Loose fittings. Kinks. Compression beneath equipment. Condensation. Internal blockage. Cracks or leaks. Incorrect tubing. Contaminated patient-end connector. Replace the sample line with a known-good compatible line when damage or restriction is suspected. Expected: The sample line is open, dry, correctly connected, and leak-free. If the gas waveform and measurements return, verify stable operation and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check the Patient Sampling Connection
steps.instructions: Verify that the sample line is connected to the correct sampling port near the patient airway. Inspect the airway adapter or circuit sampling connector for: Secretions. Condensation. Occlusion. Incorrect orientation. Loose connection. Damage. Do not test using a contaminated clinical circuit. Expected: Gas can move freely from the breathing circuit through the sampling line to the module.

steps.title: 8. Allow the Module to Complete Startup
steps.instructions: After reseating or replacing the module, allow sufficient time for: Module recognition. Internal initialization. Sensor warm-up. Automatic zeroing. Agent identification. Observe for messages indicating warming, zeroing, calibration, or temporary measurement unavailability. Expected: Temporary startup messages clear and gas values become available. Do not condemn the module before its normal initialization period has completed.

steps.title: 9. Review Gas-Monitoring Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm that the Avance is configured to display and use the installed gas module. Check relevant settings for: Gas monitoring enabled. Correct module source. CO2 waveform selected. Gas numerics assigned to the screen. Appropriate agent monitoring configuration. Automatic or manual agent identification selection. Alarm limits enabled as required. Expected: Installed module measurements are selected and visible on the configured display pages. If values were present but hidden by the screen configuration, restore the correct display setup and stop.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Controlled Power Restart
steps.instructions: When the machine is off patient and alternate equipment is available: Turn the Avance off using the normal shutdown process. Remove and inspect the gas module. Reinstall the module securely. Restart the system. Observe whether the module is recognized during startup. Do not interrupt power while the machine is supporting a patient. Expected: The Avance completes startup and recognizes the gas module without recurring communication alarms.

steps.title: 11. Test With a Known-Good Gas Module
steps.instructions: When available, install a compatible, verified gas module of the correct type. GE respiratory-module measurement options vary, and not every module option is supported by every host device. Confirm compatibility before substitution. Interpret the result: Known-good module works: The original module, water trap, or module-specific sampling system is suspect. Known-good module is also not recognized: The Avance module slot, power supply, communication path, or system configuration may be faulty. Module is recognized but measurements remain unavailable: Continue evaluating the water trap, sampling line, patient connection, settings, and test-gas source. Expected: Substitution isolates the problem to the removable module or the anesthesia-machine host.

steps.title: 12. Verify Measurements With an Approved Test Source
steps.instructions: Using an approved gas-simulation or verification method: Confirm CO2 detection and waveform response. Confirm O2 measurement response when applicable. Confirm agent identification only with an approved test source and facility procedure. Verify that displayed values stabilize and alarms operate appropriately. Do not expose personnel to anesthetic vapor or improvise agent-testing methods. Expected: The module produces stable, plausible measurements and appropriate waveforms. If the module passes verification, return the machine to service only after completing the required operational checkout.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia staff reported that the GE Healthcare Avance displayed gas measurement unavailable and did not show CO2 or anesthetic-agent values.
CCR.Cause: The gas-module water trap was saturated and the sample line contained condensation, preventing adequate sample flow.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the water trap and sample line, reseated the gas module, verified stable CO2 and gas measurements, and completed the operational checkout successfully.

helpfulDetails: Gas module model and serial number
O2 and agent values available or unavailable

title: GE Healthcare Avance Anesthesia Machine - Vaporizer Not Recognized or Interlock Fault
description: Troubleshooting vaporizer mounting, recognition, locking, or interlock problems caused by positioning, compatibility, contamination, or damaged external components.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not remove, exchange, reseat, or test a vaporizer while the Avance is actively supporting a patient. If vaporizer operation or anesthetic-agent delivery is uncertain: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Have the provider establish an approved alternate anesthetic plan. Transfer the patient to another verified anesthesia machine when necessary. Maintain appropriate ventilation and independent gas monitoring. Expected: Patient care no longer depends on equipment with uncertain anesthetic-agent delivery. Continue troubleshooting only after the machine is removed from active clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Condition
steps.instructions: Review the reported problem and determine whether: The vaporizer cannot be installed. The locking lever will not fully engage. The concentration dial will not turn. Two vaporizers can be turned on simultaneously. The machine does not respond as expected when the vaporizer is activated. The problem occurs in one mounting position or every position. Record the vaporizer type, anesthetic agent, mounting position, and any displayed messages. Expected: The complaint is clearly defined before components are exchanged.

steps.title: 3. Verify Vaporizer Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm that the installed vaporizer is an approved Selectatec-compatible vaporizer intended for use with the Avance configuration. Do not force an incompatible vaporizer onto the manifold. GE describes the Avance vaporization system as using a Selectatec interlocking mounting system that bypasses vaporizers not selected for use. Expected: The vaporizer and mounting system are mechanically compatible. If the vaporizer is not approved or compatible, remove it from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Vaporizer Externally
steps.instructions: With the vaporizer removed and its concentration dial set to OFF, inspect for: Cracks or impact damage. Bent or damaged mounting components. Loose locking hardware. Residue, liquid agent, or contamination. Damaged concentration dial or release mechanism. Missing labels or unreadable agent identification. Signs that the vaporizer was dropped. Do not install a vaporizer showing physical damage or leakage. Expected: The vaporizer is clean, intact, and safe to mount.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Avance Vaporizer Manifold
steps.instructions: Examine the mounting positions without opening the machine. Check for: Debris or liquid on the mounting surface. Bent alignment features. Damaged valve pins. Loose manifold hardware. Obstructions preventing full seating. Visible damage around the interlock mechanism. Clean only according to facility procedures and manufacturer-approved methods. Do not lubricate the manifold or interlock. Expected: The mounting surface is clean, unobstructed, and visibly undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Reseat and Lock the Vaporizer
steps.instructions: Place the vaporizer squarely onto the mounting position without rocking or forcing it. Turn the locking lever completely to the locked position. Confirm that: The vaporizer sits flat against the manifold. The vaporizer does not lift or move. The locking lever reaches its full locked position. The concentration dial remains at OFF during installation. Incomplete seating may prevent proper valve engagement or interlock operation. Expected: The vaporizer is firmly mounted and cannot be removed while locked. If reseating resolves the issue, complete the machine checkout and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check for Interference From the Adjacent Vaporizer
steps.instructions: Set both vaporizer concentration dials to OFF. Confirm that both vaporizers are: Fully seated. Fully locked. Correctly aligned. Not physically contacting or obstructing each other. Attempt to turn on one vaporizer at a time. The Selectatec interlock should prevent more than one mounted vaporizer from being activated simultaneously. Expected: One vaporizer can be selected while the other remains mechanically locked at OFF. If both vaporizers can be turned on simultaneously, immediately remove the anesthesia machine from service.

steps.title: 8. Isolate the Vaporizer From the Mounting Position
steps.instructions: Using another compatible, verified vaporizer, repeat the mounting and interlock check in the same position. Then install the original vaporizer in the alternate mounting position, when the machine configuration permits. Interpret the results: If the problem follows the vaporizer, suspect a vaporizer mechanical fault. If multiple vaporizers fail in one position, suspect the Avance mounting or interlock mechanism. If the fault disappears after reseating, suspect incomplete installation or contamination. Expected: The problem is isolated to either the vaporizer or the anesthesia machine. Do not use a patient-care vaporizer merely as an uncontrolled test component. Preserve clinical readiness.

steps.title: 9. Verify Vaporizer Dial Operation
steps.instructions: With the vaporizer properly mounted and the adjacent vaporizer set to OFF: Press the concentration-control release as designed. Turn the dial slowly from OFF to a low concentration. Confirm smooth movement without excessive force. Return the dial fully to OFF. Do not force a stuck dial. A concentration control that binds, slips, or cannot return securely to OFF requires vaporizer service. Expected: The dial moves normally and positively returns to OFF.

steps.title: 10. Run the Avance Preoperative Checkout
steps.instructions: After the vaporizer is securely installed: Confirm both vaporizers are filled appropriately and initially set to OFF. Run the required Avance checkout or full system test. Observe for leakage-test failures, gas-delivery abnormalities, or vaporizer-related messages. Verify agent output only with approved test equipment and facility procedures. GE checkout guidance includes confirming that vaporizers are off and appropriately filled before system testing. Expected: The machine completes its checkout with normal vaporizer and interlock operation. If the checkout passes and the original complaint cannot be reproduced, document the findings and return the device according to facility policy.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia staff reported that the Avance vaporizer would not lock into position and the concentration dial could not be activated.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the vaporizer incompletely seated because residue on the Selectatec mounting surface prevented full locking-lever engagement.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the vaporizer, cleaned the external mounting surface using an approved method, reinstalled and locked the vaporizer, verified interlock operation, and completed the Avance checkout successfully.

helpfulDetails: Vaporizer manufacturer, model, and serial number

title: GE Healthcare Avance Anesthesia Machine - Electronic Flow Control Malfunction
description: Troubleshooting unavailable, inaccurate, or unresponsive electronic fresh-gas flow control caused by supply, control, configuration, or gas-delivery system problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended flow-control troubleshooting while the Avance is supporting an active patient. If fresh-gas flow cannot be adjusted, displayed flow is questionable, or gas delivery is unstable: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Transfer the patient to another verified anesthesia machine or approved backup ventilation method. Maintain independent oxygenation, ventilation, and gas monitoring. Follow the facility’s anesthesia-machine failure procedure. Expected: Patient care no longer depends on an anesthesia machine with uncertain fresh-gas delivery. If the patient has been safely transferred or the machine is not in use, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Condition
steps.instructions: Record the complete displayed alarm or message and determine whether the problem involves: Flow setting does not respond to control changes; Total flow or oxygen percentage cannot be adjusted; Displayed flow differs from measured or expected flow; One gas is unavailable; Fresh-gas flow stops unexpectedly; Alternate O2 activates; The issue occurs only during startup or checkout. Expected: The complaint is clearly defined and can be reproduced safely on a test circuit.

steps.title: 3. Check for Alternate O2 Operation
steps.instructions: Inspect the Alternate O2 control and determine whether it has activated or was manually turned on. Certain system failures may cause Alternate O2 to activate automatically. When active, normal electronic gas-control operation may be unavailable or altered. Confirm the control is fully in its intended position. Observe whether the display indicates Alternate O2 operation. Do not assume normal electronic flow control is functioning while Alternate O2 is active. Expected: Alternate O2 status matches the selected operating condition. If the control was unintentionally active and normal electronic flow control returns after proper reset and checkout, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify AC Power and Startup Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The power cord is fully connected. The wall outlet is functional and approved for medical equipment. The machine recognizes AC mains power. No power-related alarms are active. The system completes startup without freezing or repeatedly restarting. Electronic gas control depends on stable system power and functional control electronics. Expected: The Avance remains powered from AC mains and completes startup normally. If power is unstable, correct the external power problem and repeat the manufacturer-approved checkout.

steps.title: 5. Verify Pipeline Gas Supplies
steps.instructions: Check the connected O2, Air, and N2O pipeline supplies as equipped. Confirm each hose is connected to the correct wall outlet and machine inlet. Inspect hoses and fittings for damage, kinks, loose connections, or contamination. Verify adequate pipeline pressure using an approved test method. Test the wall outlet or use another verified outlet when permitted. Confirm that no facility medical-gas outage or maintenance condition is present. Expected: Each required gas supply is correctly connected and available at the proper pressure. If flow control returns after correcting a pipeline connection or pressure problem, complete a full checkout, document the repair, and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Backup Cylinder Status
steps.instructions: Inspect installed backup cylinders without interrupting any required gas supply. Confirm cylinders contain adequate pressure. Verify cylinder valves are fully closed during normal pipeline testing unless the approved procedure requires otherwise. Check for leaking or damaged cylinder yokes and seals. Confirm a partially open cylinder is not masking an unstable pipeline supply. Expected: Backup cylinders are correctly installed and are not creating an abnormal supply condition.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Controls and Display Response
steps.instructions: Operate the fresh-gas flow controls in a controlled test environment. Confirm the control knob turns normally and is not physically damaged. Watch for consistent movement of the selected flow or oxygen concentration setting. Check whether selections skip, reverse, lag, or fail to register. Inspect the touchscreen and rotary control for contamination or interference. Confirm that no accessory, drape, or object is pressing against a control. Expected: Each control input produces an immediate and consistent display response. If the controls are physically damaged or intermittently unresponsive, remove the machine from service for repair.

steps.title: 8. Review Gas-Selection and Flow Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm that the selected carrier gas, oxygen concentration, and total fresh-gas flow are appropriate for the test. Increase and decrease total flow through a safe test range. Adjust the oxygen concentration. Change the selected balance gas when the configuration permits. Observe whether the displayed gas mixture changes logically. Confirm that a low-flow setting is not being mistaken for loss of flow. Expected: Displayed gas settings respond logically and remain stable after adjustment.

steps.title: 9. Inspect the Common Gas Outlet and Breathing-System Connections
steps.instructions: Check the external gas-delivery path. Confirm the breathing system is fully seated. Inspect the common gas outlet or selectable common gas outlet configuration, if equipped. Verify external circuits and hoses are attached to the intended outlet. Check for disconnected, obstructed, kinked, or incorrectly routed tubing. Confirm the machine is not unintentionally configured to direct flow to an auxiliary breathing system. GE identifies selectable common-gas-outlet components as part of the anesthesia machine’s breathing-circuit gas-delivery system. Expected: Fresh gas is directed through the intended outlet without an external restriction or misconnection.

steps.title: 10. Inspect Vaporizers and External Accessories
steps.instructions: Confirm that: Vaporizers are fully seated and locked. Only compatible vaporizers are installed. Vaporizer controls are in the OFF position during initial testing. No accessory attached to the gas pathway is visibly damaged, obstructed, or improperly installed. The issue does not occur only when one specific vaporizer or accessory is installed. Expected: External accessories do not interfere with gas delivery or system checkout. If removing a suspect accessory restores normal operation, quarantine the accessory and repeat the complete checkout.

steps.title: 11. Perform the Approved Machine Checkout
steps.instructions: With no patient connected: Install the approved test circuit and test lung. Complete the manufacturer-approved preoperative checkout. Run the system leak and gas-delivery checks available to the operator. Observe total fresh-gas flow, oxygen concentration, alarms, and Alternate O2 behavior. Verify delivered oxygen concentration with a calibrated external analyzer when required by facility procedure. The Avance breathing system is designed to support rapid control of fresh-gas flows, so delayed, unstable, or unavailable adjustment is not normal operation. Expected: The system passes checkout, flow settings remain stable, and measured gas delivery agrees with the selected settings within applicable specifications. If the machine passes all testing and the complaint cannot be reproduced, document the tests performed and return it to service only according to facility policy.

steps.title: 12. Compare With Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: When permitted, substitute known-good external items one at a time: Pipeline hose; Wall gas outlet; Power cord; Breathing circuit; Test lung; Compatible vaporizer or accessory. Repeat the relevant functional check after each substitution. Expected: A defective external component is isolated without opening the machine. If a substituted component resolves the issue, replace or quarantine the failed item, complete the full checkout, and stop.

CCR.Complaint: Anesthesia staff reported that the Avance electronic fresh-gas flow setting would not respond and Alternate O2 activated during setup.
CCR.Cause: Pipeline supplies and external connections tested normally, but electronic flow adjustment remained unavailable during the approved machine checkout.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the Avance from service, labeled it Out of Service, provided a replacement machine, and forwarded the unit for electronic gas-delivery system evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Indicator lights or unusual display behavior

title: GE Healthcare Avance Anesthesia Machine - Bellows Not Rising or Cycling Normally
description: Troubleshooting collapsed, partially rising, or irregularly cycling bellows caused by gas supply, circuit leaks, assembly problems, settings, or breathing-system restrictions.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended bellows troubleshooting while the Avance is supporting an active patient. If the bellows collapses, stops cycling, or ventilation becomes unreliable: Notify the anesthesia provider immediately. Establish ventilation using another verified anesthesia machine or approved backup method. Maintain independent patient monitoring. Follow the facility’s anesthesia-machine failure procedure. Expected: Patient ventilation no longer depends on equipment with questionable mechanical ventilation. The Avance uses ascending bellows. Bellows that fail to rise can indicate inadequate circuit volume, a significant leak, insufficient gas supply, or a ventilator problem. If the patient is safely supported elsewhere, continue troubleshooting in a controlled Clinical Engineering setting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure Condition
steps.instructions: Operate the machine using an approved test lung and determine whether the bellows: Remains fully collapsed. Rises only partially. Rises slowly between breaths. Cycles irregularly. Falls during expiration. Reaches the top but does not descend normally. Works in manual ventilation but not mechanical ventilation. Produces an “Unable to drive bellows” or related ventilator message. Record the selected ventilation mode, tidal volume, respiratory rate, fresh-gas flow, and displayed airway pressures. Expected: The failure can be reproduced consistently and tied to a specific operating condition.

steps.title: 3. Check the Medical-Gas Supply
steps.instructions: Verify that the required pipeline gases are connected securely and that supply-pressure indicators are within the normal operating range. Check for: Disconnected pipeline hoses. Loose or partially engaged gas fittings. Closed or unavailable wall outlets. Pipeline-pressure alarms. Depleted backup cylinders. Kinked or damaged gas hoses. Do not disconnect an active oxygen source while the machine is supporting a patient. Expected: Adequate drive gas and fresh gas are available without supply alarms. If restoring the gas supply returns normal bellows movement, complete an operational checkout and stop.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Adequate Fresh-Gas Flow
steps.instructions: Set an appropriate fresh-gas flow in a controlled test configuration and observe whether the bellows begins filling. A temporarily increased fresh-gas flow may help determine whether the bellows is collapsed because the breathing system lacks sufficient gas volume. GE guidance for a collapsed bellows condition includes checking drive gas and increasing fresh-gas flow. Do not use the oxygen-flush control as a substitute for correcting a persistent leak or ventilator fault. Expected: The bellows fills and reaches a stable position between mechanical breaths.
