steps.instructions: If the sensor is detected but no saturation value appears, evaluate external signal conditions using a simulator or controlled nonpatient test whenever possible. For a clinical placement check performed by authorized staff, verify: Correct sensor orientation; Proper emitter-to-detector alignment; Appropriate sensor size; Full contact with the measurement site; No excessive motion; No restrictive tape or pressure; No nail covering, strong external light, or contamination affecting the optical path; Adequate perfusion at the selected site. Clinical conditions such as low perfusion, motion, vasoconstriction, or an unsuitable measurement site may prevent a reliable reading even when the equipment is functioning. Expected outcome: A recognizable pleth waveform and stable saturation value appear when signal conditions are adequate.

steps.title: 10. Inspect the Parameter-Acquisition Hardware
steps.instructions: Inspect the connected parameter module, acquisition device, or cable interface used to provide SpO₂ data to CARESCAPE Canvas. Check for: Loose attachment or docking; Damaged parameter ports; Contaminated connectors; Bent or recessed contacts; Liquid exposure; Communication or module-disconnect messages; Other missing parameters from the same hardware; Abnormal indicator lights. Reseat the external module or acquisition connection when this can be done safely and without internal disassembly. Expected outcome: The acquisition hardware is recognized and communicates normally with the monitor. If several parameters are missing simultaneously, investigate the module or communication path rather than continuing to replace SpO₂ sensors.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After confirming that the device is not supporting an active patient: Shut down the monitoring system using the approved normal procedure. Disconnect removable external accessories as appropriate. Wait briefly for shutdown to complete. Reconnect the required parameter-acquisition hardware. Restart the system. Allow the monitor and connected components to complete initialization. Reconnect the known-good SpO₂ sensor and cable. Do not repeatedly interrupt startup or cycle power during patient care. Expected outcome: The SpO₂ hardware initializes, the sensor is detected, and a signal can be acquired.

steps.title: 12. Verify Performance Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: Use an approved SpO₂ simulator or the facility’s established performance-verification method. Confirm: Sensor recognition; Continuous pleth waveform; Stable saturation and pulse-rate values; Values within the facility’s accepted tolerance; No intermittent disconnect messages; Appropriate alarm activation; Stable operation while the cable and connectors are gently manipulated. Do not use a person as the only basis for determining measurement accuracy. Expected outcome: The complete SpO₂ measurement path performs consistently and meets the facility’s return-to-service requirements.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas displayed no SpO₂ value and did not consistently recognize the connected sensor.
CCR.Cause: Troubleshooting found an open or intermittent connection in the reusable SpO₂ patient cable; the monitor operated normally with a known-good compatible cable.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective SpO₂ cable, verified sensor recognition and stable simulated saturation and pulse-rate values, confirmed alarm operation, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Failed accessory tagged or discarded according to policy

title: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Canvas Patient Monitor - NIBP Cuff Will Not Inflate or Measurement Fails
description: Troubleshooting failed NIBP measurements caused by cuff, hose, connection, patient setup, configuration, pneumatic leakage, or acquisition-device problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended NIBP troubleshooting while the CARESCAPE Canvas system is the only device monitoring an active patient. If blood pressure monitoring is clinically required: Assess the patient immediately. Obtain a manual blood pressure or use another verified monitor. Transfer monitoring to another device before continuing. Do not repeatedly cycle the cuff on the patient while investigating the failure. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on an unavailable or unreliable NIBP channel. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the affected equipment is no longer required for active patient care.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Attempt one NIBP measurement using an appropriate test cuff or simulator setup. Observe whether: The pump does not start. The cuff begins inflating but stops. The cuff inflates and immediately deflates. The measurement times out. An air leak, loose cuff, or measurement-failed message appears. NIBP controls are unavailable or the parameter is missing. Document any displayed message and the point in the cycle where the failure occurs. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as a control, inflation, leakage, acquisition, or measurement-completion problem.

steps.title: 3. Verify the NIBP Parameter Is Available
steps.instructions: Confirm that the NIBP parameter is displayed and that the start/stop control is available. Verify the appropriate patient category is selected: Adult, Pediatric, Neonatal. An incorrect patient category may affect allowable cuff pressures, measurement behavior, and accessory selection. Expected outcome: NIBP is available and configured for the intended patient category. If correcting the configuration restores operation, complete a functional test and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Cuff
steps.instructions: Check the cuff for: Tears, punctures, or worn material; Damaged hook-and-loop fasteners; A twisted or folded bladder; Loose pneumatic fittings; Incorrect cuff type or size; Contamination or fluid intrusion. Use only a compatible cuff that is appropriate for the selected patient category and limb size. Expected outcome: The cuff is intact, correctly sized, and able to hold pressure. If a replacement cuff resolves the issue, verify repeated measurements and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the NIBP Hose
steps.instructions: Examine the entire hose for: Kinks or crushing; Cuts, splits, or abrasion; Loose fittings; Damaged connector pins or locking features; Internal obstruction; Fluid contamination; Evidence of stretching near either connector. Straighten the hose and ensure it is not trapped under equipment or furniture. Expected outcome: Air can move freely through an undamaged hose. If the hose is damaged or contaminated, replace it rather than attempting a temporary repair.

steps.title: 6. Reseat All Pneumatic Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect and firmly reconnect: The cuff-to-hose connection; Any extension-hose connection; The hose connection at the NIBP acquisition device or monitor interface. Confirm each connector is fully seated and does not pull loose with light tension. CARESCAPE Canvas is a scalable monitoring platform that may use different monitoring and acquisition configurations, so verify the pneumatic hose is connected to the component providing NIBP measurement for that bed. Expected outcome: The pneumatic path is secure from the acquisition device to the cuff. If reseating the connection restores normal inflation, complete multiple measurements and stop.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Connect a known-good, compatible: NIBP cuff; NIBP hose; Extension hose, when used. Change one item at a time so the failed accessory can be identified. Expected outcome: A defective external accessory is isolated. If the measurement succeeds after an accessory change, remove the failed item from service and document the replacement.

steps.title: 8. Check for Pneumatic Leakage
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate cuff wrapped securely around a test cylinder or NIBP simulator mandrel, start a measurement and listen for escaping air. Check for leakage at: The cuff bladder; Cuff fittings; Hose connections; Extension connections; The acquisition-device connector. Do not block, clamp, or modify the hose to force a measurement. Expected outcome: The system inflates without audible leakage or rapid pressure loss. If leakage follows the cuff or hose, replace that accessory and repeat the test.

steps.title: 9. Check for an Obstructed Pneumatic Path
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The cuff bladder is not folded. The hose is not sharply bent. Connector openings are not blocked. No dried fluid, adhesive, or debris is present. The cuff is not wrapped so tightly that inflation is mechanically restricted. Do not insert tools, wires, or compressed air into pneumatic ports. Expected outcome: The cuff and hose provide an unrestricted pneumatic path. If removing the obstruction restores operation, clean or replace the affected accessory and stop.

steps.title: 10. Restart the Measurement Function
steps.instructions: Cancel the current measurement and allow the cuff to fully deflate. Wait briefly, then start a new single measurement. If the controls appear frozen or the parameter does not respond, safely restart the affected monitor or acquisition device according to facility procedures. Do not repeatedly restart equipment while connected to an active patient. Expected outcome: A temporary software or communication condition clears and the NIBP function becomes responsive. If normal operation returns, perform several successful test measurements before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 11. Verify the Acquisition Device Connection
steps.instructions: When NIBP is provided through a connected CARESCAPE acquisition device, confirm that the device: Is powered and recognized; Is securely docked or connected; Shows no communication or hardware alarms; Displays its other supported parameters normally; Has no visible connector damage. Disconnect and reconnect the acquisition device only after the system is removed from patient use. Expected outcome: The NIBP acquisition component is recognized and communicating normally. If several parameters from the same acquisition device are unavailable, investigate the acquisition-device connection rather than assuming an isolated cuff failure.

steps.title: 12. Compare With a Known-Good Configuration
steps.instructions: When available, test the suspect cuff and hose on a compatible, known-good CARESCAPE setup. Then test known-good accessories on the suspect system. Do not exchange accessories between active patient beds without following infection-control requirements. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to either the external accessories or the NIBP acquisition hardware. If the failure remains with the cuff or hose, replace the accessory. If it remains with the monitor or acquisition device, continue to escalation.

steps.title: 13. Perform a Controlled Functional Check
steps.instructions: Using an approved NIBP analyzer or simulator: Connect the correct compatible hose. Select the proper patient category. Initiate several measurements. Confirm inflation begins normally. Confirm the measurement completes without leakage or repeated failure. Compare displayed values with the analyzer’s expected results according to facility tolerances. A patient should not be used as the test load for Clinical Engineering verification. Expected outcome: The system consistently inflates, measures, deflates, and produces acceptable results. If the device cannot complete controlled analyzer testing, remove it from service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas monitor would not inflate the NIBP cuff and displayed repeated measurement failures.
CCR.Cause: Testing found a split near the NIBP hose connector that allowed pressure to escape during cuff inflation.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged hose, completed three successful measurements using an NIBP analyzer, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the pump could be heard

title: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Canvas Patient Monitor - Invasive Pressure Channel Missing, Drifting, or Will Not Zero
description: Troubleshooting missing, unstable, inaccurate, or non-zeroing invasive pressure channels caused by transducers, cables, connections, setup, positioning, or module communication.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the CARESCAPE Canvas is the only monitor supporting an actively monitored patient. If invasive pressure monitoring is clinically required: Notify the clinical team immediately. Assess the patient and confirm hemodynamic status using another approved method. Transfer monitoring to another verified monitor when continuous invasive pressure monitoring is required. Do not assume a drifting or abnormal pressure value is solely an equipment problem. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on an unavailable or questionable invasive pressure channel. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the monitor is no longer required for active patient care.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves: The pressure channel not appearing; A transducer-not-connected message; A flat or absent waveform; A pressure value that drifts; An inability to complete zeroing; An unreasonable value after zeroing; One pressure channel or all invasive pressure channels. Document any messages, alarm behavior, channel labels, and whether the issue follows a specific accessory. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined before parts are exchanged.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Required Monitoring Hardware Is Present
steps.instructions: Confirm that the appropriate invasive pressure-capable parameter hardware is connected, powered, and recognized by the CARESCAPE Canvas system. Inspect the parameter module, acquisition device, or connected monitoring component for: Missing hardware; Incomplete insertion; Loose docking; Damaged connectors; Communication or module-recognition messages; Missing status indicators. Reseat externally removable modules or acquisition components only when the device is safely out of patient use. Expected outcome: The required invasive pressure hardware is detected and available. If the channel returns after reseating, perform a functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Pressure Cable and Transducer Connections
steps.instructions: Trace the entire connection path from the monitor or parameter module to the reusable pressure cable and disposable transducer. Check for: Loose connectors; Bent, recessed, contaminated, or damaged contacts; Cracked connector housings; Pinched or sharply bent cables; Fluid intrusion; Strain near either cable end; An incompatible cable or transducer. Disconnect and reconnect each accessible connection securely. Expected outcome: All components are fully seated, clean, dry, undamaged, and compatible. If the channel appears and remains stable, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 5. Substitute Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Replace the suspected disposable transducer with a compatible known-good transducer. If the problem remains, substitute a known-good reusable invasive pressure cable approved for the monitoring configuration. Change one component at a time so the failed accessory can be identified. Expected outcome: The channel operates normally with known-good accessories. If the issue follows the original transducer or cable, remove that accessory from use and stop after confirming normal operation.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Fluid Path and Stopcock Position
steps.instructions: Have qualified clinical personnel verify that the pressure-monitoring setup is properly prepared. Check externally for: Air bubbles; Clotted or obstructed tubing; Kinked pressure tubing; Loose connections; Leaks; An empty or improperly pressurized flush solution; Incorrect stopcock orientation; The transducer not open to atmospheric pressure during zeroing. Clinical Engineering should not manipulate an active patient line unless authorized and trained under facility policy. Expected outcome: The transducer can be safely exposed to atmosphere for zeroing, and the fluid path is free of obvious external problems.

steps.title: 7. Verify Transducer Position and Stability
steps.instructions: Confirm that the transducer is: Secured to an appropriate holder; Positioned at the clinically established reference level; Not hanging freely; Not resting on a moving surface; Not being raised or lowered during evaluation; Protected from tension caused by tubing or cable movement. Changing the transducer height after zeroing can create an apparent pressure offset or drift. Expected outcome: The transducer remains stable at the correct reference level. If repositioning corrects the reading, repeat zeroing and stop after verification.

steps.title: 8. Attempt a Proper Zero
steps.instructions: With the device removed from active patient use, have qualified personnel: Close the stopcock to the patient. Open the transducer to atmospheric pressure. Select the appropriate invasive pressure channel. Initiate the zero command. Wait for confirmation that zeroing completed. Close the transducer to atmosphere and restore the correct fluid-path position. Compatible CARESCAPE monitoring workflows may also provide a Zero All Pressures function for connected transducers. Expected outcome: The monitor confirms a successful zero without displaying an error. If zeroing succeeds and the value remains stable, perform a simulated-pressure test and stop.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Correct Channel and Pressure Label
steps.instructions: Confirm that the connected pressure input is assigned to the intended parameter, such as: ART; CVP; PAP; ICP; LAP; RAP; Another configured invasive pressure label. Check that the channel has not been disabled, hidden from the current screen layout, or assigned to an unexpected label. Review only normal user-accessible configuration settings. Do not change protected clinical configuration values without authorization. Expected outcome: The correct pressure channel is enabled, labeled, and displayed.

steps.title: 10. Check for Duplicate or Conflicting Pressure Inputs
steps.instructions: Disconnect other unused pressure transducers and reconnect only the suspected channel. Confirm that two pressure inputs are not: Assigned the same label; Confused by the selected screen layout; Connected to an unintended module input; Producing a value on a different channel than expected. Expected outcome: The intended physical input corresponds to the expected displayed pressure channel.

steps.title: 11. Compare Another Pressure Input
steps.instructions: When another compatible invasive pressure input is available, connect the known-good cable and simulator to that input. Observe whether the failure: Remains with the original input; Follows the cable or transducer; Occurs on every invasive pressure input; Appears only with one parameter module. Expected outcome: The test isolates the issue to an accessory, input channel, module, or system-level communication problem.

steps.title: 12. Test With a Patient Simulator
steps.instructions: Connect a compatible pressure simulator using approved test accessories. Verify: The channel zeros successfully; The displayed pressure matches the applied simulated value; The waveform is stable; The value does not drift excessively; Alarm limits respond appropriately when tested; The reading returns to baseline as expected. Do not return the monitor to service based only on a successful zero. Verify pressure accuracy at multiple simulated values according to facility procedure. Expected outcome: The invasive pressure channel displays stable and accurate simulated pressures. If the device passes, document the accessory or setup cause and return it to service according to facility policy.

steps.title: 13. Restart and Recheck Module Recognition
steps.instructions: If all external accessories pass but the pressure channel remains missing or unavailable: Disconnect the device from patient use. Perform a normal shutdown. Inspect external module and acquisition-device connections. Restore power and allow the system to complete startup. Confirm that the pressure-capable hardware is recognized. Reconnect the simulator and repeat the functional test. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a device displaying persistent software, module, or communication faults. Expected outcome: The system restarts normally and the pressure channel becomes available. If the issue returns, remove the device from service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas arterial pressure channel would not zero and displayed a drifting value.
CCR.Cause: Testing found an intermittent reusable invasive pressure cable that produced unstable simulated pressure readings when the cable was moved.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective pressure cable, successfully zeroed the channel, and verified stable pressure accuracy with a simulator before returning the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Patient removed from the affected monitoring channel
Exact pressure channel or label affected
Air, leaks, kinks, or obstruction observed
Whether the issue followed an accessory

title: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Canvas Patient Monitor - CO2 Module Not Recognized or No Capnogram
description: Troubleshooting missing CO2 detection or capnograms caused by module connections, sampling accessories, blockages, contamination, configuration, or communication failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the CARESCAPE Canvas is the only device monitoring ventilation on an active patient. If continuous capnography is clinically required: Assess the patient and airway immediately. Verify ventilation using another approved clinical method. Transfer CO2 monitoring to another verified monitor or capnography device. Do not assume a missing capnogram is only an equipment problem. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation continues to be assessed without relying on the unavailable CO2 parameter. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the device can be safely removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Observe the CO2 parameter area and record whether the monitor shows: CO2 module not detected; Module disconnected; Sampling line blocked; Water trap full or missing; No breath detected; Dashed CO2 values; Numeric values without a waveform; An intermittent or distorted capnogram; No CO2 parameter window. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as module recognition, sampling, waveform, or configuration related.

steps.title: 3. Identify the Installed CO2 Configuration
steps.instructions: Determine whether CO2 is being provided through: A CARESCAPE ONE with compatible Microstream CO2 capability; A CARESCAPE respiratory gas module; Another approved CARESCAPE micro-module or parameter interface. CARESCAPE Canvas supports modular parameter acquisition, but available CO2 options depend on installed hardware, software, licensing, and system configuration. Expected outcome: The correct module, accessories, and communication path are identified before components are exchanged.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Module and Host Connection
steps.instructions: Remove the device from patient use and inspect: The CO2 module or CARESCAPE ONE seating; Module bay or interface connections; Connector pins and contact surfaces; Retaining mechanisms; Communication or interface cables; Signs of liquid intrusion, contamination, cracks, or physical damage. Reseat the module firmly using normal installation methods. Do not force the module into the interface. Expected outcome: The module is fully seated, mechanically secure, and recognized by the monitor. If recognition returns and remains stable, complete functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Restart the CO2 Measurement
steps.instructions: Using the normal clinical interface: Verify the CO2 measurement is enabled. Confirm the CO2 parameter is assigned to the active screen or profile. Exit standby or measurement-off modes. Allow the module to complete its startup and initialization period. Do not enter protected service menus or alter institutional defaults unless authorized. Expected outcome: The CO2 parameter window appears and the module begins its normal initialization sequence.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Sampling Line
steps.instructions: For sidestream CO2 configurations, inspect the complete sampling path for: Loose connections; Kinks or compression; Cracks or punctures; Moisture; Secretions; Occlusion; Incorrect assembly; Expired or incompatible accessories. Disconnect and reconnect the sampling line at both the patient-end accessory and module inlet. Expected outcome: The sampling line is secure, open, dry, and compatible with the installed CO2 system. If the capnogram returns, replace any questionable disposable accessory and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Water Trap or Sampling Receptacle
steps.instructions: When the installed respiratory module uses a water trap: Verify the correct trap is installed. Confirm it is completely seated. Check for fluid, discoloration, contamination, cracks, or a blocked membrane. Replace a full, damaged, contaminated, or questionable trap with an approved replacement. GE respiratory modules use sidestream sampling, and water-trap condition can directly affect gas sampling. Expected outcome: The module begins sampling without blockage or water-trap alarms.

steps.title: 8. Test With Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Replace the installed components one at a time with compatible known-good items: Sampling line; Airway adapter or nasal cannula; Water trap, when applicable; Module interface cable, when applicable. Change only one item at a time so the failed component can be identified. Expected outcome: A capnogram and respiratory rate appear when the defective accessory is removed. If the issue is corrected, discard or quarantine the failed accessory according to facility policy and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Check for Sampling Pump Operation
steps.instructions: Listen for normal sampling-pump operation and observe the monitor for continuing blockage or flow-related messages. Do not insert tools, compressed air, cleaning solution, or probes into the sampling inlet. Expected outcome: The module draws a sample without unusual noise, repeated blockage alarms, or loss of flow. No pump sound, abnormal noise, or persistent blockage with known-good accessories suggests an internal module problem.

steps.title: 10. Test the Module on Another Compatible System
steps.instructions: When available and permitted: Install the suspect CO2 module or CARESCAPE ONE on another compatible, verified CARESCAPE system. Install a known-good compatible module on the affected CARESCAPE Canvas. Confirm software and configuration compatibility before swapping equipment. Expected outcome: If the suspect module fails on both systems, the module is likely defective. If a known-good module also fails on the affected Canvas, investigate the Canvas interface, configuration, or software. If both components work after reseating, suspect an intermittent connection.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Functional Test
steps.instructions: Connect the device to an approved patient simulator, capnography test source, or manufacturer-approved gas-analysis test setup. Verify: Module recognition; Stable CO2 numeric display; Visible capnogram; Respiratory rate calculation; Appropriate alarm response; No blockage, water-trap, or module communication messages. Do not use exhaled breath as the only return-to-service verification. Expected outcome: The CARESCAPE Canvas consistently displays and alarms on a controlled CO2 input. If the system passes, return it to service only after completing required inspection and documentation.

steps.title: 12. Check for Software or Configuration Symptoms
steps.instructions: If hardware and accessories test normally, document whether: The CO2 parameter disappears after startup. The module is recognized intermittently. The issue follows a specific clinical profile. A recent software update or configuration change occurred. Other modules also disconnect or disappear. The monitor displays communication or configuration errors. Do not reinstall software, modify licenses, or perform protected configuration changes without authorization and approved GE service documentation. Expected outcome: A software, licensing, profile, or host communication issue is distinguished from a failed CO2 module.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas did not recognize the CO2 module and displayed no capnogram.
CCR.Cause: Testing found a fluid-contaminated water trap restricting sidestream gas flow and preventing a stable CO2 waveform.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the water trap and sampling line, verified module recognition, stable capnogram, respiratory rate, and CO2 alarms using an approved test setup, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: CARESCAPE ONE software version, if applicable

title: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Canvas Patient Monitor - CARESCAPE Central Station Communication Failure
description: Troubleshooting missing central-station communication caused by network connections, configuration, admission, duplicate addressing, infrastructure, or communication-service issues.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot network communication while the CARESCAPE Canvas is the only monitor supporting an actively monitored patient. If central monitoring is unavailable: Notify the clinical team immediately. Confirm that local monitoring, waveforms, parameter values, and alarms remain functional. Assign direct observation or transfer the patient to another verified monitoring system when central surveillance is clinically required. Do not assume local alarms are being received at the central station. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues without relying on an unavailable central-station connection. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only when it is safe to do so.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The monitor is completely absent from the central station. The patient tile is present but shows communication loss. Waveforms or values are delayed, frozen, or intermittent. Alarms are not reaching the central station. The monitor connects briefly and then disconnects. Only one monitor, one room, or an entire care area is affected. Check whether the local monitor displays a network, central-station, or communication message. Expected outcome: The scope and behavior of the failure are clearly identified. If several monitors are affected, investigate shared network or central-station infrastructure before replacing monitor components.

steps.title: 3. Verify Local Monitoring Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the CARESCAPE Canvas: Powers on normally. Displays current patient waveforms and parameter values. Produces local visual and audible alarms. Responds normally to controls. Does not show a system freeze, repeated reboot, or configuration-loading error. Expected outcome: The monitor operates normally except for central-station communication. If the monitor is also freezing, rebooting, or losing local parameters, remove it from service and evaluate the broader monitor failure first.

steps.title: 4. Verify Patient Admission and Bed Assignment
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The patient is properly admitted or associated with the correct bed. The monitor has the expected unit, room, and bed assignment. The same patient or bed is not active on another monitor. The central station is configured to display that bed. The monitor has not been moved from another care area without being discharged or reassigned. Correct obvious admission or bed-assignment errors according to facility workflow. Expected outcome: The correct patient and bed appear at the intended central station. If communication is restored, verify live waveforms and alarm delivery, document the correction, and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Physical Network Connection
steps.instructions: For a wired installation: Confirm the Ethernet cable is fully seated at the monitor or docking connection. Confirm the wall jack or network connection is secure. Inspect the cable and connector tabs for damage. Look for bent contacts, contamination, or a loose docking interface. Check for network link or activity indicators when visible. Reseat the cable at both accessible ends. Expected outcome: The connection is secure and network link activity is present. If communication returns and remains stable, complete a functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 6. Test with a Known-Good Network Cable
steps.instructions: Replace the existing network cable with a verified compatible cable. Do not use visibly damaged, tightly kinked, crushed, or unapproved cables. Expected outcome: A known-good cable establishes stable communication. If the replacement cable resolves the problem, remove the defective cable from use, verify central waveforms and alarms, document the replacement, and stop.

steps.title: 7. Test the Network Port or Wall Jack
steps.instructions: When permitted by facility network policy: Connect the monitor to a known-working approved network port assigned to the monitoring network. Alternatively, connect a known-good compatible monitor to the suspect port. Do not connect the monitor to an unapproved general-purpose network. Expected outcome: Testing identifies whether the failure follows the monitor or remains with the network port. If the known-good monitor also fails, escalate the port, switch, VLAN, or network-path issue to the appropriate IT or network support team. If the CARESCAPE Canvas fails on a verified working connection, continue monitor-specific checks.

steps.title: 8. Check the Docking or Mounting Connection
steps.instructions: If network communication passes through a dock, mounting interface, or connected system component: Confirm the monitor is fully seated. Inspect accessible contacts for contamination or damage. Remove and reseat the monitor only when it is safe and permitted. Verify that the dock or mounting component has power and is recognized. Expected outcome: The monitor establishes a reliable connection through the docking interface. If reseating restores communication, verify stability by observing live data at the central station before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 9. Review Network and Central-Station Status Messages
steps.instructions: Record any messages indicating: Network disconnected. Central station unavailable. Duplicate network address. Invalid configuration. Bed already assigned. Communication timeout. Server or monitoring-network unavailable. Do not change IP addresses, VLAN settings, host names, certificates, or protected network configuration without approved documentation and authorization. Expected outcome: The displayed message directs troubleshooting toward a connection, configuration, addressing, or infrastructure problem.

steps.title: 10. Check for Duplicate or Incorrect Network Identity
steps.instructions: Coordinate with the facility’s monitoring-network administrator or IT department to confirm that the monitor has: The approved network identity. The correct assigned address or approved addressing method. No duplicate IP address or host identity. The correct monitoring-network segment or VLAN. The expected unit and central-station association. A duplicate network identity may cause intermittent communication, repeated disconnection, or the wrong monitor appearing at the central station. Expected outcome: The monitor has a unique, approved identity on the correct monitoring network. If an addressing or assignment error is corrected, verify communication, patient association, waveforms, and alarm delivery before returning the monitor to use.

steps.title: 11. Determine Whether Other Devices Are Affected
steps.instructions: Check other monitors connected to: The same wall jack area. The same network switch. The same care unit. The same central station. Also confirm whether the central station is powered, operating normally, and receiving data from other beds. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the monitor, a specific network location, or shared infrastructure. The CARESCAPE Central Station is designed to display monitoring information delivered through the CARESCAPE monitoring network, so widespread loss generally indicates a shared network or central-system issue rather than simultaneous monitor failures.

steps.title: 12. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After confirming that the patient is no longer dependent on the device: Discharge or preserve patient information according to facility policy. Shut down the monitor using the normal procedure. Wait briefly for shutdown to complete. Restart the monitor. Allow network and monitoring services to initialize fully. Reconfirm the unit, bed, and patient association. Do not repeatedly cycle power as a substitute for identifying an ongoing network problem. Expected outcome: Communication services initialize and the monitor reconnects to the central station. If communication returns, observe the connection long enough to confirm it remains stable.

steps.title: 13. Verify Central Monitoring and Alarm Communication
steps.instructions: Before returning the monitor to service: Confirm the correct bed appears at the central station. Confirm live waveforms and values update continuously. Compare central values with the local monitor. Generate an approved test alarm or use an approved simulator. Confirm the visual and audible alarm is received at the intended central station. Confirm alarm clearing and patient identification operate correctly. Expected outcome: Live data and alarm communication are correctly transmitted and displayed. If values appear but alarms are not received, keep the device out of service until the alarm-routing problem is corrected.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas displayed patient data locally but did not appear at the CARESCAPE Central Station.
CCR.Cause: The monitor’s network cable failed substitution testing and did not establish a stable network link.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged network cable, confirmed live waveforms and test-alarm delivery at the assigned central station, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Patient, unit, room, and bed assignment
Whether one or multiple monitors were affected
Ethernet link or activity indicator status
Duplicate address or configuration issue identified
IT or GE HealthCare case number

title: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Canvas Patient Monitor - Alarm Speaker, Alarm Light, or Audible Alarm Failure
description: Troubleshooting missing, weak, distorted, or inconsistent audible and visual alarm indications caused by settings, connections, configuration, power, or hardware failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an alarm-output failure while the CARESCAPE Canvas is the only monitor supporting an active patient. If alarm audio or the visual alarm indicator is unavailable: Notify the clinical team immediately. Transfer the patient to another verified monitoring system. Confirm that the replacement monitor produces both audible and visual alarms. Do not rely solely on a central station, waveform display, or staff observation as a substitute for functional local alarms. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues on equipment with verified alarm annunciation. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the affected monitor is safely removed from patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Alarm Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported problem involves: No alarm sound; Weak or distorted sound; Intermittent alarm sound; Alarm light not illuminating; Incorrect alarm-light color or behavior; Visual alarm message without audible output; Audible alarm without the expected visual indication; One alarm priority affected or all alarm priorities affected. Review any displayed system messages and determine whether the problem occurs continuously or only after startup, standby, transport, or configuration changes. Expected outcome: The affected alarm function and conditions are clearly identified. If the alarm operates normally and the complaint cannot be reproduced, document the testing performed and continue observation before returning the monitor to service.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Monitor Externally
steps.instructions: Check the CARESCAPE Canvas for: Physical damage; Cracks near the speaker or alarm-light area; Liquid intrusion or residue; Tape, labels, covers, or accessories obstructing the speaker opening; Contamination blocking the speaker grille; Signs of impact damage; Unusual heat, odor, or sound. Do not insert tools or cleaning materials into speaker openings. Expected outcome: The alarm speaker and visual indicator are unobstructed and the monitor has no visible damage. If contamination or an external obstruction caused the problem, clean the device using approved procedures and repeat alarm testing. Stop if the alarm functions correctly.

steps.title: 4. Verify Power and Startup Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The monitor is connected to an approved power source. Power indicators are normal. The power cable and external power connections are secure. The monitor completes startup without error messages. The display is fully operational and not frozen. No repeated rebooting or abnormal shutdown occurs. A monitor experiencing unstable power or incomplete startup may not initialize its alarm-output functions correctly. Expected outcome: The monitor starts normally and remains powered without system errors. If correcting the power connection restores alarm operation, complete functional testing and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Alarm Volume and Audio Settings
steps.instructions: Review the permitted alarm settings and confirm that: Alarm volume is not set to its lowest unintended level. The speaker has not been muted through an authorized alarm-audio control. An audio-pause or alarm-silence condition is not still active. Alarm volume is appropriate for the care environment. The selected care-unit profile has not changed the expected alarm behavior. Password-protected minimum-volume requirements remain consistent with facility policy. Do not permanently lower or disable alarm volume to troubleshoot nuisance alarms. Expected outcome: Alarm-audio settings permit an audible alarm at an appropriate volume. If correcting a setting restores normal alarm audio, verify all alarm priorities and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check for Active Audio-Pause or Alarm-Silence Indicators
steps.instructions: Observe the display for alarm-silence, audio-pause, or similar status indicators. Allow any temporary silence period to expire, or cancel it using the approved control. Confirm that the monitor returns to normal alarm readiness. Expected outcome: No active audio-pause condition prevents the expected alarm tone. If audible alarms resume normally, document the operational condition and stop.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Loaded Profile and Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct: Patient type; Care-unit profile; Alarm configuration; Audio configuration; Site-approved default settings are loaded. Compare the affected monitor with another verified CARESCAPE Canvas configured for the same clinical area. Do not copy settings from a different department or patient population without authorization. Expected outcome: The monitor is operating with the correct approved configuration. If reloading an approved profile corrects the problem, verify that the configuration remains active after a controlled restart and stop.

steps.title: 8. Check External and Modular Connections
steps.instructions: Power down the system when required by facility and manufacturer procedures, then inspect accessible connections between the Canvas display and its associated monitoring components. Check for: Loose external cables; Partially seated connectors; Bent, damaged, contaminated, or recessed connector contacts; Strain or damage near cable ends; Incorrect or unapproved cables; Connections disturbed during transport, cleaning, or equipment relocation. Reseat only user-accessible connections. Do not open the monitor or disturb internal wiring. Expected outcome: All external system connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an external connection restores the alarm functions, perform a complete alarm test and stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After confirming that the device is not supporting a patient: Shut down the monitor through the normal software process. Allow the shutdown to complete. Disconnect external power if required by the approved procedure. Wait briefly. Restore power and restart the monitor. Observe for startup errors or delayed alarm-system initialization. Avoid repeated power cycling. Recurring loss of alarm function after startup requires escalation. Expected outcome: The monitor completes startup and initializes its audio and visual alarm systems normally. If the restart restores operation, continue testing to ensure the problem does not recur.

steps.title: 10. Test the Audible and Visual Alarm Functions
steps.instructions: Using an approved patient simulator or manufacturer-supported test method, generate controlled alarm conditions. Verify: A visible alarm message appears. The correct audible tone is produced. Sound is clear and sufficiently loud. The alarm light illuminates as expected. Different alarm priorities produce the expected indications. Audio pause and alarm acknowledgement operate correctly. Alarm annunciation returns after the pause period. The alarm is also communicated to the central station when applicable. Do not create test alarms on an active patient. Expected outcome: Audible, visual, and networked alarm indications operate consistently for each tested priority. If any alarm priority lacks the expected audible or visual indication, remove the monitor from service.

steps.title: 11. Compare with a Known-Good Configuration
steps.instructions: When available, compare the affected monitor with an equivalent CARESCAPE Canvas using: The same approved profile; The same software release; The same external connections; The same test simulator; The same alarm conditions. This helps distinguish a device-specific failure from a department-wide configuration or workflow issue. Expected outcome: The comparison identifies whether the failure follows the device or is related to the system configuration. Do not exchange internal components or perform undocumented configuration changes.

steps.title: 12. Evaluate Central Station Alarm Behavior Separately
steps.instructions: If local alarms work but the central station does not receive or announce them, troubleshoot the network and central-station communication path separately. If the central station receives alarms but the local Canvas speaker or alarm light fails, treat the issue as a local alarm-output failure. Central monitoring does not replace required local alarm functionality. Expected outcome: The local alarm system and remote alarm communication path are evaluated independently.

steps.title: 13. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before considering the monitor operational, verify: High-, medium-, and low-priority alarm indications as applicable; Audible alarm clarity and volume; Alarm-light operation; Audio-pause behavior; Visual alarm messages; Alarm acknowledgement; Central-station communication, when used; Stable operation after restart; No system error messages. Expected outcome: All applicable alarm functions pass consistently. Return the monitor to service only when every required alarm-output function operates normally.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas displayed alarm messages but produced no audible alarm tone.
CCR.Cause: Alarm settings and external connections were verified, but simulated alarm testing confirmed that the local speaker produced no sound at any alarm priority.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the monitor from service, applied an Out of Service label, and forwarded it for authorized bench evaluation of the alarm-audio system.

title: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Canvas Patient Monitor - Secondary Display or Video Output Failure
description: Troubleshooting a blank, intermittent, distorted, or missing secondary display caused by power, cabling, input selection, configuration, or external display failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended display troubleshooting while the CARESCAPE Canvas is actively supporting patient care. If the primary display is also unavailable, unreadable, or unreliable: Notify the clinical team immediately. Transfer monitoring to another verified patient monitor. Confirm that alarms, waveforms, parameter values, and patient identification are visible on the replacement device. Do not rely solely on a remote or secondary display for alarm recognition or clinical decisions. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues without depending on an unreliable display system. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the affected equipment can be safely evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Display Has Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects: Only the secondary display; Both the primary and secondary displays; The secondary display intermittently; The picture only, while the display remains powered; A particular screen, room, mounting location, or video connection. Check whether the primary CARESCAPE Canvas display is operating normally and showing live parameters. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the secondary display path or identified as a broader monitor problem. If the primary display is also blank, frozen, or restarting, stop this procedure and troubleshoot the main monitor power or startup condition instead.

steps.title: 3. Check the Secondary Display’s Power
steps.instructions: Verify that: The display power cord is fully seated. The power supply or external adapter is connected, when applicable. The display power indicator is illuminated. The power switch is in the correct position. The connected outlet is functional. Test the outlet with an approved electrical tester or connect the display to a known-good approved outlet. Expected outcome: The secondary display powers on and shows a startup logo, status message, or input notification. If restoring power resolves the issue, verify stable operation and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the External Video Cable
steps.instructions: Inspect the video cable from the CARESCAPE Canvas system to the secondary display for: Loose connections; Partially inserted connectors; Bent or damaged connector pins; Damaged locking hardware; Cuts, crushing, or sharp bends; Excessive tension at the monitor arm or wall mount; Contamination or fluid exposure. Disconnect and firmly reconnect both ends when safe. Secure any connector fasteners without overtightening them. Expected outcome: The connector remains firmly seated and the secondary image returns without interruption. If reseating the cable resolves the issue, gently move the cable near each connector to confirm the image remains stable, then stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Correct Display Input
steps.instructions: Use the secondary display’s external controls to confirm that the selected input matches the connected video cable. Look for messages such as: No Signal; Check Cable; Unsupported Signal; Input Not Found; Power Saving Mode. Do not change clinical settings on the CARESCAPE Canvas while checking the external display input. Expected outcome: The display is set to the correct input and begins showing the monitor image. If selecting the proper input resolves the issue, confirm the display does not revert after a power cycle and stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Adapters, Extenders, and Docking Connections
steps.instructions: If the installation uses a video adapter, signal extender, wall plate, docking connection, or other intermediary device: Confirm every connection is fully seated. Verify that any powered extender has power. Check for damaged status indicators or loss-of-link lights. Bypass a removable adapter or extension device when this can be done safely with an approved known-good cable. Do not substitute unapproved consumer adapters for permanently installed clinical equipment. Expected outcome: The video path is complete and the image is restored when a defective or disconnected intermediary component is corrected. If the image returns after bypassing an accessory, remove that accessory from service and stop.

steps.title: 7. Test With a Known-Good Video Cable
steps.instructions: Replace the existing external video cable with a compatible, approved known-good cable of the same connection type. Route the test cable directly when possible to eliminate wall plates, extensions, and cable-management pinch points. Expected outcome: A stable image appears on the secondary display. If the known-good cable resolves the issue, replace the defective cable, secure it properly, and stop.

steps.title: 8. Test the Secondary Display Independently
steps.instructions: Connect an approved known-good video source to the secondary display when permitted by facility procedures. Confirm whether the display can produce a stable image using the same input. Expected outcome: The test determines whether the secondary display itself is functional. If the display fails with another known-good source, remove the secondary display from service for repair or replacement. If the display works normally, continue evaluating the CARESCAPE Canvas video-output path.

steps.title: 9. Test the CARESCAPE Canvas Output With a Known-Good Display
steps.instructions: Connect the video output to a compatible known-good display using an approved cable. Do not change resolution, service settings, or system configuration unless authorized by GE HealthCare documentation and facility policy. Expected outcome: The test isolates the failure to either the original display or the monitor’s video-output path. If the known-good display works, replace or repair the original secondary display. If the known-good display also shows no image, continue to the next step.

steps.title: 10. Verify the Installed Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the secondary-display function is part of the device’s approved installed configuration and was previously operational. Review: Equipment configuration records; Installation documentation; Recent software or configuration changes; Monitor replacement history; Room renovation or cable-routing work; Whether the failure began after service, relocation, or an update. CARESCAPE Canvas is a configurable monitoring platform, so available connections and display behavior may depend on the installed hardware and system configuration. Expected outcome: The secondary display is confirmed as an approved feature and no unauthorized configuration change is identified. If the installation was recently changed, restore the last verified configuration only when authorized and documented.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After ensuring the monitor is not supporting an active patient, perform a normal controlled shutdown and restart according to facility procedures. Avoid repeated rapid power cycling. Observe whether: The primary display starts normally. The secondary display shows startup activity. The video signal appears only after the operating interface loads. Any error or configuration message appears. The image disappears again after startup. Expected outcome: A temporary communication or startup condition clears and both displays remain stable. If the secondary display returns, operate the system long enough to verify the image remains stable before returning it to service.

steps.title: 12. Complete a Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before returning the system to clinical use: Confirm the primary display remains normal. Confirm the secondary image is stable and readable. Verify displayed patient information matches the primary display. Check that waveforms and parameter values update normally. Verify there is no flickering, distortion, color loss, or intermittent blanking. Confirm cables are secured without strain. Perform any required post-service operational and electrical safety checks. The secondary display must not obscure, delay, or incorrectly represent patient-monitoring information. Expected outcome: The complete display system operates reliably and passes the facility’s return-to-service requirements.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas primary screen was operating, but the connected secondary display remained blank and showed “No Signal.”
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the video cable at the secondary display was loose and intermittently lost connection when the monitor arm was repositioned.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and secured the video cable, verified a stable image on both displays, completed functional testing, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Message shown on the secondary display
Whether the issue followed relocation or service

title: GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Canvas Patient Monitor - Patient Profile, Configuration, or Settings Will Not Load
description: Troubleshooting profiles, display configurations, patient settings, or care-area defaults that fail to load because of workflow, connection, software, or configuration issues.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot profile or configuration problems while the CARESCAPE Canvas is the only monitor supporting an active patient. If required settings, alarm limits, waveforms, or patient information cannot be confirmed: Notify the clinical team. Transfer the patient to another verified monitoring device. Verify alarm limits and monitored parameters on the replacement equipment. Do not assume the intended settings loaded successfully. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues on equipment with confirmed parameters, alarm limits, and patient identification. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the affected system is safely removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine what is not loading: Patient information or demographics; Patient category; Care-area or unit configuration; User or clinical profile; Display page or waveform layout; Parameter settings; Alarm limits or alarm configuration; Network-delivered configuration; Previously saved settings after restart. Record any message displayed and note whether the system loads incorrect defaults, remains on a loading screen, freezes, or returns to the previous configuration. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined before settings are changed. If the requested profile loads normally, verify its displayed settings and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the Correct Patient and Care Location
steps.instructions: Verify that the monitor is associated with the intended: Patient; Bed; Room; Unit or care area; Patient category. A patient or bed association mismatch may prevent the expected configuration from appearing or may cause a different default profile to load. Do not alter or overwrite patient demographic information without following the facility’s approved patient-association workflow. Expected outcome: The patient, bed, care area, and requested configuration correspond correctly. If correcting the association restores the intended profile, verify all alarm limits and parameters, document the action, and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check for an Incomplete Admission, Discharge, or Transfer Workflow
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem began after: Admitting a new patient; Discharging a previous patient; Transferring a patient between beds or units; Moving the monitor or acquisition equipment; Reconnecting a CARESCAPE ONE monitor; Changing patient category. Confirm that the previous patient session was properly completed and that the new patient was correctly admitted or selected. Expected outcome: No incomplete patient session or transfer is preventing the new configuration from loading. If completing the approved workflow resolves the issue, verify the loaded patient information and settings, then stop.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Requested Profile Is Available
steps.instructions: Review the profiles, display pages, or configuration choices available through the normal clinical interface. Confirm that: The requested profile appears in the selection list. The correct care area is active. The user has appropriate access to select the profile. The requested profile has not been renamed, replaced, or removed. The monitor is not intentionally restricted to an approved default configuration. Do not enter service-level configuration areas or modify protected institutional defaults without authorization. Expected outcome: The intended profile is present and selectable. If the profile is absent on multiple Canvas systems in the same area, escalate the issue as a configuration-management problem rather than changing individual monitors.

steps.title: 6. Check the CARESCAPE ONE Connection
steps.instructions: CARESCAPE Canvas may operate with CARESCAPE ONE as part of its monitoring platform. Confirm that the CARESCAPE ONE monitor is: Fully seated in its mount or docking connection; Powered normally; Free of startup or communication messages; Connected using undamaged approved hardware; Recognized by the Canvas display. Inspect accessible connectors for looseness, contamination, bent contacts, or physical damage. Do not probe connector contacts or perform internal disassembly. Expected outcome: The acquisition monitor and Canvas display communicate normally. If reseating an approved external connection restores the profile, verify patient information, parameters, alarm limits, and waveform layout before returning the system to service.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Network Connections
steps.instructions: If profiles, patient information, or care-area settings are delivered through the hospital network, inspect the accessible network path. Check: Ethernet cable connection; Wall jack connection; Docking or mounting-station connection; Visible link or communication indicators; Cable damage or loose connectors; Whether the network-disconnected symbol or message is present. Use a known-good approved cable or verified network port when permitted by facility policy. Do not change IP addresses, VLAN settings, hostnames, certificates, or enterprise network parameters without coordinating with the responsible network or integration team. Expected outcome: The monitor has a stable physical network connection without communication warnings. If restoring the connection allows the configuration to load, verify the complete patient profile and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Compare the Issue With Another Canvas System
steps.instructions: When available, compare the affected system with a working CARESCAPE Canvas assigned to the same care area. Determine whether: The requested profile appears on the comparison system. Both systems are assigned to the same unit. Both systems show normal network connectivity. The problem follows a particular CARESCAPE ONE monitor. The problem remains with the Canvas display or bed location. Multiple systems are affected simultaneously. Do not move equipment supporting an active patient for comparison testing. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the profile, acquisition monitor, Canvas display, network connection, bed location, or broader system. If multiple systems are affected, notify the monitoring, integration, or network support team rather than repeatedly restarting individual devices.

steps.title: 9. Attempt a Controlled Profile Reload
steps.instructions: Using only normal operator-accessible controls: Exit the current configuration screen. Return to the approved profile-selection area. Select a known valid profile. Allow sufficient time for the configuration to load. Observe for error messages, freezing, partial loading, or a return to defaults. Avoid repeatedly switching profiles or saving changes during a failed loading process. Expected outcome: A valid profile loads completely and remains stable. If the profile loads, verify alarm limits, patient category, enabled parameters, display pages, and patient identification before stopping.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is removed from patient use and that restarting will not interrupt active monitoring or networked patient data. Use the normal shutdown process. Allow the system to shut down completely before restoring power. After restart: Observe the complete startup sequence. Record any errors or unusually long loading periods. Confirm communication with connected monitoring components. Attempt to load a known valid profile. Verify that the selected settings remain stable. Do not repeatedly cycle power if the system freezes, restarts unexpectedly, or consistently fails at the same point. Expected outcome: The system completes startup and loads an approved configuration normally. If a controlled restart resolves the issue, complete a functional inspection and verify all safety-critical alarm settings before returning the monitor to service.

steps.title: 11. Check for Unsaved or Unauthorized Configuration Changes
steps.instructions: Ask whether the issue began after: A software update; Configuration deployment; Unit relocation; Network maintenance; Profile editing; Monitor replacement; CARESCAPE ONE replacement; Integration or central-station work. Determine whether the requested settings were formally saved and distributed through the facility’s approved configuration process. Do not attempt to rebuild institutional profiles from memory or copy settings without authorization. Incorrect profiles may create inappropriate alarm limits, patient categories, or parameter behavior. Expected outcome: Configuration history identifies whether the issue followed an authorized system change. If the issue began after a deployment or update, preserve the displayed error information and escalate to the system administrator or GE HealthCare support.

steps.title: 12. Verify Operation Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: After the profile loads successfully, confirm: Correct patient category; Correct patient and bed association; Expected waveform layout; Required parameters are available; Alarm limits are appropriate; Alarm volume and visual indicators function; Settings remain after navigating between screens; Network communication remains stable; No configuration or communication messages return. Perform testing according to facility policy using approved simulators or test equipment when applicable. Expected outcome: The intended configuration loads completely, remains stable, and supports safe clinical monitoring. Do not return the system to service if settings are incomplete, incorrect, unstable, or cannot be independently verified.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the CARESCAPE Canvas would not load the adult ICU patient profile and returned to the default display configuration.
CCR.Cause: The CARESCAPE ONE connection was not fully seated, preventing the Canvas system from completing communication and loading the assigned profile.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the system from patient use, reseated the external CARESCAPE ONE connection, restarted the system, loaded the approved ICU profile, and verified patient category, parameters, alarm limits, waveforms, and network communication.

helpfulDetails: Patient, bed, and care-area association verified
Admission, discharge, or transfer status checked
Network cable and wall connection checked
Known-good cable or network port tested
Time and frequency of failure documented
Recent update or configuration deployment identified
Alarm limits and alarm operation verified
Accessories swapped or external connections reseated
Power behavior during startup and restart
Environmental factors or recent equipment relocation
Indicator lights and communication symbols observed

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5500 HD Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - 12SL Analysis Or Interpretation Not Generated
description: Troubleshooting missing 12SL analysis or interpretation caused by lead quality, patient data, acquisition mode, settings, licensing, or software problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Clinical Decision-Making
steps.instructions: Do not delay clinical evaluation of a symptomatic patient while troubleshooting automated ECG interpretation. Provide the ECG waveform to a qualified clinician for direct review. Repeat the ECG on another verified device when clinically necessary. Treat automated interpretation as decision support, not a replacement for clinician assessment. Do not assume a normal tracing because no interpretation printed. Expected outcome: Clinical care continues without depending on unavailable automated analysis.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Analysis Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: No interpretation appears on the screen or printout. Measurements appear but interpretive statements do not. Analysis fails only for certain patients. The ECG is marked as poor quality. The issue began after a configuration or software change. The waveform itself is complete and readable. Expected outcome: The problem is identified as missing measurements, missing statements, poor-quality rejection, or configuration-related behavior.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Electrode Placement and Skin Preparation
steps.instructions: Confirm that clinical staff used the approved 12-lead placement. Check for: Incorrect limb or precordial lead placement Loose electrodes Dried or expired electrodes Hair, lotion, moisture, or poor skin contact Excessive cable tension Lead-wire reversal Clinical staff should correct patient preparation and electrode placement. Expected outcome: All electrodes make stable contact and the displayed lead configuration is clinically appropriate.

steps.title: 4. Evaluate Signal Quality
steps.instructions: Observe the ECG waveform for: Baseline wander Muscle artifact Electrical interference Flat or missing leads Excessive noise Lead-off indications Pacemaker spikes or rhythm conditions that may affect analysis Reacquire the ECG only after improving signal quality. Expected outcome: A complete, stable, low-artifact 12-lead tracing is available for analysis.

steps.title: 5. Verify Patient Demographic Entry
steps.instructions: Confirm required patient information is entered accurately. Review: Patient age or date of birth Sex or other required demographic fields Patient ID Acquisition type or patient category Do not enter fabricated demographic values to force an interpretation. Expected outcome: Required patient information is present and accurately associated with the ECG.

steps.title: 6. Confirm the Correct Acquisition Mode
steps.instructions: Verify the ECG was acquired using the intended resting 12-lead workflow. Confirm all required leads are present. Ensure the device is not in a rhythm-only, preview, or other workflow that may not produce the expected analysis. Confirm the ECG acquisition completed rather than being stopped early. Expected outcome: A completed diagnostic 12-lead ECG is available for analysis.

steps.title: 7. Review Normal User-Accessible Print and Analysis Options
steps.instructions: Check whether the selected report format is configured to display measurements or interpretation. Confirm the interpretation is not merely omitted from the chosen print format. Review the on-screen record as well as the printed copy. Do not change licensed features or restricted analysis configuration. Expected outcome: Existing analysis is found in the record or the correct report format displays it.

steps.title: 8. Test With an ECG Simulator
steps.instructions: Disconnect the patient and connect an approved ECG simulator. Use a stable standard simulated rhythm. Acquire a complete 12-lead ECG. Observe whether measurements and interpretation are generated. Do not use simulator results to judge clinical accuracy beyond functional operation. Expected outcome: The device generates expected analysis output from a stable simulated signal. If successful, the original issue was likely signal, lead placement, or patient-workflow related.

steps.title: 9. Compare With Another MAC 5500 HD
steps.instructions: When available: Use the same approved simulator and equivalent acquisition workflow. Compare whether another unit generates analysis. Confirm the affected unit has the expected analysis capability and approved configuration. Expected outcome: A device-specific failure or broader configuration expectation is identified.

steps.title: 10. Restart and Retest
steps.instructions: When no patient record is active: Shut down the device normally. Restart it. Repeat the simulator acquisition. Verify the analysis appears consistently. Expected outcome: The analysis function returns after restart and remains stable.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction: Acquire a clean simulator ECG. Confirm all 12 leads display. Confirm measurements and applicable interpretive output are generated. Verify the information appears in the saved record and intended report. Confirm printing and transmission do not remove or alter the expected analysis section. Expected outcome: The device consistently generates and preserves the expected 12SL analysis output. The unit may be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the MAC 5500 HD printed the ECG waveform but did not generate 12SL interpretation text.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found significant artifact and one intermittently disconnected precordial lead during acquisition.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the lead connection, repeated testing with an ECG simulator, and verified complete 12-lead acquisition with measurements and interpretation.

helpfulDetails: Whether measurements or statements were missing

title: GE Healthcare MAC 5500 HD Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Acquisition Module Or Patient Cable Not Recognized
description: Troubleshooting an unrecognized acquisition module or patient cable caused by loose connections, damage, contamination, incompatibility, or an external accessory failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety and Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not rely on the MAC 5500 HD for diagnostic ECG acquisition when the acquisition module or patient cable is not consistently recognized. Stop the current acquisition attempt. Notify clinical staff that the ECG system is not ready for use. Use another verified electrocardiograph when the ECG is clinically urgent. Do not repeatedly connect or disconnect patient-applied cables while the patient remains connected. Expected outcome: The patient is disconnected safely from unreliable equipment and ECG testing continues on another verified device when required.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The acquisition module is not detected at startup. The module disconnects intermittently. Lead waveforms are absent despite the module being displayed. The problem began after a cable, module, or accessory change. The issue occurs with every patient or only one setup. Record any displayed message without assuming that it identifies a failed internal component. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined as a recognition, intermittent connection, or signal-path problem.

steps.title: 3. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: Disconnect the patient and power the electrocardiograph down normally. Disconnect the acquisition module or patient cable. Wait briefly for the unit to shut down completely. Reconnect the accessory firmly. Restart the device and observe whether the accessory is recognized. Do not force connectors or use damaged connector hardware. Expected outcome: The module or patient cable is detected normally after restart. If recognition remains stable, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the External Connectors
steps.instructions: Inspect the device connection, acquisition module connector, cable strain reliefs, and connector pins or contacts. Look for: Bent, recessed, loose, or contaminated contacts Cracked connector shells Damaged locking features Fluid residue Cable cuts, crushing, or severe twisting Loose strain reliefs Remove the accessory from use if electrical conductors, contacts, or insulation appear damaged. Expected outcome: Connectors are clean, dry, undamaged, and seat securely. Any visibly defective cable or module is removed from service.

steps.title: 5. Verify Correct Connection and Seating
steps.instructions: Reconnect the acquisition module or patient cable using the correct orientation. Confirm the connector is fully inserted. Verify any latch or locking feature engages. Ensure the cable is not partially pulled out by its own weight. Position the cable so it is not under tension. Expected outcome: The connection remains secure when the cable is gently repositioned. If recognition returns and remains stable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check for Cable Movement or Intermittency
steps.instructions: With no patient connected, observe the device while gently moving the cable near each strain relief and connector. Do not sharply bend or twist the cable. Watch for: Recognition appearing and disappearing Waveform channels dropping out Status changes when the cable is moved Unexpected restart or interface response Expected outcome: Recognition remains stable during gentle movement. A repeatable dropout indicates the affected accessory should be replaced or sent for evaluation.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Accessory
steps.instructions: When available, connect a verified compatible acquisition module or patient cable. Use only accessories approved for the device configuration. Change one component at a time. Repeat startup and basic lead-signal verification. Expected outcome: If the known-good accessory is recognized, the original accessory is the likely cause and should be removed from service. Troubleshooting can stop after documentation and final testing.

steps.title: 8. Test the Suspect Accessory on Another Compatible Unit
steps.instructions: When safe and available, connect the suspect accessory to another verified compatible MAC system. Do not transfer an accessory that is contaminated, physically damaged, or electrically unsafe. Expected outcome: If the problem follows the accessory, remove that accessory from service. If the suspect accessory works normally elsewhere, the original electrocardiograph requires bench evaluation.
